passages.text: Did you see the looks on their faces? Were they mad?

passages.title: The Shoe Is On The Other Foot
passages.text:
I see you and Ningna have been up to some mischief. Unfortunately, this type of behavior is not condoned by the Order--

Wait, where did you find those shoes? I've been looking for that pair of moleskin riding boots for ages!

Well... I suppose I will let this slide... this time. Hmph.

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text:
<Your serpent catches your gaze and ducks its head bashfully.>

You can tell that someone has gotten out of its pen and had "an accident."

Well, at the rate that the hatchling's been eating, it had to come out the other end... somewhere.

You had better find the serpent's poop and clean it up before the Serpent Masters find out.

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text: <The hatchling watches you innocently.>

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text: The hatchling plays contentedly, oblivious to your efforts. Sigh... sometimes, the life of a serpent trainer is quite thankless.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text:
As you near, your serpent opens its mouth and begins drooling. It looks quite hungry since you last left it.

From the way it whimpers and slaps its tail, you can tell it is not looking for just any treat, but a special favorite snack.

Your serpent loves to munch on tiny spider eyes, but this delicacy comes only from the Widowspawn spiders in the cave along the coast to the north.

Well, what's a rider to do? Your serpent is waiting.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text: Your serpent perks up at your return.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text: Your serpent nudges your hand affectionately, then proceeds to devour the treats!

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text:
Those Oona hozen have gone too far this time.

Do you know what they are doing with wild cloud serpents? Captured hatchlings are forced to fight one another in the pits, for nothing more than the Oona's amusement.

Savages!

If the young hatchlings learn such aggressive behavior at a young age, they may become violent and corrupted adults. A malicious cloud serpent is not something we want to deal with.

We must save the hatchlings.

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text:
The Order of the Cloud Serpent has worked for centuries to make the cloud serpents into loyal companions. Our kindness brings out the best in these creatures.

Unfortunately, violence and anger can quickly turn them into destructive monsters.

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text: Ah yes, these hatchlings look quite tired. They have been through a great ordeal, but thanks to you, they are safe now.

passages.title: Regeneration Takes Time
passages.text:
Vol'jin would be dead if he were any race other than a troll. His regeneration is impressive, but it is being blocked by a poison.

We need to cleanse this poison so that he can regenerate the damage.

Take to the skies and travel southeast. Across the mountain tops of the Secret Aerie you will find needle sprites. Bring me some of the hardest needles from them you can find.

With them I can attempt an acupuncture technique that should purge the poison from his body and accelerate his regeneration.

passages.title: Regeneration Takes Time
passages.text: My herbs are the only thing keeping Vol'jin from death. I dare not leave his side.

passages.title: Regeneration Takes Time
passages.text: Very good. These should work nicely.

passages.title: The Handle
passages.text:
There once was a Chief named Ingoo Ingoo,

Who beat me in a drink drink boogaloo.

He took the mallet's handle for winning,

Not knowing you can't beat the King in drinking.

Monkey King had to hide the mallet from the bell,

But Ingoo's children do not use the handle well.

Over the years they have used the handle to do harm,

Now we must find the current chief so we can disarm.

Go south to Unga Ingoo, Monkey King meet you there.

Only wikkets show to a party with hands bare.

passages.title: The Handle
passages.text: Ingoo was a great hozen. Good leader, nice parties, and good booze.

passages.title: The Handle
passages.text: Artifacts not make people great. Artifacts allow people to be more of themselves. Good becomes gooder. Bad becomes badder. And Chief Ingoo Ingoo became worser.

passages.title: The Head
passages.text:
Monkey King receive word on where to find the head,

The hozen who got it has long since been dead. 

Kunzen chiefs pass the relic from father to son, 

But then virmen Skiggit came and the head it won. 

Now the wikket worships it in a hollow. 

Since it was too ookin' big for him to swallow. 

I sent a royal finder north to find him and stand. 

Look for finder in mountains west of the Heartland.

passages.title: The Head
passages.text: You got head?

passages.title: The Head
passages.text:
What virmen do not understand, they worship, fight or flee.

I should send them a few statues of me.

passages.title: The Harmonic Ointment
passages.text:
Legends are not born, they are made.

Much like your next target, a mogu named "The Blade." 

In his bags you will find,

An ointment whose sound plays with the mind.

Bring this nibby ointment to the Monkey King!

And with it, he shall make the mallet sing!

Travel north along the wall, and when you reach the end, turn left.

passages.title: The Harmonic Ointment
passages.text:
How the mogu found the ointment is a wonder.

But a lot has happened since the world tore assunder.

passages.title: The Harmonic Ointment
passages.text: Woot woot!

passages.title: The Call of War
passages.text:
If you are reading this letter, it likely means that I am dead. Please deliver this to my son, Faran, at Teluuna Observatory.

Dearest Faran and Elsa,

I have fallen in the line of duty while defending the Temple of Karabor.

Please know that I love you both with all of my heart. My spirit will watch over you for the rest of your days. Be strong, love one another, and live this life to the best of your ability.

I am so proud of you both.

Love,

Your Mother

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text:
Pieces of a Thunderlord chain lay on the ground. It is of a very simple design, but effective.

With enough parts, even the most unskilled person could assemble a chain and grapple as effective as those used by the Thunderlord Grapplers.

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text: This shoddy, beaten anvil is used mostly for crafting chains and what little other metal working the Thunderlord require.

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text: With a quick tap of a hammer and a snip of the rings, the Thunderlord Grapple is as good as new.

passages.title: The Inkmasters of the Arboretum
passages.text: I have heard that the Inkmasters at the Arboretum are in need of aid from a scribe of great skill. You should speak with Inkmaster Wei, if you wish to help.

passages.title: Demons Among Us - Horde
passages.text:
If you are reading this, it means I have fallen in battle. As my last request, please deliver this letter to Thalia at Teluuna Observatory.

Dearest Thalia,

You have always been my best friend, ever since we were children growing up in Tuurem.

I have always been too afraid to tell you my feelings, but I cannot leave this world without finally speaking the truth.

Thalia, I love you with all my heart.

I shall wait for you in the next world. I will for eternity for you.

Love,

Thamuun

passages.title: Just the Beginning
passages.text:
I forgive Orgrim. He acted as well all must - we do what our hearts tell us is right.

We should return to your outpost and discuss our next course of action. There is nothing left for us here.

I will ask the human to open a portal for us. We shall speak again there.

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text:
Looks like we'll soon have another obstacle in our way: that ridiculously large tank that they have pointed at the Dark Portal. The Iron Worldbreaker, I think they call it.

If I had some documentation on how it might work, then I might be able to figure out how to shut it down. Maybe some o' those machinists and laborers have some documentation on how it works?

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text:
Mmm... yes... simple enough.

<The dwarf flips through the pages and no longer seems to notice your presence.>

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text:
Ey, <pal/lady>! We got an issue, here.

Me ol' pal Thaelin's rigged together this here plunger out of spare Blackrock parts - engineerin' whiz that he is - but we're gonna need some gunpowder if we really want ta' do any damage.

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text: Don't go doin' anything inappropriate with that gunpowder, now.

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text: Woo hoo hoo haaaaa!

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text:
Ameeka created this book to document and pass down our most cherished crafting techniques to our children. She must have dropped it while traveling. She will be relieved to see her book.

From what I have heard from other villagers, she was last seen on the road to Elodor. Perhaps you can find her there.

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text: Hello, traveler! Is there something that I can help you with?

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text: Is that my tailoring tome? It is! I'm so glad it is safe! How can I ever repay you?

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text: Now that the engineering works is complete, we can start producing gearspring parts for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: From Within
passages.text:
A few of our demon hunters, Kor'vas Bloodthorn and Cyana Nightglaive, took a small force of the Illidari across to Faronaar. Their mission was to weaken the Legion from within.

I haven't heard from them in a while.

It would be best if you could find and lead them to success. Agreed?

passages.title: From Within
passages.text:
A friend it would seem.

Kayn did not think we could handle this? He might have been right this time.

passages.title: [UNUSED]Blood of the Annihilan
passages.text:
We must make contact with Lord Illidan's spirit. But to do that, we need something powerful enough to fuel the nether crucible. I know just the thing.

A pit lord named Malinoth has taken over a nearby cave. If we acquire his blood, you can use it to power the crucible. Then, you can make contact with Illidan in the Twisting Nether.

passages.title: Craig's Test Quest Again!
passages.text: An honorable person gives me cloth

passages.title: Our Very Bones
passages.text:
You seek the Tidestone of Golganneth?

Yes, I know where it lies. It is in a place to which I prefer not to return.

You may be of use to me. In the midst of this naga attack, those horrid fish-men flopped their way onto my lands and raided our graveyards. They steal the bones of our ancestors, and indeed, the very bones of my people.

Help me bring some solace to my people. Then I shall tell you more about the Tidestone.

passages.title: Our Very Bones
passages.text: My people may not care much for me, but that will not stop me from caring for them.

passages.title: Our Very Bones
passages.text:
Our bones are all we have left of an existence we left behind a long time ago.

<The prince stares intently into your eyes.>

Stay with me, <class>. I will help you find your Tidestone.

passages.title: The Blood of Demons
passages.text:
The time has come to make contact with the Master's soul. It is somewhere in the endless expanse of the Twisting Nether. Luckily, so is Mardum.

Such a thing is not unheard of, but it will be exceedingly difficult, even here. In addition to what the matron mother had us gather, we need a great deal of demon blood.

Like, a lot of it!

passages.title: The Blood of Demons
passages.text: Once we have enough demon blood, you can begin the ritual.

passages.title: The Blood of Demons
passages.text: If this is not enough demon blood, no amount will be. Now, let us see if we can make contact with Illidan's spirit in the Twisting Nether.

passages.title: A Simple Plan
passages.text:
Like many dreadlords, Detheroc cannot help but gloat. He was careless and I overheard many of his plans while I was held captive.

With your leave, I would like to underscore the gravity of the situation in Stormwind. The fate of Azeroth hangs in the balance.

But for all of that, I have a simple plan: get 'em.

passages.title: A Simple Plan
passages.text: We need to listen to Shaw's plan and then come to a consensus on the way forward.

passages.title: A Simple Plan
passages.text: Then, it's decided. We either expose Detheroc or it's war between the Alliance and Horde, and we lose the world to the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Dark Revelations
passages.text:
I'm not going to let Cordana Felsong get away with this. There is no way in hell I am going to let that warden witch turn my people.

As for Nightglaive... I will NOT suffer a traitor to live!

Are you with me, <name>?

passages.title: Dark Revelations
passages.text: The traitor must be killed. It is the only way.

passages.title: Dark Revelations
passages.text:
Grim news indeed. We cannot afford the loss of even one demon hunter, but you and Kor'vas were right to put an end to Nightglaive.

More importantly, you have made a good friend in Stellagosa. The remnant of the Blue Dragonflight could prove to be a powerful ally.

passages.title: Saving Stellagosa
passages.text:
During the fighting, of all things, I saw a blue drake swoop in and attack the demons. I couldn't believe my eyes. I'd heard that the Blue Dragonflight had gone extinct.

The Legion managed to bring the drake down, but not until after she'd killed a score of them. She was magnificent. Last I saw, they were dragging her in the direction of the southern camp.

We should see if she's still alive. A dragon could prove a powerful ally.

passages.title: Saving Stellagosa
passages.text: If there's a remnant of the Blue Dragonflight nearby, we should do whatever we can to ally ourselves with them.

passages.title: Saving Stellagosa
passages.text:
Beautiful creatures... pure, one with the world. I didn't think that I could hate the Legion more.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Walk of Shame
passages.text:
The echoes of Nar'thalas still haunt me, and I cannot bear the pain of this accursed town any longer. I may still be able to get you closer to the Tidestone, however.

<Farondis' eyes narrow in newfound determination.>

We will need to skirt around the edge of town. Follow me.

passages.title: The Walk of Shame
passages.text:
<The prince appears emotionally drained.>

This is the end of the road for me, <name>. I can't bear to look at them. Moreover, my mere presence puts you in danger.

Beyond this point, you must walk alone.

passages.title: Into the Academy
passages.text:
The sunken structure on the other side of this bridge was once called Nar'thalas Academy: the center of magical studies in all of Azeroth. You should have seen her in her full splendor.

The Tidestone should be locked up within. I dare not enter, but you - my champion - you go with my blessing.

passages.title: Into the Academy
passages.text: New student?

passages.title: The Tidestone: Shattered
passages.text:
I suppose you can go in, then.

The shattered pieces of the Tidestone of Golganneth are contained within the academy's eastern wing. Even as curator, I cannot attest to their condition, as I have not been in to inspect them in many millennia.

Oh, young <name>? Please do not touch anything.

passages.title: The Tidestone: Shattered
passages.text: <The last remaining piece of the Tidestone lies before you.>

passages.title: The Tidestone: Shattered
passages.text: <You notice the reflection of something sinister upon the core's surface...>

passages.title: The Head of the Snake
passages.text:
Those naga have the Tidestone shards, <name>. They will soon be dragging them into their watery holes, away from our reach.

It would be wise to take out their leaders before that happens.

passages.title: The Head of the Snake
passages.text: I... I can't believe it...

passages.title: The Head of the Snake
passages.text:
You killed Athissa, <name>.

That is to say, you and... and my people...

My people... they fought for us...

But, Warlord Parjesh has escaped through the portal with the Tidestone. You must pursue him and retrieve the Pillar of Creation.

passages.title: Nar'thalas Still Suffers
passages.text:
They have not forgiven me. I cannot blame them.

Past crimes aside, I am still their prince. Even in death, I will do what I can to protect my people.

<name>. Act as my champion. Find and defeat the creature that leads this naga attack against the people of Nar'thalas. After all these years, you - |5<race> <class>, of all things - may be the instrument of my redemption.

passages.title: Nar'thalas Still Suffers
passages.text: I will make it up to them. WE will make it up to them.

passages.title: Nar'thalas Still Suffers
passages.text:
She spoke of the Tidestone? That sea witch must not realize how close she truly is to finding it.

We should move quickly. We are close to your prize, and the naga are circling in.

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text:
I'm concerned for Elder Aldryth. He went out for a walk about ten thousand years ago, and he has not returned.

With these naga attacking, I fear he may be in danger!

If you dare venture out into the fray, do look out for our court elder.

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text: Have you seen him?

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text:
I can't tell you how relieved I am that Elder Aldryth has returned.

Honestly, life here in the palace hasn't been the same without him. Everything seemed to have... lost its color. Perhaps now we can get back to our normal lives.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shipwreck Arena
passages.text:
The giants at Shipwreck Arena are very fond of smashing ships that sail too close to shore. They take the sailors prisoner and use them for their own amusement.

I suppose it will be easy for you to infiltrate the place. It's breaking out that will be the difficult part.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shipwreck Arena
passages.text: Did you get my bottle? Are you here to help us escape?

passages.title: Trailing the Tidestone
passages.text:
Your quest for the Tidestone... it intrigues me. More than that, it suits my needs quite well. I have been in need of a champion for a very, very long time.

It is decided, then. I shall join you.

We will have to head east, through Nar'thalas.

Shall we depart?

passages.title: Trailing the Tidestone
passages.text: Perhaps this was a mistake.

passages.title: Boss Whalebelly's in Charge
passages.text:
Great, let's get started! If we're going to break everyone out of here, you need to pose as a pit fighter like the rest of us. They won't just let you run around anywhere you want in here.

First thing you need to do is present yourself to Boss Whalebelly. The giants may run this place, but as far as posing as one of us, Whalebelly's in charge.

He's speaking with his goons just to the south.

passages.title: Boss Whalebelly's in Charge
passages.text: Go on. Go talk to him.

passages.title: Boss Whalebelly's in Charge
passages.text:
That could have gone better. Sounds like you've already made an enemy.

Still, that'll work to our advantage. You versus Boss Whalebelly. The fight of the century... or at least, the day.

Now to set everything up.

passages.title: Sternfathom's Champion
passages.text:
Since you defeated Ooker Dooker, there's a pit fighter spot open on Sternfathom's team. You should go establish yourself as his champion. That way, the giants won't think twice about why a stranger is suddenly coming and going as <he/she> pleases.

Meanwhile, I'll start to sow some chaos so that we can strike at Prince Oceanus.

passages.title: Sternfathom's Champion
passages.text:
Hello, what can I do for you, little <race>?

Ahahaha... it's you!  I like how you came in and immediately confronted Whalebelly. That little tuskarr's got it coming.

I can tell you're going to win big for me in the arena.

passages.title: The Haunted Halls
passages.text:
Now, what was it you wanted? You're here to see the Tidestone of Golganneth? Hah! Ho ho ha ha haa!

Hooo my.

No, only the academy's headmistress has the keys to that chamber, and she hasn't opened the door in... oh, I'd say about ten thousand years.

You'd best be off to class, now. Go on, then! Into the west wing with you!

passages.title: The Haunted Halls
passages.text: Yes, the headmistress is in her study, but I can't have you bothering her right now. Classes are about to start.

passages.title: Let Sleeping Giants Lie
passages.text:
We're going to need a diversion to get close to Prince Oceanus. Are you thinking what I'm thinking?

See Sleepy Dhow over there? He's guarding all of the weapons the giants take from our shipwrecks. We can use those weapons to arm the rest of the pit fighters that are held in the caves.

All you have to do is get past that giant without waking him.

passages.title: Let Sleeping Giants Lie
passages.text: As soon as I can, I'll arm the gladiators in Oceanus Cove.

passages.title: Let Sleeping Giants Lie
passages.text: I couldn't have snuck past him better. Now, to get these weapons into the right hands.

passages.title: Save Yourself
passages.text:
Of course I couldn't sit back and let them just cart you away.

I will explain everything.

passages.title: Save Yourself
passages.text: Let me show you what happened.

passages.title: Save Yourself
passages.text: What happened, Farondis?

passages.title: [UNUSED]Rolling With the Tidestone
passages.text:
Before I forget, <name>: the Tidestone shards. They are yours to protect now.

Bring them back to your dragon. The people of Azsuna stand behind you.

passages.title: Morale Booster
passages.text:
Things may look good from where you're standing, but, we're losing. However, do not fret, my little <race> friend. You can help.

Listen closely. Ooka Dooker, Ooker's sister, is back over yonder in the champions' cave making her world famous Fighter Chow. It'll do the trick and boost our team's morale.

All you have to do is to convince her to hand it over.

passages.title: Morale Booster
passages.text:
Yes, this'll do nicely... oh no! The last of my pit fighters have been defeated.

It's just you and me now, little <race>.

passages.title: No Time for Tryouts
passages.text:
We don't have time for you to go through a lengthy set of tryouts. But, fighting in the arena is our best chance at getting you in good with the giants.

That kind-hearted giant over there that's losing against Bilgerudder is Sternfathom. If you were to defeat his hozen champion, you'd make yourself a spot on his team.

Looks like Ooker Dooker's taking a rest between bouts. Now's the time to deliver a good ol' monkey beatdown.

passages.title: No Time for Tryouts
passages.text:
By giving that hozen a good beating, you'll be making a spot for yourself in the arena.

You don't have to kill him, though.

passages.title: No Time for Tryouts
passages.text:
You made quick work of that monkey. Now there's an empty position on Sternfathom's team that you can fill.

But first, let's get me set up for what comes after your big match.

passages.title: The Right Weapon for the Job
passages.text:
<You and Okuna were going to arm the captives in here. The idea was to free them and cause as much chaos as possible. It's the only sure way to be able to get close to the prince.

You still have the weapons. You're just going to have to be careful sneaking around the giants.>

passages.title: The Right Weapon for the Job
passages.text:
Now the captives are free. Thank you, <name>.

Ready for the prince?

passages.title: The Prince is Going Down
passages.text:
<name>! I knew you'd come.

Quick, let me out of here and we'll take this giant down.

passages.title: The Prince is Going Down
passages.text:
With Oceanus dead, the skrogs will start fighting amongst themselves. They'll certainly be too busy to provide any further assistance to the naga.

I'd say this was a job well done, despite my being captured. Good thing you came along.

I'll see you around, <name>.

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Now that the alchemy lab is complete, we can start producing alchemical catalysts for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text: Now that the tannery is complete, we can start producing burnished leather for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: Demon Souls
passages.text:
I need to extract information about the Burning Legion from these foul creatures. But living, the demons are almost impossible to break.

However, like you, I wield a powerful artifact -- the Scythe of Souls.

Take one of my soul gems. If you place it next to a demon's corpse, it will rip the 'soul' out. Then, we will see if the scythe can get them to talk.

passages.title: Demon Souls
passages.text: We need those demon souls, <name>.

passages.title: Demon Souls
passages.text: Yes. Already, I can tell their souls are weaker than their flesh.

passages.title: Fel Machinations
passages.text:
My force wiped out the demons' forward base here. But, an imp mother and her brood took the rest of my demon hunters hostage, including Cyana Nightglaive.

We need to free the Illidari and destroy the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Fel Machinations
passages.text: If we're to defeat the Legion, we need to know exactly what they're up to.

passages.title: Fel Machinations
passages.text:
I've always had my doubts about Cyana. Something was never quite right there. Looks like she cracked and joined the Legion.

Still, we are not going to let her, or this Cordana Felsong, get away with it.

passages.title: Reignite the Wards
passages.text:
The demons are weakening my defenses. They must be far more powerful than what we've faced before.

Will you help me to reignite the wards to keep the Legion from overrunning our position here?

passages.title: Reignite the Wards
passages.text: All of the wards need to be reignited if we're to hold the front.

passages.title: Reignite the Wards
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. That will give us the breathing room we need to launch our counter-offensive.

passages.title: The Captain's Foot Locker
passages.text:
I don't care what you do, mate. But, if you get caught, you didn't see me.

I wasn't here.

passages.title: The Captain's Foot Locker
passages.text: <Amongst the moldering remains of the chest, you find the captain's log. Its pages are partially intact and it contains interesting information about the possible whereabouts of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, the new warchief of the Horde.>

passages.title: Hit the Books
passages.text:
<The librarian speaks in shushed tones.>

One problem with maintaining such a large arcane library is that the books often pick up an errant enchantment and start darting about on their own. These overmagicked books need to be destroyed before they cause any further damage.

If you encounter any of these exasperating essays, please put them down. Quietly.

passages.title: Hit the Books
passages.text: <The librarian sighs quietly.>

passages.title: Hit the Books
passages.text:
Don't worry about the scattered pages and spines - I will have my aides clean up.

Thank you. You may return to your studies.

passages.title: Those Who Remember
passages.text:
The ghostly elves, to the south, once had the Pillar of Creation known as the Tidestone of Golganneth.

Their great city of Nar'thalas was destroyed an eon ago. The city's ruler, Prince Farondis, fell with the city. You small ones die so easily.

If anyone knows where the fragments rest, it will be the ghost of the prince. Seek out his people.

passages.title: Those Who Remember
passages.text:
Who goes there?

Are you an emissary from that bizarre floating city?

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]The Ancient One
passages.text:
This place is now the home of what is left of the Blue Dragonflight. Its eldest dragon, Senegos, lies ahead within a pool of ley energy. If any are wise enough to help us find the Pillar of Creation that we seek on Azsuna, it will be him.

Stellagosa went ahead to join her grandfather. She assured me that we are welcome to enter the repose.

Come, <name>, we must hurry. Even from here, I can sense his life force waning. Let us approach him together.

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text:
As you must know, I'm a connoisseur of drinks... specifically, arcane-infused spirits. Cocktail mixing is alchemy, and as everyone knows, alchemy is magic.

My latest drink must be more exotic than anything I've conjured before. I already have most of what I need. But there are a couple of items left on the list.

Notice the herons down in the lagoon? As with many of the creatures on Azsuna, the magic coursing through the island permeates them.

Their eggs will do nicely.

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text: Are we speaking again because you have my eggs?

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text:
Capital! A prodigious start.

I implore you to create this marvelous mixture for yourself. I want to share the delight of alchemical spirits with the world!

You'll need to get more eggs for yourself, though.

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text:
The eggs will provide the 'oomph' to my drink's character. But there's another element, and this must not be underestimated!

Presentation.

Now, you could go with your standard olive skewered on a toothpick. Maybe a carrot stalk stuck slapdash out of a glass.

But then, you wouldn't be me.

No, my friend. What MY drink needs to sell it visually comes from a one-of-a-kind creature. I'm only going to serve it once and so my drink deserves something unique.

The eyes of Gangamesh are what I need.

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text: Yes? You have the eyes?

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text:
I was going to present this to one of the ladies of the court. Doing so might increase my standing in certain social circles.

But, I just can't bring myself to do it. Who better to drink my latest masterpiece than, well... me?

passages.title: Pop Quiz: Advanced Rune Drawing
passages.text:
Still aching to get into the headmistress' study, eh? I suppose I can let you in... as long as you prove that you've been studying.

Proper rune formation is essential when it comes to spellcasting. If you can draw a rune, you can cast a spell.

I will provide outlines for you. You can simply use your feet to trace the runes.

passages.title: Pop Quiz: Advanced Rune Drawing
passages.text: Go on, then! Get those feet moving!

passages.title: Pop Quiz: Advanced Rune Drawing
passages.text: Exemplary work, young <name>. With runes like these, you'll be graduating in no time.

passages.title: Prince Farondis
passages.text:
I'm glad to see that my doubts in you were unfounded.

You seek Prince Farondis? Follow me. I will show you to the prince's hall.

passages.title: Prince Farondis
passages.text: That's him, behind me.

passages.title: Dressing With Class
passages.text:
Now stop right there. Look at you! You look like you just walked in off of the street. Where are your robes and hat?

And don't tell me you've entered the academy without your wand and spellbook.

Freshmen.

Put yourself together, and maybe then I will consider letting you enter the academy.

passages.title: Dressing With Class
passages.text: Still trying to get into the academy, I see.

passages.title: Dressing With Class
passages.text: Your hat and robes don't match, but you still look better. I hardly recognize you.

passages.title: Mana Bark
passages.text:
We need bark from the trees if we are going to fix the wood.

Being a mortal, you can walk right in and pick up the mana bark without any trouble, as long as you don't get eaten by something.

Can you get us some mana bark?

passages.title: Essence of the Unbound
passages.text:
I need your help, mortal.

Something has warded the Mana Wood against our kind

That same something is changing the song of the wood. We can hear it.

Enter the wood and gather essence from some of the local wildlife and maybe we can track this thing down.

I will project an image of myself in the wood for when you are done.

passages.title: Rift Rippers
passages.text:
Something is opening rifts to the twisting nether using the ley line energy.

That is never a good thing.

Our kind may not be able to enter the forest, but you can.

Take this gem and look for these unbound rifts. The gem will let you seal these breaches.

I will project an image of myself into the forest when you are done.

passages.title: The Last of the Last
passages.text:
We need help.

Since the fall of Deathwing, we dragons have lost nearly all of our power. To make matters worse, we can no longer bear eggs.

My whelplings are the last of the last.

I need you, champion. Help defend my whelplands, and I swear to you, the blues will be at your side when you need them.

passages.title: The Last of the Last
passages.text:
Don't you worry, small one. I am still back in Azurewing Repose, resting in my pool.

It doesn't take much energy to throw a projection of myself here and there. I may be old and dying, but I AM still a blue dragon.

passages.title: The Withered
passages.text:
The withered are the worst kind of pest. They capture our whelplings, knock them unconscious, and then drink whatever mana they can from the helpless babes.

Normally our drakes and keepers would fend them off. Today, it looks like we may need your help.

passages.title: The Withered
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Withered
passages.text:
Twelve withered slain? Very good.

That should be enough to keep them away for a few months.

passages.title: Runas Knows the Way
passages.text:
I wish to make it up to you for whatever I did that made you want to kill me.

Hmm... your dragon complains about being weak. I know why. Runas can fix it, my friend.

One of my kind, Ael'Yith, pulls ley energy from the very ground of Azsuna. I can take you to the location of his mana siphons.

It's not too late to undo the harm the others have done. You've done well to trust me.

passages.title: Runas Knows the Way
passages.text: I still don't trust him.

passages.title: Runas Knows the Way
passages.text: They're tapping into the ley lines?

passages.title: Stellagosa
passages.text:
Something is wrong, <name>.

I sent Stellagosa to assist you, but I can no longer sense her.

Please, go out there and find out what's happened to my granddaughter.

passages.title: Stellagosa
passages.text: ...so many of them...

passages.title: The Consumed
passages.text:
<The whelpling is alive, but unconscious. One of the withered must have already drained it of mana.>

<You've already learned that exposed ley crystals contain a small amount of magical energy. Perhaps you can use one to revive some of the whelps.>

passages.title: The Consumed
passages.text: Clever <race>. Yes, a ley crystal should bring them back to their senses.

passages.title: The Consumed
passages.text:
I owe you a great debt, <name>.

Helping a weakened old dragon like me is valorous enough. Saving my whelplings, and securing the future of our bloodline?

I am now firmly committed to your cause.

passages.title: The Nightborne Prince
passages.text:
<Senegos is focused.>

I sense it now. In the ruined building, to the east. One of these cretins must have tapped deep into the ley line.

I suspect he will be heavily defended, <name>. Once again, the well-being of my brood is in your hands.

passages.title: The Nightborne Prince
passages.text:
He may not be slain, but at least he is gone.

Without their leader, the mindless withered should soon scatter and die.

passages.title: Still Alive
passages.text:
Wait, what was it that I heard? Was it... "feast on the dragons"? We must check on grandfather, right away!

Let me know when you're ready to depart.

passages.title: Still Alive
passages.text: No... we're too late!

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
Thank the Light I found you!

Highlord Fordring has called all paladins to Light's Hope Chapel to discuss our next course of action following the Broken Shore. He sent me to personally make sure you were in attendance.

I will ask Khadgar to direct this portal to Light's Hope for you. We must make haste.

passages.title: Runas the Shamed
passages.text:
I fell so quickly, <name>. I am not as strong as I once was. We truly do need your help.

One of these disgusting creatures ran off with several of the whelplings. I heard him called by name:

Runas.

I will survive. Home is not far. You still have strength, though. Slay this Runas before he does any more damage to our brood.

passages.title: Runas the Shamed
passages.text: Ah, Stella. Always so quick to act. She is still young.

passages.title: Runas the Shamed
passages.text:
Keep your distance from that one, <name>.

Those fallen elves are all the same. As two-faced as they come.

passages.title: The Hunger Returns
passages.text:
<Runas looks antsy.>

I can help you, and I very much want to help you, but I'm a bit distracted. Look at all that raw, unfiltered, mouthwatering mana...

<Runas slaps his own face.>

No! NO! You must stay in control!

I simply need to clear my head. Yes, that's it. A few of my depraved brethren carry small mana jewels around with them in case they need a quick burst of energy. Find a few for me? Then I will show you how to get your ley line back.

passages.title: The Hunger Returns
passages.text: Do you have them? Please tell me you have them, my friend.

passages.title: The Hunger Returns
passages.text:
<Runas feverishly crushes the jewels and gets to work rubbing magical dust on his face, arms, and back.>

<He is, for the moment, in bliss.>

passages.title: Leyline Abuse
passages.text:
These monsters are pulling mana directly out of the ground. This explains why not even my mana pools can dull my pain.

I worry about my brood. Without the power of the ley lines, we are nothing. At this rate, I may not even be able to help you with your Tidestone.

Look for their mana siphons, and punish the cowardly nightfallen elves that are using them.

passages.title: Leyline Abuse
passages.text: With each one of these cretins you slay, I grow stronger.

passages.title: Leyline Abuse
passages.text:
I do feel a bit stronger.

Those siphons nearly did me in, <name>.

passages.title: Agapanthus
passages.text: <This whelpling is trying to get your attention. She locks eyes with you, then quickly flicks her head toward the northeast.>

passages.title: Agapanthus
passages.text: Hail, <class>. We could use your aid.

passages.title: Feasting on the Dragon
passages.text:
You killed their leader, so they came here? Understandable. These creatures crave only one thing - magic - and they can sniff it out from leagues away.

Without a leader, they will soon wither and die. Our only recourse in the meantime is to put as many as possible down before they take these dragons with them!

passages.title: Feasting on the Dragon
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: Feasting on the Dragon
passages.text: That will have to do for now.

passages.title: Supplies From the Skies
passages.text:
Are you feeling alright? Say 'ah.'

<Mishka attempts to depress your tongue with a damp twig.>

Sorry... we are in desperate need of medical supplies here. The infirmary on the Skyfire was well-stocked, but it's all scattered to the winds now.

Anything you can salvage from the wreck will save lives!

passages.title: Supplies From the Skies
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: Supplies From the Skies
passages.text: Just in time! I was about to start bandaging wounds with leaves.

passages.title: Boarded!
passages.text:
Glad to see you survived the crash. Unfortunately, so did most of the enemy's boarding party.

Just the thought of those monsters setting foot on my ship makes me sick. Wipe them out, adventurer. For my crew... For King Wrynn...

For the Alliance!

passages.title: Boarded!
passages.text: There will be no peace with those monsters running free.

passages.title: Boarded!
passages.text:
Don't worry about the ship - it's just wood and metal.

The Skyfire lives on as long as we keep fighting.

passages.title: Lightning Rod
passages.text:
<Overspark's tiny hands move like lightning, affixing coils and tubes to the device before cramming it into a parachute pack.>

Put this on.

Just up the hill you'll find the front half of the Skyfire - and the big nest of storm drakes it crashed into! We can use the energy from those drakes to charge the transponder.

You'll have to incite them, of course, but the device should draw most of the power.

The probability of you being electrocuted is well within acceptable parameters!

passages.title: Archdruid of the Claw
passages.text:
Near the southern edge of our forest you will find Sleeper's Barrow.

There, Archdruid Koda Steelclaw and her dedicated disciples carry out their sacred duty to observe the Emerald Dream.

Find disciple Rylissa Bearsong in Steelclaw Vale and notify her of the crisis in the Grove of Cenarius.

passages.title: Archdruid of the Claw
passages.text:
The forest already whispers of Malfurion's return. There are few among us who have not heard of his deeds.

The trees said he also travels with a companion, one named <name>. Are you he?

passages.title: Awakening the Archdruid
passages.text:
Now, we must focus our efforts on waking Archdruid Steelclaw.

She and our druid brethren slumber in the barrow dens to the south.

With the furbolgs quelled, we can pass safely to the entrance.

Go and awaken the Archdruid. I pray to Elune that we are not too late.

passages.title: Awakening the Archdruid
passages.text: <The Archdruid's deep, shallow breaths rumble across the chamber.>

passages.title: The Demons Below
passages.text:
Something, someone, intended us to never awaken. I sense their presence is still here in the barrow.

<Koda takes a moment to stand.>

My body is weak from deep slumber.

If you would aid us, clear our barrow of any enemies.

passages.title: The Demons Below
passages.text: This was no accident. Someone intended us to sleep forever.

passages.title: The Demons Below
passages.text: Excellent. The chambers are clear. Very impressive, <class>.

passages.title: Out of the Dream
passages.text:
Malfurion Stormrage... A name I have not heard in centuries.

He was teacher to many of us. If he seeks my audience, I cannot refuse.

I will go to the Grove of Cenarius, but first, we must awaken the rest of my clan. They slumber with no way of waking.

A mysterious force of great power is at work against us.

I am still too weak from my hibernation. Please, stranger, go and free them from their dreams.

passages.title: Out of the Dream
passages.text: The Druids of the Claw must awaken. We are needed.

passages.title: Out of the Dream
passages.text: Well done, hero. With my brethren at my side, we will be ready to aid Malfurion.

passages.title: The Chieftain's Beads
passages.text:
The ceremonial beads, decorated with shells and feathers, are worn by the clan's chieftain.

Perhaps Elder Sookh would be interested in seeing these.

passages.title: The Chieftain's Beads
passages.text:
Graw was the first to succumb to the madness, and the rest of the clan followed.

With these, I will take the reins as our clan's new chieftain.

Thank you, traveler. I will do my best to rebuild my clan.

passages.title: Entangled Dreams
passages.text:
I sense powerful magic emanating from deep within the barrow.

Whatever is down there weaves a powerful spell, entangling us within our dreams.

I am still too weak, but your skills are quite impressive, hero. I can see why Malfurion puts his trust in you.

Go and eliminate the source of this magic.

passages.title: Entangled Dreams
passages.text: Someone entangled us within a sinister spell.

passages.title: Entangled Dreams
passages.text:
In my dreams, I saw the satyr's leader. His face was familiar, though I could not see it clearly.

I pray to Elune that it is not too late. I will go to Malfurion at once.

passages.title: Making the Rounds
passages.text:
You must be wondering what all of this is about. Please, walk with me.

I have some final preparations to make before we set sail, and I know that your presence will inspire the crew.

passages.title: Making the Rounds
passages.text: As soon as preparations are complete, we set out for Stormheim.

passages.title: Making the Rounds
passages.text: Are you with us?

passages.title: The Ancient Trials
passages.text:
<As the raven stares into your eyes, an odd voice fills your mind.>

I know who you are, champion, and I know what you seek.

Come to me, if you think yourself truly worthy.

passages.title: The Ancient Trials
passages.text:
I'm sure your head is filled with questions. Answers will come, in time.

I am Havi, and my words are those of the Valarjar - the glorious keepers of the Halls of Valor. 

You will need my help if it is the Aegis you seek. Oh yes, I know your goals outsider. As I know many things...

passages.title: Preserving The Lore
passages.text:
<A cool breeze of thought and memory enters your mind as you touch the strangely glowing stone. Within an instant, the purpose of this stone has been made manifest.>

<You realize that what you hold is a Stone of Remembrance; an object imbued with druidic knowledge and lore. The greedy Stoneblood harpies must have stolen these precious artifacts from the druids in Thas'talah. You decide to search for more of these missing stones and return them to the Archdruid of Lore.>

passages.title: Defending The Grove
passages.text:
The harpies have had a presence in Val'Sharah for hundreds of years. They have never been much more than an occasional nuisance; thus we have tolerated their presence here within these woods.

However, something has emboldened them... it feels as though the forest is weakening... they must sense it as well.

The opportunistic harpies have broken the peace and attacked us in a time of weakness.

Help us defend Thas'talah by slaying the invaders.

passages.title: A True Leader Inspires Others
passages.text:
<Lord/Lady> <name>, for all of your mastery over the Light you cannot possibly be everywhere at once. As newly ordained Knights of the Silver Hand it is our duty to carry out your will and defend our world from the darkness.

There is an ancient tome within this sanctum by the armory that can serve as the means to disperse your will - direct our blades and we will carry out your command.

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text:
Per your contract you will help me gather supplies for a perfectly harmless ritual.

I need feathers, and horns. Lots of horns. See those shadowrunners, prowlers and heron over there in the Olivian Veil? They should have lots of both.

Oh! And I need olives. Lots of olives. One for each finger.

Minion! Let's ride!

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text: This land is ripe for the taking. Especially the olives. They are really ripe. And I love ripe olives.

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text: Mmmm. Olives. I love these things. They are the only reason worth to come to this filthy world.

passages.title: Solid as a Rock
passages.text:
Cenarius requires me?

I shall depart as soon as I am able, but I mustn't leave while my druids are in danger. A vile harpy coven has emerged and seeks to claim my grove as their own.

These vermin inflict a petrifying disease which, given time, will destroy the infected.

While I wish for all of my followers to be cured, it is crucial that my elder disciples survive to protect the grove in my absence.

If you would assist us, find my disciples and rouse them from this terrible state.

passages.title: Solid as a Rock
passages.text: Have you roused my disciples, traveler?

passages.title: Solid as a Rock
passages.text:
Your arrival was a blessing, friend.

Ande'thoras-ethil.

passages.title: Totemic Call
passages.text:
I heard the others talking earlier. I may know the cause of their fear.

They say the Chieftain has a mysterious totem. It gives him power, and fearful visions.

If you destroy the totem, the madness will end.

passages.title: Totemic Call
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>! My nephew is returned to me.

He explains that the source of the madness comes from a powerful totem, deep in our village. 

It makes sense, but who - or WHAT - gave us such a thing?

I will share this knowledge with the druids at once.

passages.title: Seeds of Remedy
passages.text:
Several of my fellow druids have been gravely wounded. Although my restorative abilities will keep them stabilized, there is still more we can do to aid them.

<Aaelar produces a handful of glowing seeds from his pouch.>

These are efflorescent seeds imbued with the blessing of nature. If I had more of them, I could create a potion that would greatly aid in the recovery of the wounded.

Harvest the efflorescent saplings that grow near the fountain of Delyra and I will prepare the potion.

passages.title: Menacing Sprites
passages.text:
The local sprites are running amok and causing all sorts of problems!

Val'sharah is home to a variety of forest and pond sprites will take any opportunity to spread mischief and chaos. It seems as though an especially wicked group of sprites have descended upon Thas'talah in the wake of the harpy invasion.

They are attacking the local wildlife and bullying the nearby faerie dragons. If you aid the local woodland creatures by taking care of the sprite menace, you will have our thanks.

passages.title: Val'sharah
passages.text: [PH] Go through the portal in Dalaran and meet Malfurion Stormrage in Val'Sharah.

passages.title: Cenarius, Keeper of the Grove
passages.text:
Greetings, hero.

Welcome to Val'sharah. It has been an age since I have set foot in these precious woods. Too long...

Our work here is simple. We must call upon my mentor, Cenarius, and learn where he safeguards the Tears of Elune. With them, you will be one step closer to sealing Sargeras' Tomb and thwarting the Legion.

You have many treacherous tasks in front of you. Consider your visit here a brief respite.

Come, this will not take long.

passages.title: Eyes in the Overlook
passages.text:
Alliance personnel from the Skyfire were spotted parachuting into Blackbeak Overlook.

I was unable to confirm numbers or positions during my flyover, but I did see parachutes tangled in treetops and a LOT of ravenbears on the ground.

If anyone is up there, they must be laying low and keeping an eye on us.

I have posted a rider at the top of the overlook to keep watch while I press forward into Stormheim.

- Liza Cullen, Dread-Rider - 1st Wing

passages.title: [PH] Worg Pelts
passages.text:
You know, it looks awful cold up there. If you plan on surviving your trip through those mountains, you should probably go prepared.

You'll find some worgs roaming the hills around here, and some of them still have their winter coats. Get yourself a few pelts to layer on while you're up there.

passages.title: Accessories of the Cursed
passages.text:
Wait! Before ye go rushin' off, we might want to be gettin more than just seaweed. 

Ye see, these vrykul also be carrying bones with them - worn all over like jewelry. If ye can get yer hands on some of the bones they got lyin around, it'll add to the disguise.

So what ye waitin for?

passages.title: Accessories of the Cursed
passages.text: Make sure ye've got enough bones before we move on.

passages.title: Accessories of the Cursed
passages.text:
Ah yes, these will do. 

Now lets see what we can make to fool old Guarm, eh?

passages.title: The Ranger Lord
passages.text:
Good to see you survived the wreck. Nathanos made it as well, though his face is now even uglier than before.

He took a group of rangers north to look for Sylvanas - nobody has seen her since the battle.

He asked me to send you his way if you ever woke up.

passages.title: The Ranger Lord
passages.text:
<Nathanos narrows his eyes at the wreckage of Sylvanas' ship.>

She's out there... she has to be.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
The vrykul around here seem to use scales from these drakes to fashion their armor. 

If you were able to gather enough material from the local drakes, you may be able to make something useful out of it.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text: Oh, what do you have there?

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
Good thinking gathering up these scales. 

It should be simple enough to make a solid piece of armor from them.

passages.title: Halting the Nightmare
passages.text:
The corruption of the vale is the work of satyrs.

The new power they wield is unlike any I've seen... it is dark, seething and terrible.

Nefarious demon totems help spread their taint upon the land.

The Nghtmare totems must be destroyed if we are to hold back the tide of corruption.

passages.title: Stealth by Seaweed
passages.text:
There! The disguise be complete!

Don't mind the smell, there. It's probably better that we smell like the kvaldir, as well. Though I have a feeling I'll be needin a priest to get this stench out once we're gone.

passages.title: Stealth by Seaweed
passages.text:
Gods, what is that stench?! 

This disguise had better work!

passages.title: Stealth by Seaweed
passages.text: That was a truly revolting, outsider. Even in death I've never witnessed such a disgusting smell.

passages.title: Rescued From Darkness
passages.text:
Midnight Vale is home to a unique breed of Nightsaber known as the Vale Prowler. For centuries, our clan has lived in harmony with these great feline hunters.

However, even as we speak satyrs are twisting and corrupting the vale into a place of death and nightmare. Even the forest itself lashes out in torment against the living, causing many of the forest creatures to flee the vale.

I fear for the safety of the youngest nightsabers, who may yet be caught in the twisting chaos, unable to escape.

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text:
Exposure to this particular "byproduct" is quite nasty.

Rapid cell degeneration quickly reduces the subject to a shambling husk incapable of any reason or thought beyond a violent, throbbing hatred for the warmth of life.

As you might imagine, the local fauna have been affected by the spill. Oh, and most of the crew as well...

Anyway, good luck!

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text:
Come now, surely you don't intend to leave them in this state? Have you no compassion?

How about money - you like money, don't you?

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text: The R.A.S. is nothing if not humane.

passages.title: The Emerald Queen
passages.text:
<name>, you have returned. Good.

I have counseled with the other archdruids and concluded that Cenarius' condition is merely a symptom of a much greater problem. Your experiences in Moonclaw Vale make that clear.

We need help.

There is one who can bring understanding to these events. With Thaon gone, we must ask that you aid us in reaching out to the Lady of Dreams.

passages.title: The Emerald Queen
passages.text: Behold, Ysera, the Emerald Queen.

passages.title: Archdruid of Lore
passages.text:
Elothir resides in the ancient grove Thas'talah, where he communes with nature and instructs his acolytes in the ways of healing and the preservation of lore.

Seek him out and tell him that he is desperately needed here.

passages.title: Archdruid of Lore
passages.text: Welcome, traveler.

passages.title: Archdruid of the Vale
passages.text:
Deep within our forest lies Moonclaw Vale.

There you will find a reclusive group of feral druids charged with the protection of Val'sharah from any that would seek to disrupt the balance of nature.

These druids are led by Thaon Moonclaw, the most fierce of the Archdruids.

Seek him out. Let him know that Cenarius is in need of his aid.

passages.title: Archdruid of the Vale
passages.text: Cenarius will have my aid once my grove has been made safe.

passages.title: Nature's Call
passages.text:
What vile power is this?!

A curse with the strength to paralyze a demigod? Unimaginable!

Quickly, <name>, you must gather the archdruids of the forest. With their help, we can summon Ysera. She will surely know what horror has overtaken my mentor.

I will remain here and lend Cenarius what aid I can.

Return to Lorlathil and speak with Aranelle. She will know the archdruids' whereabouts.

And please, friend, make haste...

passages.title: Nature's Call
passages.text: Cenarius is in need? Lord of the Forest, we shall not fail you...

passages.title: Bottled Up
passages.text:
<You've found a message in a bottle on the corpse. It's a request for aid from someone named Okuna Longtusk. Okuna claims that he and his fellow shipmates are being held prisoner by sea giants.

Maybe if you show the note to the ghost of Lady Irisse at the Crumbled Palace, she can point you in the right direction?>

passages.title: Bottled Up
passages.text:
You say you found this message in a bottle? How quaint.

Yes, I can point you in the right direction, but are you sure you want to take on the sea giant prince and his skrogs? Just to free a bunch of unwashed sailors?

passages.title: Wings of Liberty
passages.text:
When the Felskorn assaulted the nest, the Thorignir fought bravely to save our brood. But their demonic allies proved too much, and many of us were captured.

Even now they work to corrupt my brothers and sisters to turn them to their side. 

Please, outsider, free them from this fate!

passages.title: Wings of Liberty
passages.text: What news do you bring of my brothers and sisters?

passages.title: Wings of Liberty
passages.text:
I am truly indebted to you for this act. My siblings were not able to defend themselves against the Felskorn, and would have ended up their slaves. 

You are a true friend of the Thorignir.

passages.title: Heart of a Dragon
passages.text:
Through brute force and corruption, the God-King has taken the power you seek, but there may be hope for you and the Thorignir, <class>.

With the aid of fel powers such as I've never seen, the Felskorn are corrupting our young and seeking to enslave the Thorignir. Their leader, a demon of great power, has captured our mother and seeks to bend her to the God-King's will.

Find her and free her from the demon's grasp - only then might the Thorignir regain our power and grant you aid.

passages.title: Heart of a Dragon
passages.text: Have you found our brood-mother?

passages.title: Heart of a Dragon
passages.text:
I am relieved to hear that our mother is safe. 

I am sure she will wish to thank you herself.

passages.title: The Ashbringer
passages.text:
The blade fell... during the battle... Broken Shore...

<Tirion coughs up blood.>

My time... is short. You must go ahead... into the temple ruins...

You must... retrieve...

...the Ashbringer.

passages.title: Journey to the Repose
passages.text:
For now, the Illidari can hold the line against the Legion. We will return later to help them drive the Legion from the upper reaches of Faronaar. You and I must concentrate on the Pillars of Creation if the Tomb of Sargeras is to be resealed.

Your saving of Stellagosa is fortuitous. Surely if anyone knows where a Pillar of Creation is, it will be her grandfather, Senegos.

The Azurewing Repose is to the northeast. I will meet you there, <name>.

passages.title: Journey to the Repose
passages.text:
He is... he's dying! Senegos is possibly the oldest dragon alive. We cannot simply let him slip away.

There is something not quite right with the magic energy here, I can feel it.

passages.title: Unfortunate Circumstances
passages.text:
The Illidari ask us to trust them, but all I see is failure. Look around... this entire city has been lost!

I tracked down the pit lord Malinoth here and brought what few of my men I had with me to put an end to this depravity. They were not enough.

The brute threw us in this cage and was 'saving us for later.' We need your help, <name>.

passages.title: Frenzied Furbolgs
passages.text:
I would help you seek audience with the Archdruid, but we have a difficult situation on our hands.

The nearby furbolgs have gone into a frenzied rage.

For days, it has been all we can do to protect our grove from their aggression.

They have cut off our access to the barrow dens, where the Archdruid and our clan sleep in the Emerald Dream.

In order to awaken them, we must first get past the furbolg.

passages.title: Frenzied Furbolgs
passages.text: The conflict against the furbolgs is abated, for now.

passages.title: The Ancient Trials
passages.text:
<As the raven stares into your eyes, an odd voice fills your mind.>

I know who you are, champion, and I know what you seek.

Come to me, if you think yourself truly worthy.

passages.title: The Ancient Trials
passages.text:
I'm sure your head is filled with questions. Answers will come, in time.

I am Havi, and my words are those of the Valarjar - the glorious keepers of the Halls of Valor. 

You will need my help if it is the Aegis you seek. Oh yes, I know your goals outsider. As I know many things...

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text:
Hey there!

You seem like a gullib- er... um... "intelligent" type.

I propose a deal.

I need a minion to be my muscle to help me acquire a few special... "ingredients" for a ritual.

In exchange, I'll give you my former master to do with whatever you demon-slaying types do with demons.

If you are interested, just sign here. In blood, please.

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text: Yeah! Yeah! You read the contract? I made it myself. Really good binding clauses in there.

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text: At last! A minion of my very own!

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text:
I have a theory, <name>.

Have you encountered the nightfallen elves of Azsuna? They descend from the Highborne, and the accomplishments of Highborne smiths are legendary.

These fallen elves do a bit of arcane tinkering, crafting sentries to patrol their camps.

Bring me a memory core from one of their constructs. Who knows what manner of smithlore might lie within!

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text: Hopefully we can extract something useful.

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text: If my guess is correct, the answer to our welding problem lies within this core.

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text:
I think I have just the thing to extract the information from this core for you.

<Timofey loads the core into the hopper of a clearly goblin-made machine, then covers his ears.>

You may wish to avert your eyes, blacksmith.

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text: Highborne! Ancient Highborne! What an amazing find!

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text: ...is what I would say if we weren't floating directly above the ancestral home of the Highborne. You need this translated or something?

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text:
I could spend hours poring over the details of this fascinating manuscript!

...is what I would say if this weren't the simplest of tasks for someone of my skill level. It's about something called "Leysmithing". Here.

<The gnome scribbles down a translation on the back of the scroll.>

There it is, word-for-word. Bring me something interesting next time.

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text: Did you find the engineering shop?

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text:
I hadn't even thought far enough ahead to realize you'd need this to be translated, too. Good thinking.

See, this is why I keep adventurers like you around the shop.

passages.title: The Highmountain Smiths
passages.text:
I think we've gone as far as we can go with what I know, <name>.

The tauren of Highmountain must have some smiths among their ranks. See if you can find out how to further progress our leysmithing abilities from them.

passages.title: The Highmountain Smiths
passages.text: You, outsider, think yourself worthy of our wisdom?

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text:
You wish me to teach you how to strengthen your crafts? We do not simply share the secrets of our trade with outsiders who ask for them.

We do, however, respect craftsmanship and discipline.

Let's see your hammerwork. Our greenhorn trainees use those small anvils over there. Craft your best pair of gauntlets so I may judge your work.

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text: I'm waiting, outsider.

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text:
The craftsmanship is good, but the quality is feeble at best.

<Barm snaps the gauntlets in half and throws them to floor>

You have proven yourself worthy of my tutelage however.

passages.title: From One Master to Another
passages.text:
Now young one, go back to your master
in Dalaran and continue to practice your swing. We'll always be here if you wish to come back and learn more.

passages.title: From One Master to Another
passages.text: I see, the strength of their work comes from the technique of their hammer strikes. Very interesting...

passages.title: Felsmith Nal'ryssa
passages.text:
Word has been circulating in smithing circles about a pair of Illidari blacksmiths that have been doing exciting work out on the demon-infested front lines of Suramar. I'd follow up myself, but anything described as "demon-infested" is a little too exotic for my tastes.

I just make the armor. I prefer not to wear it.

You, though... you could follow up on this tip. Be on the lookout for Nal'ryssa. From what I hear, she's a hell of a smith.

passages.title: Felsmith Nal'ryssa
passages.text: You here to lend us a hand?

passages.title: Part of the Team
passages.text:
You're a blacksmith?

<The elf looks down at your hammer.>

Still working in leystone, are you? I might be able to help you out.

Alliances out here are hard-won. You've got a pretty face, but that's no guarantee that you aren't working for the demons. I can't afford to trust you yet.

Don't come back until you're caked in demon's blood. Then we'll talk smithing.

passages.title: Part of the Team
passages.text: That'll do.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text:
You lack recipes for boots?

What, were you trained by a tauren or something?

Hurry up, then. We probably have a few minutes before the demons attack again. Here's a pattern - show me your work.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text: Watch your step out here on the front lines. This isn't your peaceful floating city's blacksmithing shop.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. You know how to swing a hammer.

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text:
Listen, <class>. We need smiths like you to carry on the traditions of the Illidari, should we fail in our crusade against the Legion. You are ready to learn.

Bring me materials. Lots of them. When you return, we will have much to discuss.

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text: Are you ready to learn?

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text: Good. Now let's get to work.

passages.title: The Firmament Stone
passages.text:
When working with felslate and demonsteel, one must use special equipment. Specifically, an anvil hard enough to withstand the energy given off when felslate is hammered.

Urael and I no longer possess such an anvil. But your friends, the Highmountain tauren, do.

Gain access to the Firmament Stone, their sacred anvil, and we can start working with demonsteel again.

passages.title: The Firmament Stone
passages.text:
You have returned, <name>. Have you come for more training?

What? The Firmament Stone?

That's another matter entirely.

passages.title: Tribal Knowledge
passages.text:
First, however, you'll need proper patterns for demonsteel armor. While access to the stone is earned through hard work and perseverance, access to our recipes is limited to the trusted members of our tribe.

Perhaps you should seek another smith if you wish to discuss demonsteel patterns.

passages.title: Tribal Knowledge
passages.text:
I wouldn't expect the tauren to part with their recipes easily. We are not quite as... bull-headed as they are, but even our recipes will come at a price.

Still, you have earned access to the Firmament Stone, and proven the path to another great anvil, should Urael and I need it.

You have earned this recipe, as a token of our thanks.

passages.title: Lord Hal'shara's Tomb
passages.text: The tomb, I've found it.

passages.title: See Ya Later, Oscillator
passages.text:
Those jawless mooks are actually trying to salvage parts from our ship! They can't possibly appreciate superior gnomish technology... Perhaps its shiny nature is appealing to their simple inclinations.

In any case, I need a crystal oscillator for our new transponder. It's the shiniest part of the whole system, they're bound to have it set aside somewhere!

passages.title: See Ya Later, Oscillator
passages.text: Did you find the oscillator?

passages.title: See Ya Later, Oscillator
passages.text:
<Overspark examines the crystal carefully.>

Yep, still shiny.

passages.title: Worthy of the Stone
passages.text:
You have nothing more to prove to me, <name>. Your training is complete.

Only a very small herd of smiths have earned the right to the Firmament Stone. You should speak with Muirn Ironhorn, who maintains vigil over our sacred stone. He will tell you what to do next.

passages.title: Worthy of the Stone
passages.text:
A new face? It's been years...

This is the Firmament Stone. Memorize her curves. Learn her intricacies. If you truly wish to push your smithing skill to the next level, I predict that you will be spending a lot of time at her side.

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text:
Now that we know the foxflower flux is safe to use, we can start stocking it. That being said, I don't particularly feel like picking flowers. Do you feel like picking flowers? Didn't think so.

Go talk to the alchemists and herbalists across the way. I'm sure we can set up some sort of work order arrangement.

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text: Have you spoken with the alchemists and herbalists yet?

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text: Now that that's all taken care of, we can move on to improving our recipes.

passages.title: To Old Friends
passages.text:
I sense a powerful dark presence here, <name>, but it is not of Xavius. This feels too familiar.

I sense a druid's touch here, a druid twisted by the shadow of the Nightmare.

We must deal with this threat if we are to find Xavius. I will take to the skies and lend you my aid.

Find this corrupted druid and cut down his tainted and twisted plants.

passages.title: To Old Friends
passages.text:
Know this, <name>. You did the only thing you could.

When a mortal has become corrupted by the nightmare, there is no return. Only death will set them free.

passages.title: Malfurion's Fury
passages.text:
The loss of Cenarius to the nightmare is a devastating blow to us all.

Though Malfurion's rage is justified, his hatred of Xavius has burned for centuries and I fear that his blind rage will be used as a weapon against him.

May Elune guide us in our search for him, lest we have yet another friend to mourn today.

passages.title: Malfurion's Fury
passages.text:
Oh, <name>...

What is becoming of this precious land?

passages.title: TRACKING Nightmare 02
Gates of Valhallas
passages.text:
Escaping the grasp of Helya is no small feat. You may prove to be a worthy warrior after all.

Skovald has entered Valhallas; you are running out of time. Legion has corrupted the minds of the Skovald's men. A battalion of unworthy vrykul is attempting to enter the portal to Valhallas.

The giants that protect the gates are fighting a losing battle. There is no end to Legion's onslaught.

Speak with the dragon, Vehdir, inside the gates near the portal. He will aid you on your next task.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
The vrykul around here seem to use scales from these drakes to fashion their armor. 

If you were able to gather enough material from the local drakes, you may be able to make something useful out of it.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text: What have we here?

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
Good thinking. If the vrykul can use the drake scales for their armor, why not us? 

It shouldn't be too tough to work this into something serviceable.

passages.title: Cry Thunder!
passages.text:
You have proven yourself an ally of the Thorignir and we will lend you our strength. I would ask one last favor of our new champion, though. 

The dragon who guided you to me awaits his vengeance against the vrykul. Together I wish for you to show these Drekirjar what it means to cross the Thorignir. Be they Felskorn or not, their malice has caused suffering to my brood. Their toll must be paid in blood.

Speak to Vethir when you are ready.

passages.title: Cry Thunder!
passages.text:
<The raven squawks, and Havi's voice fills your head>

You are indeed mighty, as the trial shows. 

But valor is a different animal - one you think to tame?

passages.title: The Temple of Elune
passages.text:
Cenarius is in danger.

If his condition is not reversed soon, he will be lost to the Nightmare that threatens the Emerald Dream. To spare him that fate, we must have the Tears of Elune - the same relic you were sent here to retrieve.

Elune's temple is not far. Go there. Find Lyanis. Show her my seal and instruct her to release the tears into your custody.

Hurry, <name>. Time is short.

passages.title: The Temple of Elune
passages.text:
You - you bear the mark of The Dreamer. Elune be praised!

You've arrived just in time, visitor. Shaladrassil's roots are at our doorstep...

passages.title: A Village in Peril
passages.text:
The corpse of Darcy Heathrow lies before you pierced by several arrows and knife wounds.

In one hand she clutches a note, written with a feeble hand, that reads:

"The dead march on Bradensbrook.

Help us, please!"

passages.title: A Village in Peril
passages.text: We don't need any help, and we don't like strangers wanderin' around on our land.

passages.title: Children of the Night
passages.text:
I am no enemy to these people, but there is no convincing them of that.

Their village has come under attack by some very old friends of mine. Friends who are no longer... living.

There's no telling who or what controls them, but in life these noble soldiers would never engage in such acts. That's a mystery for another time.

For now, help me earn the trust of these villagers. Strike down the Black Rook enemies who are terrorizing their citizens.

passages.title: Children of the Night
passages.text: The attackers are night elves, yes, but they are not the same night elves I once knew.

passages.title: Children of the Night
passages.text: Good. These innocent villagers have done nothing to deserve these attacks. You have done well to help them.

passages.title: A Sight For Sore Eyes
passages.text:
Do you see those ravenous birds flying above my farm? Vicious creatures are spreading their filth an' eatin' my crops.

I'd get rid of them with my trusty gun, but my eyesight's gone downhill.

Take this flare gun and mark them for me.

Once I get my sights on them, I'll make 'em scatter.

passages.title: A Sight For Sore Eyes
passages.text: Heh? Is that you again?

passages.title: A Sight For Sore Eyes
passages.text: Well love, we sure did take care of them! Thank you, <class>. Glad ta see I 'aven't lost my touch.

passages.title: For the Corn!
passages.text:
I've got a full summer's corn harvest just sittin' out in the field. I need some muscle to bring it in before the night elf raiders can destroy it.

Get out there and bring me those crops, and I'll reward you handsomely.

The folks back in town need this food, and I sure as heck ain't eating rats for another winter.

passages.title: For the Corn!
passages.text: The corn isn't gonna gather itself.

passages.title: For the Corn!
passages.text:
All right, I'll get those barrels loaded up and delivered to the village in no time.

Thank you, <name>. There'll be a lot of full bellies because of you.

passages.title: Black Rook Orders
passages.text:
The letter is written in midnight ink:

"A demon invasion is imminent, but as long as the fires of Black Rook Hold blaze, we shall protect kaldorei lands. Kill any intruders who stand in our way."

- K.R."

Perhaps Jarod Shadowsong will want to see this.

passages.title: Silence in the City
passages.text:
There is a troubling silence from Suramar City this day.

Oculeth just informed me that the teleporter to the Waning Crescent has gone dark. He is not able to reach Vanthir, nor am I.

While I am hesitant to believe something dire has happened, I do feel this warrants investigation.

Speak with Oculeth and see if he can transport you to the Waning Crescent. We need to find out what happened.

passages.title: Silence in the City
passages.text: Something is amiss. I can feel it in my bones.

passages.title: Root Cause
passages.text:
The massive roots of Shaladrassil are spreading a horrible corruption throughout the forest.

If we are to save Val'sharah, we will need to find a way to stop the encroachment of the world tree.

If you bring me enough corrupted root samples, I may be able to discover their secrets.

passages.title: Root Cause
passages.text: Have you collected the root samples?

passages.title: Root Cause
passages.text:
It is as I feared, <race>. This corruption is... irreversible.

Our only course of action is to somehow find a way to fight it at its source.

passages.title: Mark of the Demon
passages.text:
The demonic rune glows in your hand, emanating dark power. A single word, inscribed in demon tongue, glows coldly... 

...GRAVAX...

passages.title: Mark of the Demon
passages.text: I am impressed that you were able to defeat such a powerful demon. We are fortunate that you have lent us your aid.

passages.title: Aid For the Wounded
passages.text: [PH] Many of our defenders have been gravely wounded on the battlefield. Take with you this moonstone and use it on our wounded allies on the battlefield. Heal their wounds and renew their courage against the forces of the enemy.
