passages.title: Cleansing the Corruption
passages.text:
All along the battlefield, the satyrs have erected dark totems that spread the corruption of the Emerald Nightmare upon the land.

As long as the Nightmare totems remain, we will not be able to hold back the corruption!

If you truly wish to aid us in the fight, destroy the totems that you encounter upon the battlefield.

Our survival depends on it!

passages.title: Nightmare Bombs
passages.text:
[PH] The satyrs have taken to the skies on giant bats. From the air they rain down the corruption of the nightmare upon us.

Disarm the nightmare bombs before they further corrupt the forest.

passages.title: Tears for Fears
passages.text:
The Tears of Elune are a sacred artifact, protected by my order for thousands of years. I tell you this so that you may understand the gravity of your request.

That said, Ysera is noble and wise and I trust in her guidance. You will find the tears in a vault at the eastern edge of the temple grounds.

Proceed with caution though, as that area has been overrun by demons.

passages.title: Tears for Fears
passages.text: Do you have the Tears of Elune?

passages.title: Tears for Fears
passages.text:
Xavius has stolen our sacred artifact?

Elune, forgive me. I have failed you.

passages.title: The Die is Cast
passages.text:
Thanks to your efforts the temple is safe, for now.

But the Tears of Elune are stolen and Shaladrassil, the world tree that once protected this land, is now an instrument in the hands of our enemy. The Emerald Dream itself is being overrun by Nightmare.

The hearts of our people falter, their faith tested like never before. Return to Ysera with my report, <name>, such as it is.

I shall plead with Elune with what time I have left here. May we somehow yet prevail.

passages.title: The Die is Cast
passages.text:
This is dire news indeed, <name>.

Draw upon your courage now, friend, for Azeroth needs her heroes more than ever before.

passages.title: The Demon's Trail
passages.text:
Xavius! How many times must I end that wretched satyr before he stays dead...

We must get to Shaladrassil and find Xavius before it is too late!

My wounds are grave, but they will heal... do not concern yourself with my safety. There is little time... we may already be too late...

passages.title: Our Last Hope
passages.text:
Your jailor, Maiev Shadowsong, stands outside the open door to your cell. The leader of the Wardens has just finished removing your bonds.

In the distance, you can hear sounds of battle. The unmistakable stench of the Burning Legion wafts through the air.

passages.title: Our Last Hope
passages.text:
The Vault has fallen to the Burning Legion.

It pains me to say it, but all is lost, but for one glimmer of hope... YOU. Believe me when I say, I did NOT want to have to do this. However, it would seem I have no choice.

Help me, demon hunter, and I will grant you your freedom.

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text:
Is this the end?

Our beloved Malfurion. I saw him in the Dreamer's clutches, but Ysera was... changed. Twisted.

Shaladrassil, our mighty world tree, is corrupted beyond recognition.

We were forced to flee our home without our belongings. Some were heirlooms, sacred to us. Return them to me if you can, <class>, I beg you.

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text: Have you retrieved them?

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text: It is not much, but it is better than I could have hoped for. You have our gratitude.

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text:
We cannot fight our way out of the Vault alone.

Two of your allies, Kayn Sunfury and Altruis the Sufferer, are imprisoned within this room. 

Free them with haste. Their strength will be of great use to us.

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text: <The lever seems to control the door.>

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text: <Pull the lever.>

passages.title: The Wormtalon Crone
passages.text:
A wicked coven of harpies have overtaken our village.

It was the twisting of the forest that forced us out of our village, but now that the harpies have moved in I fear that we may never be able to return.

The Wormtalon coven are led by a witch called Grelda the Crone. She has made her nest in a cave near our village.

If their leader is defeated, the remaining harpies will surely flee.

Slay Grelda the Crone and we will be forever in your debt, <class>.

passages.title: Malfurion's Cure
passages.text:
The cleansed Mooncaps glow radiantly in your hands as you lift them from the waters of the ancient moonwell.

Mender Onelle will need the Mooncaps in order to make a healing poultice for Malfurion's wounds.

passages.title: Heart of the Nightmare
passages.text:
I know only that my husband is somewhere deeper in this twisted forest.

He is still alive, but it remains to be seen if he is whole.

<Tyrande's expression hardens into a scowl as she peers at you.>

Elune herself cannot protect Xavius if he is not.

passages.title: Heart of the Nightmare
passages.text: No one is safe from this corruption.

passages.title: Reading the Leaves
passages.text:
<name>, my friend. You must succeed where I have failed. You must find our dear Malfurion.

As the Nightmare consumes my thoughts, I hear the voices of these twisted trees. I must cling to sanity long enough to aid you.

Venture into Ash'theran and bring me Corrupted Petals from the fallen denizens there.

With them, I might find your Archdruid while my mind is still my own.

passages.title: Reading the Leaves
passages.text:
Ahh... the fear! The panic!

I haven't the strength to fight much longer...

passages.title: Reading the Leaves
passages.text: The waking world is slipping further and further from my mind. But on the vestiges of this corruption consuming my mind, I sense Malfurion!

passages.title: Close Enough to Touch
passages.text:
He is near, <name>, I can feel it.

We must scour this place in search of my husband. I fear if we do not find him soon it will be too late.

You have been courageous throughout our search. I know you will not fail me now, <name>.

Thank you, and please hurry.

passages.title: Close Enough to Touch
passages.text: This cannot be!

passages.title: Hope Remains
passages.text: The Tear of Elune floats effortlessly, glistening in an ethereal pillar of moonlight.

passages.title: Fel Infusion
passages.text:
So many years of imprisonment has left us weak.

The Vault is overrun with demons. Kill them and gather their souls to regain your strength.

passages.title: Fel Infusion
passages.text: The color has returned to your face, <name>.

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text:
Look down there. We are vastly outnumbered.

We will need more allies on our side if we are to escape from here intact. Free the other Illidari imprisoned within the cells of this chamber.

We will need everyone to escape this place alive.

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text: Have you freed those you found in the cells?

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text: We always knew the Illidari would be called upon to defend this world. It is why we sacrificed everything to become who... WHAT... we are.

passages.title: Jarod's Mission
passages.text:
Since Maiev chased after Gul'dan at the Vault of the Wardens, her sisters among the Wardens have been searching far and wide for her whereabouts.

With so few Wardens remaining, I volunteered to join the search. I hope I will find sign of her within Black Rook Hold.

The fortress will be well guarded, and I will need help to break through. Help me find her, and I will reward you handsomely.

passages.title: Jarod's Mission
passages.text: Did you have any trouble getting here?

passages.title: Jarod's Mission
passages.text: What does the Legion want with Ravencrest? He was dead and buried ten millennia ago.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Kill Feral Dogs
passages.text:
You've done more than enough, <name>. My people and I can clean things up here.

You should return to town and report on our victory.

passages.title: Regroup
passages.text:
These people may be able to hold out here, but I know for certain that we cannot.

Every moment we spend here places them in danger of Elisande's forces retaliating against us.

We need to move. We need to find a place to regroup and recover.

Follow me. I think I know how we can get out of here.

passages.title: Regroup
passages.text: Oculeth has anticipated our arrival. Good, one less thing to worry on.

passages.title: Crackdown
passages.text:
Thalyssra is right to be concerned!

The network has not responded to my attempts to re-establish connection with the Waning Crescent. I do not know what happened, but given the circumstances I believe it prudent to investigate in person.

<name>, would you do the honors? I will send you as close to the Waning Crescent as I can.

passages.title: Crackdown
passages.text: Elisande... how could you?

passages.title: Crackdown
passages.text:
Someone must have informed the Grand Magistrix of Vanthir's involvement in the rebellion. Such violence is...

Elisande... How could you?

passages.title: The Warden's Signet
passages.text:
The night elf was carrying a signet engraved with the crest of the Wardens.

The band, made from a silvery, unbreakable metal, has been worn down by time, as if absently twisted and rubbed against its owner's finger.

passages.title: The Warden's Signet
passages.text:
<Jarod gazes at the ring for a long minute before closing his hands around it. He puts the ring in a pocket.>

This is Maiev's ring. She would never part with it.

She must be at Black Rook Hold!

passages.title: The Crusade Calls
passages.text:
((You have just finished the introduction sequence in Dalaran.))

Lord Maxwell Tyrosus of the Argent Crusade sent for you. He mentioned knowing of a weapon we could use against the Legion.

As much as I loathe their ilk, you should go to Krasus' Landing and speak with him. We need every advantage we can muster.

passages.title: Maiev's Trail
passages.text:
The fortress grounds are just up ahead. There is a large area to search, but if we split up, I believe we can cover a lot of ground.

Search the prison cages, the forge, and the guard tower for any signs of Maiev. I will check the upper ramparts and meet you on the other side of the keep.

passages.title: Maiev's Trail
passages.text: We will give this area a thorough search.

passages.title: Maiev's Trail
passages.text: Good work, <name>. There is no doubt that they have already moved Maiev into the prison cells beneath the tower.

passages.title: Black Rook Hold
passages.text:
Inside the chest, hidden amongst various knickknacks, is a signet engraved with a unique crest.

The band, made from a silvery, unbreakable metal, has been worn down by time, as if absently twisted and rubbed against its owner's finger.

passages.title: Black Rook Prison
passages.text:
I did not come this far to lose her in the final moments.

Maiev must be in the cells beneath Black Rook Hold.

I scouted above, and the entrance to the prison is guarded by a fearsome jailor.

I will sneak past and take out the guards inside. Defeat Araxxas, take the keys, and then meet me within.

passages.title: Black Rook Prison
passages.text: Do you have the keys?

passages.title: Black Rook Prison
passages.text: Good, these keys should open any of the cells within the prison.

passages.title: Kur'talos Ravencrest
passages.text:
Lord Ravencrest was a fearless leader, a seasoned commander, a man of integrity and honor, a teacher, and a protector of his people.

Malfurion, Illidan, Tyrande, and I... we were still young when he helped shape our destinies.

The sigil of his house was legendary. Observe, for a moment, the sigil over his former resting place and I shall tell you more of his legacy.

passages.title: Kur'talos Ravencrest
passages.text: The attacking spirits spoke of their lord and master. I fear the Legion has raised Lord Ravencrest to do their bidding. What price was paid for such a sinister revival, I do not know.

passages.title: Illidari Freedom
passages.text:
<The Illidari demon hunter is bleeding from several ghastly wounds. It appears he was left here to die.>

Within the prison are three of my... <cough>... comrades.

We were taken by surprise while scouting the area.

I am not long for this world, but please, save them.

passages.title: Illidari Freedom
passages.text: The other Illidari did not make it, but I owe you my life. There is one thing I learned during my time in the prisons: the demons within Black Rook Hold must die.

passages.title: No Reason to Stay
passages.text:
Elisande's purge of the Waning Crescent came so swiftly that few could react. Many of my people are dead or taken.

Some may have endured this atrocity. We need to make sure they are not left behind.

I need you to search the houses nearby for any survivors. See that they flee before they are discovered. Reassure them that there is no reason to stay. 

Not here, not while Elisande's insanity reigns.

passages.title: No Reason to Stay
passages.text: Did you find anyone?

passages.title: No Reason to Stay
passages.text: I see you managed to find some survivors. Good, that is a weight off my mind.

passages.title: Lieutenant of the Tower
passages.text:
All of your instincts were correct. Gul'dan raised Lord Ravencrest, and his ghostly army, from beyond the grave. Now, they serve the Legion, protecting secrets within the tower.

Although Ravencrest commands from above, Lieutenant Desdel Stareye operates the prisons.

He tormented me these past few moons, but I did not yield.

<Maiev runs a finger along her curved blade.>

His life must be ended.

passages.title: Lieutenant of the Tower
passages.text:
Lord Stareye came from a noble house, but in war, he never came close to Ravencrest or my brother.

Now that he is defeated, we can turn our attention to his commander.

However, that will be no easy task. We must gather our strength before facing Lord Ravencrest himself.

passages.title: Stop Gul'dan!
passages.text:
After his defeat at the Black Temple, we brought Illidan's lifeless body here, to be interred forever within the Vault of the Wardens.

Gul'dan has found his way through our defenses and is trying to steal the Betrayer's corpse.

Even in death, Illidan's body can be used by the Burning Legion. Gul'dan CANNOT succeed.

passages.title: Stop Gul'dan!
passages.text: Excellent. You have absorbed the powers of these brutes. Look how strong you have grown!

passages.title: Brotherly Love
passages.text:
Maiev will be somewhere in the prison. I found her discarded armor on my way here.

Let's split up to search the cells more quickly.

We must find her.

passages.title: Brotherly Love
passages.text:
<Maiev's face is bruised, her lips cracked, and her body covered in scars. She looks thin and ragged, but she moves with purpose.>

For weeks they tried to break me. Amateurs!

I kept my silence. I counted the minutes, measured their steps, and listened to the voices beyond my cell.

I have been waiting for my chance to escape, and to strike back at my captors.

Now, you bring my armor AND my blade. My salvation will be followed by bloodshed.

<Maiev smiles.>

passages.title: Into the Foul Creche
passages.text:
One of the demons that I interrogated revealed a particularly juicy bit of information. Apparently, there's an imp mother in the volcano that scribes Legion secrets.

Kor'vas has gone out to find that demon and bring those secrets back for us.

passages.title: Into the Foul Creche
passages.text: <name>. I've found her.

passages.title: Return to the Black Temple
passages.text:
Quickly, <name>, use the Sargerite Keystone.

We must get back to the Black Temple before it is too late!

passages.title: Return to the Black Temple
passages.text:
<As you invoke the power of the Sargerite Keystone, the fel portal is suffused with an otherworldly energy.

It is time to return triumphant to the Black Temple and aid Lord Illidan in repelling the invading forces from Azeroth and Shattrath City.>

passages.title: An End To War
passages.text:
It appears that the great Ancient of War, Ironbranch, has fallen to the Nightmare.

It pains me greatly to ask this of you, but Ironbranch must be put to rest.

In life, he once stood vigil in Shala'nir as a protector of the world tree. In death, my dear friend is no more than a destructive weapon that will be used to cause even more violence.

He must be slain before he does more harm to Val'sharah.

In my heart, I know that he would thank you for this mercy...

passages.title: The Fate of Val'sharah
passages.text:
Malfurion, my love.... My heart breaks for him, but I cannot follow where he goes.

I have sworn myself to Elune, my goddess, to defend her temples and lands with all that I am. I cannot stand by while my order is in danger.

May she keep you in her graces, Malfurion.

<Tyrande turns away, eyes glistening with tears.>

passages.title: The Fate of Val'sharah
passages.text: This shall be remembered as one of the darkest days in the history of our world. But hope remains. Elune's light has strengthened our resolve.

passages.title: Hard Lessons
passages.text:
Please understand, stranger, that I am a being of peace. I have discarded any vengeful nature long, long ago.

In my youth, however, many hard lessons were learned through discipline. When applied wisely and properly, discipline can be a great teacher and shaper of character.

It is in the spirit of wisdom and guidance that I would have you teach these harpies a memorable lesson.

passages.title: The Demon's Trail
passages.text:
Malfurion is nearby. I can sense him.

Search the summit of Andu'talah while I continue to scour the forest.

Be swift, <name>. Time is of the essence!

passages.title: The Demon's Trail
passages.text:
My husband, Malfurion, what has become of him?!

Answer me!

passages.title: Before We're Overrun
passages.text:
The doomguard commander and his queen must be dealt with. His eredar are summoning in a huge number of reinforcements.

We need to put an end to him before the Legion overruns our new foothold up in the volcano!

As an added benefit, you can steal his demonic power.

passages.title: Before We're Overrun
passages.text:
Already, the flow of demons from below has slowed to a trickle.

I can sense the doom guard's energy. You have become more powerful.

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This ore looks like nothing you've seen before.

A mystical sheen moves through the metal in complex, unpredictable patterns. Your trainer in Dalaran would certainly like to see this.

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text: What's that you've got there, boy?

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text:
It's so light. So pretty, too! Reminds me of elementium, a bit.

If you see any more ore like this, try and strike it with the grain. You'll waste much less of it.

passages.title: Turn the Keys
passages.text:
My roots wither... my branches die...

The Bonespeakers, they seek to silence the Runewood. The runestones are the key...

Turn the stones... release my bonds...

passages.title: Turn the Keys
passages.text: My shackles remain...

passages.title: Turn the Keys
passages.text:
So it was your footsteps I felt upon my woods as the runestones released their grip? 

You have my thanks, outsider.

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text:
This ore has clearly absorbed some of the latent ley energies within the Broken Isles. It is cool to the touch, and reflects light in odd, playful angles.

Your trainer in Dalaran should analyze this.

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text: What've ye brought me now?

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text:
Look at that! She's a lovely one, isn't she?

Treat this type of ore with care, lad. No fat-muscle shoulder swings necessary - just a gentle tap on the right spot and you'll extract much more ore than a beginner.

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text:
This is no normal leystone. It is much livelier, shimmering in complex, enthralling patterns. It is easy to stare at.

Your trainer in Dalaran would certainly like to have a look at this.

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text: Oh, my...

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text:
Now isn't that somethin'? You got this offa one of those rocky creatures down there?

Looks like ye only brought me a bit o' the torso, though. Next time, make sure to get the arms and head too. Lots o' good meat in there.

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text:
Leystone is a sensitive ore. Our smiths can coax great power out of it, but as miners, we must treat it with respect, or else its power will retreat inward.

<The tauren hands you what appears to be a GLASS mining pick.>

The next time you mine some leystone ore, use this pick. It will break if you strike too hard. THIS is the respect that leystone requires.

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text: You haven't broken my pick, have you?

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text:
You've learned much, <name>.

Stay a while. I have a story for you.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text:
A long, long time ago, a tauren by the name of Rethu entered this land. His exploits paved the road that all miners walk.

If you wish to learn more about mining, you must first learn about Rethu.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text: Listen well, <name>.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text: Echoes of Rethu's time in this land still remain, <name>. Be on the lookout for his influence when you are out in the field.

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text:
Tucked in between a few pieces of rubble, a scrap of paper catches your eye.

Mining carefully, you uncover the tattered remains of an old scroll. The tauren handwriting is archaic, but one word catches your eye:

"Rethu".

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text: Greetings, miner. What have you here?

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text:
This... this cannot be! A piece of Rethu's own mining log!

Look here, miner... it details a leystone mining technique he was working on...

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text:
This seam has been mined before - it bears the telltale diagonal ruts of a miner's pick.

Looking down, that pick now lays on the ground - handle broken, pick-point dulled with use and years.

Carved into the haft is a familiar name:

"Rethu"

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text: What is that you hold, miner?

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text:
Rethu's own mining pick...

Well, one of them, anyhow. Stories say he went through them almost weekly.

Still, I've never seen one with my own eyes. Look at the wear on the blade, miner. The angles he used... the strength with which he struck: we could learn much from studying this artifact.

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text:
The corpse of the rocky beast yielded an unusual treasure: a battered chunk of tauren's horn.

It is clearly very, very old, but something about its color and curve reminds you of Ronos Ironhorn at the Ironhorn Enclave.

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text: What... what is that, miner?

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text:
This... this could not be...

This is from a member my tribe, <name>. Where did you find this?

One of the first stories we ever learn about Rethu involves the day he lost his horn in battle. There is no way of knowing if this belonged to him but... but...

passages.title: Rethu's Lesson
passages.text:
You... miner... let me see your pick a moment.

<The tauren spirit eyes your mining equipment.>

You remind me of myself, when I once walked this land. Savor these moments, miner. They cannot last forever.

<With a bow, the spirit disappears.>

passages.title: Rethu's Lesson
passages.text:
You saw a spirit while out mining in the wilds?

No, I do not believe you. One mustn't spend too long out mining, it fatigues the mind. You must be seeing things.

Still, something seems... different about you. You've learned something. Perhaps there's some truth to your tale after all...

passages.title: Rethu's Experience
passages.text:
Miner... you... you know who I am?

I see. That is good. My tribe continues to honor its roots.

If you return to the land of the Ironhorn tribe... let them know that they are looked upon with pride.

passages.title: Rethu's Experience
passages.text:
<The tauren listens as you describe your encounter with the spirit of Rethu Ironhorn.>

I would not normally believe you, but... I can sense truth in your tale. You are a lucky miner.

I am pleased to know that our ancestors look upon us with pride. We have chosen an admirable path.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Rethu's Sacrifice
passages.text:
Miner... speak with me a moment. I haven't much time in this place.

I see you fight for your ore. I believe that is the most noble way to obtain your stone. It gives the land a fighting chance.

Still, one mustn't be callous with their own life. Dig too deep, and the land will overcome you. No stone is worth the price I paid.

But that is a tale for another day...

passages.title: Rethu's Sacrifice
passages.text:
The spirit of Rethu Ironhorn? Tell me everything he said.

He said he... dug too deep? I see. The Earthmother took him.

Thank you for coming to me, miner. This is a tale that the rest of the tribe must hear. We are all the wiser for it.

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This is one nasty-looking stone.

Your trainer in Dalaran should see this.

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text: You bring me somethin' new?

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This is no natural stone, miner. It stinks of demon's blood. Where'd you find this?

Reminds me a bit of old fel iron. Come 'ere, lemme teach you a trick or two on how to properly gather this stuff.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text:
This ore is remarkably heavy. More disturbingly, it seems to darken and hiss at your touch.

Perhaps your mining trainer in Dalaran has some insights.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text: Looks like you've been busy down there, miner.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text: This came out of a cliffside seam? Remember, ye can't mine seams like ye mine deposits. Totally different thing. I'll show ye my trick.

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text:
Your miner's instinct is kicking in. Chunks of the infernal's corpse appear to be usable.

Still, there must be a way to extract more ore from the demon's body. Perhaps your mining trainer in Dalaran will know how.

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text: What's that?

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text:
This came from a blasted infernal? Look out, we've got mister COMBAT miner, here!

Some o' this ore seems to 'ave lost its shine on the trip back, however. Next time, make sure to cut out the sword and spell wounds before ye mine it.

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text:
To mine for felslate is to seek the very blood of demons. To improve at it, you must become part demon yourself.

Why the dirty look? You said it yourself: you're willing to make sacrifices.

Luckily for you, I'm an expert in this area. I won't put you in any danger, as long as you trust me.

Are you ready?

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text: Don't waste my time, miner.

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text:
It is done.

Stretch it out a bit.

You may experience some stray urges to burn worlds and sow chaos for the next week or so. Do your best to resist them.

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text:
Oddly enveloped within the felslate deposit is a humanoid eye.

It quivers with life. You get the sense that it would blink at you if it had an eyelid.

A mining expert should take a look at this.

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text: Is... is that...?

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text:
It is. This eye once belonged to my sister, Rin'thissa.

Poor fool, she cut out her own eye and replaced it with a hunk of ore. That was the tipping point... she's completely fel-maddened now.

Learn from her mistake, <name>.

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text:
You blink and rub your eyes, but they do not deceive you. This is a woman's arm, completely enveloped within a felslate seam.

The arm is bloodless, but still twitches. Fel-colored streaks remain where veins once were.

Felsmith Nal'ryssa will certainly want to see this.

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text: Lyrelle, no...

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text:
This was my sister's. Lyrelle's.

Her fate is clear now. She no longer needed that signet ring... the girl must have traded in her own mining arm for one carved out of felslate itself.

Aren't you glad we only used three small shards?

Take this to heart, <name>: you can lose everything to greed if you don't exercise restraint. Poor Lyrelle paid that price for all of us.

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text:
What at first looked like another chunk of felslate is, in fact, a humanoid heart, encrusted in rock and filled not with blood but a vile, demonic substance.

It does not appear to belong to the beast you carved it out of... it seems that the infernal was holding it like a keepsake. Luckily your mining pick didn't hit it straight on.

Felsmith Nal'ryssa will want to see this.

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text: Ondri...

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text:
My sister Ondri was the first among us to mine, and the first among us to fall. Some Nathrezim dreadlord convinced her to replace her own heart - her heart! - with a chunk of felslate.

I slew the dreadlord myself, but couldn't find the heart. This must be it.

Big sister... I am sorry. Your loss will not be forgotten. We will learn from your missteps.

passages.title: Rin'thissa
passages.text:
My sister Nal'ryssa has her claws in you, doesn't she?

That weakling doesn't know the first thing about mining. She was always too afraid to take the leap. True knowledge comes only from the Great One, the God of Fel and Flame.

You want to truly learn how to mine? Come to Suramar's northwestern corner, and speak my name:

Rin'thissa.

passages.title: Rin'thissa
passages.text:
My sister's soul rests now. I have you to thank for that.

Rin'thissa was always a charmer. You did well to avoid her invitations, and even better to slay her and end her demonic possession. You've learned much since we first met, <name>.

passages.title: Lyrelle
passages.text:
Look at you, miner. Still held back by the limitations of your fragile, decaying flesh.

To truly become one with the demon-tinged rocks of these lands, you must shed your skin and submit to a darker power.

Join us, miner. Bring your feeble body to Felsoul Hold, and speak my name:

Lyrelle.

passages.title: Lyrelle
passages.text:
Poor Lyrelle.

I do not blame you for putting her down, <name>. I thank you. I hope that you would do the same to me, if I were to slip and fall down that same path.

Just... try to learn something from your ordeal. Reflect on your experience. I would hate to see her sacrifice be for nothing.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text:
You are nothing compared to me. You think yourself hardened, experienced... heroic, even. Hah!

You have no idea what I've been through. The tortures I've endured, the sacrifices I've made. All for the sake of my trade!

Yes, I'm a miner, just like you. Want to learn what I have to teach? Come to the Crimson Thicket in Suramar, and speak my name:

Ondri.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text: Ondri has always heartless, one way or the other.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text:
My sister's villainy is finally at an end.

She was always the wisest among us. Sad that she had to go out the way she did. I'm certain there was much she could have taught us.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text:
This ore. Smells. Horrible. It combines the odor of sulfur with all the worst parts of a rotting corpse.

Someone will probably want it for something.

Maybe your mining trainer in Dalaran will take it off of your hands.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text: Excuse me, I must have... wait, that smell is coming from YOU?

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text:
This odiferous morsel ye've brought me... it's infernal brimstone, isn't it?

Amazing.

I've heard tales, but I've never actually SEEN the stuff before.

I've got to study this. In the meantime, here's all I know about this rare, rare ore.

passages.title: Bjornharta
passages.text:
The afterlife leaves the dead hungry for the delicacies of their former lives. For the vrykul kings, none such offering is prized more than Bjornharta - a celebratory feast of an engorged bear heart. 

The bears of the Runewood eat well, and have long been prized for their tender meat. Hunt them and find a suitable heart of offer to the ancient rulers. They will not be able to resist such an offering.

passages.title: Bjornharta
passages.text: How went the hunt, outsider?

passages.title: Bjornharta
passages.text:
These hearts are fat and bloody. 

The slumbering rulers will not refuse an offering of Bjornharta.

passages.title: The Dreaming Fungus
passages.text:
So an outsider would seek to be judged by the ancient rulers of the vrykul? Curious, this. Know that they will not take to your presence kindly, stranger.

If you are so hasty to meet judgment, you can call them forth with a ritual of wakening. To complete this ritual, you will require an aromatic to burn and an offering to present.

A plant grows in the Runewood that will make a suitable incense. Gather it, and I will instruct you further.

passages.title: The Dreaming Fungus
passages.text: What do you bring?

passages.title: The Dreaming Fungus
passages.text:
Yes, these Soulcaps should be adequate for your ritual. 

Speak with me once you are ready to proceed and I will guide you further.

passages.title: Judgment Day
passages.text:
You have proven resourceful thus far, stranger. As promised, I will instruct you on the ritual of wakening.

First, you must place the offering directly atop the grave of the ruler you wish to awaken. Burn the incense so that its aroma wafts over the grave. If your offering is adequate, the ruler will rise, and you may ask your judgment.

Take care, outsider. The dead vrykul kings will not enjoy being awakened from their slumber.

passages.title: Judgment Day
passages.text:
Ashildir's grave has been disturbed, outsider. 

Do you know something of this?

passages.title: Waking the Shieldmaiden
passages.text:
With the rituals disrupted and her bones returned, we may be able to wrest Ashildir from the grasp of these Bonespeakers.

Deeper within Haustvald, the mystics possess a special altar that can reunite the body and spirit of a fallen warrior. With this, we may be able to return Ashildir's spirit into her bones, and out of the grasp of these foul mystics.

Go outsider, I will rally her guard.

passages.title: Waking the Shieldmaiden
passages.text:
Where... where am I now? 

I... know you...

passages.title: Breaking the Bonespeakers
passages.text:
The crimes of these ritualists must not go unpunished, but we cannot be their executioners. The rune magic they practice grants them untold power over the dead.

You, however, are not dead, and I can sense great power from you. Take the fight to these heretics, and show Ashildir that you are truly worthy of her judgment!

passages.title: Breaking the Bonespeakers
passages.text: Your glorious battle honors the Valkyra queen.

passages.title: Regal Remains
passages.text:
So you seek the judgment of the queen of the Valkyra? This must be your fault!

The Bonespeakers of Haustvald have committed an atrocity and stolen Ashildir's bones. They must have done this to keep an outsider from completing the trials. You must not let this stand!

Enter Haustvald and retrieve her remains. I hope, for your sake, that Ashildir is in a forgiving mood.

passages.title: Regal Remains
passages.text: Were you able to recover her remains?

passages.title: Regal Remains
passages.text:
The treachery of the Bonespeakers knows no limit. 

Their rituals seek to sunder the very essence of our queen, but we will use their own magic to return her to us!

passages.title: The Final Judgment
passages.text:
In my fragmented state, I captured glimpses of a hero meting out justice to the corrupted mystics of Haustvald. I see now, this hero was you, <class>. 

I know you seek my judgment, but my spirit is still fragmented. As we speak, Runeseer Faljar is calling upon dark, forbidden magics in an attempt to banish my spirit to Helheim. If he succeeds, your trial will be lost.

My connection here is fading. Go, there is little time!

passages.title: The Final Judgment
passages.text:
I cannot believe this fate... 

I am sorry, outsider, for I had underestimated Faljar's power.

That he could banish us here... is unthinkable.

passages.title: Your Will Be Done
passages.text:
Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker has drawn a rough map of what we know of the Broken Isles.

You should speak with him at once - he can best advise you on where we should first strike against the Legion.

passages.title: The Art of Demonsteel
passages.text:
The Firmament Stone is one of the few anvils beneath the sky that can tolerate the hammer strikes necessary to craft demonsteel.

Here, I will show you.

Two parts leystone, one part felslate. No heat, no tempering, just pure strength and finesse.

Try it. I will coach you.

passages.title: The Art of Demonsteel
passages.text:
There you have it... demonsteel.

Welcome to the next level of smithing, <name>.

passages.title: Into the Fray
passages.text:
The Burning Legion has beaten us here, but so too have the Illidari. It looks like the demon hunters are holding their own, but just barely.

Come, let's put that weapon of yours to use. I'll figure out our next move while you crush the Legion.

passages.title: Into the Fray
passages.text:
The two of you are a welcome sight. We pushed the demons out of these ruins, but they are stronger than any we have encountered before.

Your help is appreciated. If we do not crush this Legion invasion now, they will overrun Azsuna and then the rest of the Broken Isles.

passages.title: Done with Waiting
passages.text:
Mom got a message and said blood called for blood. She told me to wait here while she went out, but it's been two weeks since then. I'm tired of waiting.

I'll stay home if you go find her. She said she was going to the cliffs far to the south.

passages.title: Fishy Business
passages.text:
Makrura are massing down by the shore, and far too many of them seem to practice water magic.

I think once they've got enough spellcasters, they're planning to summon a massive wave.

passages.title: Die, Fish-People
passages.text:
Makrura are massing down by the shore, and far too many of them seem to practice water magic. I think they're planning to summon a massive wave.

Also, I've come a long way, and I'm out of supplies. I'm so hungry, I could eat almost anything. Even the makrura you kill. Just cut the heads off first.

passages.title: Holy Retribution
passages.text:
I fell in what you now call Tirisfal Glades at the claws of two of Yogg'Saron's most powerful lieutenants... the C'Thraxi. I was able to slay one in my death throes - Az'jtal.

Now, the dark forces deep beneath Azeroth have begun to usher Az'jtal once again into this world. You must go to Tyr's Fall and strike Az'jtal down again before it can fully manifest.

Only once this deed is done may you receive my blessing upon the Ashbringer.

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
Throm'ka, <class>. My name is Seska. I represent a... trading company. As you can see, I've fallen victim to these giants and their naga allies.

Three of my associates were also captured while surveying this cove. I'm certain that my employer, Mr. Shackle, would be most grateful if you could procure their release.

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
You say your name is <name>? Welcome to our humble den. Seska is very grateful for her freedom.

You haven't perchance seen the rest of my people?

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
Excellent, my good sir. I cannot thank you enough for the freedom of my people. Rosh is especially appreciative.

<Gentle Rosh grunts.>

Perhaps you and I can do some more business together.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text:
Why the Thistleleaf are collecting the Lunarwing eggs is anyone's guess, but you can be sure it's not to give them a loving home.

Saylanna Riverbreeze will know what to do with these.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text: Gather as many eggs as you can and bring them back to me. I will keep them safe.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text: Until I can discover what is vexing the Thistleleaf, I'll have to look after the Lunarwing eggs. At least I know they will be safe.

passages.title: Inspiration Strikes
passages.text:
The blood of this creature glows with magical energy. It doesn't SEEM to be poisonous.

Your training in the culinary arts has presented you with some strange ingredients before, but this one is particularly inspiring. Perhaps someone within the Azurewing Repose can suggest a preparation for Leyblood.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Bidding
passages.text:
Uh, are these guys friendlies? I guess it's a good sign they haven't tried to eat Duchess... yet.

Anyway, I have orders. Nathanos caught up with the dark rangers, who were sent forward aboard the Oblivion on a secret mission from Lady Sylvanas herself! Unfortunately the Alliance caught wind of our plan, and now Greymane is attacking the outpost!

We could really use you over there, <name>. Duchess can take you there, just give me the word.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Bidding
passages.text:
Finally someone competent arrives at this sorry excuse for an outpost. 

Our efforts to complete Sylvanas's mission are at a standstill, but now we have even more pressing matters on our hands.

passages.title: Clear the Deck!
passages.text:
Our mission in Skold-Ashil will have to wait, <class> - for now, we have more pressing matters to attend to.

I had just recently arrived with reinforcements for our assault when Greymane's ship sailed in and began barraging our walls. We deployed our siege weapons, but their ground forces quickly overwhelmed us.

If you can get to those catapults and take out the dogs manning the cannons, it may give us the window we need to push the attack!

passages.title: Clear the Deck!
passages.text: Hah! Greymane will find his cannons aren't so useful when the blight takes his crew!

passages.title: Shielded Secrets
passages.text:
Our goal lies within that vault, <class>. I don't have time to explain in detail - just know that it is vital to the Forsaken that we succeed.

The shieldmaidens have proven tenacious in their defense, but I believe there may be another way in. A chosen few of their order are allowed entrance, and I need you to find out how.

In the town I have seen intricately engraved shields which I believe are passed down from these champions. The scenes they depict may be the key to passing into the vault.

passages.title: Shielded Secrets
passages.text:
I would hope that you bring me some good news, <class>. 

For both of our sake.

passages.title: A New Life for Undeath
passages.text:
It seems that you are full of surprises, <name>. With the blessing of the Valkyra queen, you have opened a path that will shape the destiny of Azeroth.

I invite you to bear witness, for today a new day dawns on the Forsaken!

passages.title: A New Life for Undeath
passages.text:
It looks like we underestimated Greymane's tenacity - a mistake that cost the Forsaken dearly. 

This Eyir cannot hide for long, however. If I must I will hunt her through the Halls of Valor! 

Go now, <class>. I will call upon you when you are needed.

passages.title: The Highmountain Tauren
passages.text:
Ye've brought me a bit of interesting rocks to look at, <name>. I've got a special assignment for ye, if ye're up for it.

I hear stories about these tauren, up in Highmountain, who claim mastery over minin'. I don't know if they're as talented as you or me, but they've been minin' leystone longer.

Pay 'em a visit. See what they have to say.

passages.title: The Highmountain Tauren
passages.text: You are indeed a miner. You have the look of it. There is ore in your blood.

passages.title: Not Dead Yet!
passages.text: They're not dead yet! A little nitro here, a jolt of electricity there... we can bring 'em back! And then, they can pay me! Whaddya say, <name>? Wanna go into business with me?

passages.title: Scouting Report
passages.text:
We were supposed to meet back here, and then sneak back to Gatgetzan. That was hours ago, <name>! The others fanned out across all of Tanaris to gather intel.

Anything you can find will help in the defense of Gadgetzan. Keep your eyes open, <name>!

passages.title: The Felsmiths
passages.text:
Ye have a knack with this felslate, <lad/lass>. Best ship ye off to someone who knows the stuff better than I.

The Illidari have a knack with all things demonic, really, and I've heard about a few miners who've set up shop out near the demons in Suramar.

Pay 'em a visit. See what they have to teach ye.

passages.title: The Felsmiths
passages.text:
You want to mine felslate?

Do you really think you have what it takes?

Are you willing to make sacrifices?

Good.

passages.title: To the Rescue
Keepers of the Hammer
passages.text:
The Highmountain Tribes had intended to pledge our allegiance to your forces. We know war has come with the Burning Legion.

However, we have been betrayed from within and must now ask for your aid.

A great relic, the Hammer of Khaz'goroth, was stolen from our people by the vile drogbar.

We need your help in recovering it.

passages.title: Keepers of the Hammer
passages.text: We must be swift. I was overlong in finding you.

passages.title: Keepers of the Hammer
passages.text: I know you seek the Pillar of Creation but I am sad to say it was one of many things we lost today.

passages.title: Get to High Ground
passages.text:
It is no accident that Dargrul attacked the Rivermane in force. It is their farms and their pastures that supply food for the region.

Please, get Jale to Thunder Totem. With luck, Mayla will have reinforcements to send to the area.

We will rally the survivors here and follow as quickly as we can.

passages.title: Get to High Ground
passages.text: Have you had any luck with the Rivermane?

passages.title: Get to High Ground
passages.text:
Riverbend was... destroyed? That disgusting beast Dargrul! I will not stop until I see him dead.

But we cannot do that with the army we have.

We need help from the other tribes.

passages.title: Rocs vs Eagles
passages.text:
High Crawliac has taught her witches how to curse our beloved eagles into the vile rocs you see assaulting the valley.

There is no way to break this curse once it has taken hold.

We will take to the skies and do battle with the rocs, but we need your help on the ground.

Head north through Darkfeather Valley and release any eagles that you find.

Every eagle you save is one less roc we must kill later.

passages.title: Rocs vs Eagles
passages.text:
Your bravery has returned to us some of our fine feathered friends. Well done.

Now how do you feel about a frontal assault?

passages.title: The Rivermane Tribe
passages.text:
What has happened here requires more time than I have to explain. In short, our tribes have scattered in the wake of the attack that left the Hammer of Khaz'goroth in the hands of the barbaric drogbar.

Even now the drogbar are raiding the Rivermane tribe, and I have too few braves left to send to their aid. 

We need a hero. Please, go to Earthmother's Bounty and lend what aid you can.

passages.title: The Rivermane Tribe
passages.text:
Mayla was still able to send help? I could hug that child.

Welcome, outsider. I am Jale Rivermane, Chieftain of the Rivermane tribe. And we could really use your help.

passages.title: The Bloodtotem Tribe
passages.text:
The Bloodtotem are led by Torok, a volatile but useful tauren chieftain. He is wary of outsiders, but I believe you have already met an emissary to their tribe--Oakin Ironbull--whom you rescued at Riverbend.

Use that small thread and you may be able to bring the Bloodtotem back into the fold. Highmountain needs them if we are to defeat the drogbar and reclaim the Hammer of Khaz'goroth. Be on your guard, <name>.

passages.title: The Bloodtotem Tribe
passages.text: Outsider, you are one of few from beyond Highmountain who has made it into these woods alive. With me vouching for you, the Bloodtotem have been given a no-kill order by Torok.

passages.title: The Skyhorn Tribe
passages.text:
The Skyhorn people are some of the greatest pathfinders and hunters this world has ever known.

They are a proud people, but should be willing to listen to reason.

If the roads feel unsafe, you may ask any flight master in Highmountain to fly you there.

Please, adventurer, go to their leader Lasan and remind him that only together, we are Highmountain.

passages.title: The Skyhorn Tribe
passages.text: Ha ha! And what are you, tiny creature? Have you come to battle us or join us in battle?

passages.title: Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text:
Now that you are familiar with our greatest hero, perhaps you are willing to assist me on a very dangerous endeavor.

To this end I have sent word for one of your allies to join us.

When you are ready, join us in my spirit lodge. It is up the elevators and across the southwestern most bridge.

passages.title: Battle of Snowblind Mesa
passages.text:
Your timing is fortunate. Our forces at Snowblind Mesa report seeing the Underking above ground.

What is more, he is lightly guarded, and has the hammer with him. Thanks to your efforts, we can meet them in battle.

Meet us at Snowblind Mesa and let us take the fight to Dargrul together.

passages.title: Battle of Snowblind Mesa
passages.text: That... is a lot of drogbar.

passages.title: Littlefur
passages.text:
Stranger, I beseech you! My once peaceful brethren are now cursed with insatiable wrath.

My nephew and I tried to leave against the Chieftain's wishes. The clan wrested him from me, and would have torn me apart if I did not flee.

He is trapped in the village, and I fear the worst.

Great <class>, please save him. I am too old and too weak to do it myself.

passages.title: Littlefur
passages.text: Uncle?

passages.title: Logistical Matters
passages.text:
I think we are ready to... reintroduce ourselves to the Legion on the Broken Isles.

Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker has volunteered to help coordinate our forces on the ground. You should speak with him immediately, Highlord.

passages.title: Logistical Matters
passages.text: Now is the time to strike back against the Legion.

passages.title: Unused - Wraith Zapper
Unbearable
passages.text:
Not far away, a bear cub looks to be in some distress. Perhaps you should investigate?

passages.title: Assault on Skold-Ashil
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: Consult the Locals
passages.text:
Whoever wove this fabric CAN'T have intended it only for belts and shoulderpads. There must be some way to sew thread into this material.

Head on down to Azsuna and try to find a tailor. We need to sew if we're going to do any real tailoring.

passages.title: Consult the Locals
passages.text:
My my, look at you! Such an attractive young <class>, and all bedecked in magical finery and weaponry. To what do I owe the pleasure?

Aha! Tailoring! It's your lucky day, er...

I'm sorry, what was your name? <name>?

It's your lucky day, <name>! I happen to be one of the best tailors in Suramar...

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text:
Let me guess... thread troubles? Mm-hm.
I suspected as much. My people weave sumptuous silks, but those silks can be fickle about the types of thread they'll accept.

Shal'dorei silk has a bit of ley energy woven right into it. You need something that's learned to coexist with the ley energies of this land.

I'm talking about owlcats, my good friend! They have what you need. You'll find them amongst the ruins of Llothien.

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text: They are quite remarkable creatures, really. I used to keep one as a pet and mount... but that was a lifetime ago.

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text: Perfect. Marvelous!

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text:
When I worked at the tailoring guild in Suramar, I would usually work off of a pattern. Something that inspired me.

Unfortunately, I've run into streak of bad luck, and I'm ashamed to say that I no longer have my patterns.

The naga sorceresses in the lagoon to the west, however, have expertly-sewn wristwraps. And the nightfallen to the north wear robes that we can use... if you can pry one from their greedy clutches.

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text: What've you got in your hands, there?

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text: You, <name>, are a person of great skill. I send you out for patterns, and you do so without question. Remarkable!

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text:
Might I ask a favor, <name>?

As I am recently without a home, shop, family, or friends, I was wondering if you might show me your floating city? I must admit, I am VERY curious about the place. I've also heard good things about their tailoring shop.

I have no way of getting there myself, but certainly such a magical city has SOMEONE who can summon me.

<Lyndras looks at you with hopeful apprehension.>

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text: Did you find a tailor yet?

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text:
Your friend certainly has an... interesting appearance.

He taught you to sew this silk? Hmm. Maybe we should keep him around for a while.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras?
passages.text:
That's strange. Lyndras was here one moment, and then he ran off the next. He had such a strange look on his face.

Perhaps we should track him down.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras?
passages.text:
Sorry about that, <name>. You caught me snooping around. I suppose my curiosity got the better of me.

Allow me to make it up to you.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Again?
passages.text:
Oh dear.

He had just promised you that he wouldn't wander off, and then he did it again!

I'm starting to think that this Lyndras character might be a bit too impetuous for my tastes.

Please, go find him, before he gets into any more trouble.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Again?
passages.text:
My most sincere apologies, <name>. Not only did I make a spectacle of myself, I fear I may have also put the good name of your tailoring shop at risk.

You have every right to be upset with me.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text:
I wish I had more patterns to share, but my notebook was lost along with my shop. We'll need to come up with some patterns on our own.

I've been thinking about the leather breeches that the Stormheim vrykul wear. They're certainly much thicker and heavier than anything we could sew, but their embellishing runework is quite impressive.

If I had a few pairs, perhaps I could re-imagine this runework on a more... refined garment.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text: I'm looking forward to this.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text:
Aha! This will be much simpler than I'd first thought.

<Lyndras takes a moment to jot some instructions down on a scrap of vellum.>

Here, <name>. You should have it.

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text:
Your assistance, <name>, if you have a moment.

I've been attempting to reproduce a pattern for footwear that I spotted a while back, but I'm having trouble getting the right color for my dye. Our black dye is too dark, our blue dye is too bright, and mixing the two doesn't look right.

The color I'm looking for is more of a squid-ink blue. If, in your travels, you come across any dyes of this color, would you do me the favor of bringing some to me?

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text: I'm quite close to completing these slippers.

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text: Marvelous!

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Now?
passages.text:
Lyndras couldn't have gone very far. I mean, we're floating a thousand feet over the sea. 

I heard some commotion across the way this morning near the alchemy shop. I pray that wasn't Lyndras.

Could you please go over there and make sure?

passages.title: The Nightborne Connection
passages.text:
Now that you're able to disguise yourself, you should go to Suramar City and try to find this guild of tailors.

Good luck, <name>, and try not to get caught.

passages.title: The Nightborne Connection
passages.text:
Ah, a fellow tailor. Pleasure to make your acquaintance, uh... <name>, was it?

I trust you'd like to come into the fold of our guild? Where did you receive your prior training?

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text:
<Tytallo listens as you recount what happened with Lyndras.>

I see. You sound almost... sympathetic to the wretch.

The nightfallen are liars and thieves. ALL of them. Lyndras included.

I will not tolerate a student that has any respect or sympathy for those... things. And have you witnessed what they turn into at the depths of their depravity?

If you want to get on my good side, do not return until you are covered in the blood of the withered.

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text: If you wish to earn my tutelage, you must first prove that you are on our side.

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text:
Hmm.

Very well. We may continue.

passages.title: TRACKING Encounter Botanist
passages.text:
(PH)
Darkgrove has run out of places to hide. Now it is time to finish him off.

If we stop him now, there may be hope for this valley yet.

passages.title: Black Rook Invasion
passages.text:
Once, this area was peaceful and prosperous. Then we saw the first bad omens: strange ailments, spoiled crops, and the like. Now ghosts attack us from that castle across the river, and undead assassins slay our fishers so as to cut off the village's food supply.

We're the last family living this close to the castle, but we daren't retreat: this river is the best route for fishers to bring their hauls in to town. Please, will you take the fight to these undead?

passages.title: Rise to the Occasion
passages.text:
The Lich King made a wise choice in giving you that weapon, <name>.

You've proven your strength and cunning on countless occasions and it is time that you have a position fitting for your accomplishments.

passages.title: Grasp of the Underking
passages.text:
If we have one good fortune in this it is that Dargrul has no knowledge of how to use the hammer.

He keeps thinking of the hammer as a weapon instead of a tool of creation.

Even so, he has imprisoned our tribesman in fists of stone summoned from the earth. Our weapons have proven useless against this magic.

You might have power enough to break these fists. Can you help?

passages.title: Grasp of the Underking
passages.text: How are the captives? Did you find them alive?

passages.title: Grasp of the Underking
passages.text:
It has been an age or more since the drogbar last walked the surface in such numbers.

They became the dark stories we tell children.

passages.title: The Drogbar
passages.text:
It wasn't enough for Dargrul to just destroy this village. He has also sent his Stoneraiders to take what is left.

Please champion, prove to my people that you are the hero I foresaw.

Slay enough of these Stoneraiders that it breaks their resolve.

passages.title: The Drogbar
passages.text: The drogbar were supposed to be our allies against the Burning Legion.

passages.title: The Drogbar
passages.text: Your battle skills are impressive.

passages.title: Dargrul and the Hammer
passages.text:
We are about to follow a drogbar into a cave, something we warn our children never to do.

Even so, several of our warbraves have already followed Dargrul inside.

Come, join us in battle and let us reclaim the Hammer of Khaz'goroth.

passages.title: Dargrul and the Hammer
passages.text: This is a hard day.

passages.title: Dargrul and the Hammer
passages.text:
Oro and the others? Did they make it out as well?

Such destruction. So many good warbraves have fallen today.

It is clear now, we will need the full might of the Highmountain tribes if we are to recover the hammer.

passages.title: REUSE ME
passages.text: asdf

passages.title: A Summons from Saylanna
passages.text:
Sprites have always been mischievous creatures, but lately their mischief has turned to violence.

One of the druids I call friend, Saylanna Riverbreeze, reports that they are assaulting the faerie dragon nesting grounds.

The Lunarwing Shallows lie to the south. You will find Saylanna there.

passages.title: Bitestone Enclave
passages.text:
This is an old drogbar enclave that we used to trade with. Now it is a base of operations for their raids.

I need more time to gather what is left of our warbraves. Go, enter the enclave, and slay any you find in there.

Buy us the time we need to gather our strength.

passages.title: Bitestone Enclave
passages.text: Highmountain stands!

passages.title: Bitestone Enclave
passages.text: Thank you for clearing us a path. We should have a straight shot at Dargrul now.

passages.title: Call of the Illidari
passages.text:
<name>, Altruis requests that you meet him at Krasus' Landing at once.

<Kor'vas leans in close, her voice an urgent whisper.>

You must hurry. The Legion has eyes everywhere.

passages.title: Call of the Illidari
passages.text: We need to move quickly. With every moment we sit here, the Legion's hold strengthens.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text:
This demon has proved less than useful. I have been using the Scythe of Souls on it, but so far, it has resisted my inquiries. We will see how long that lasts.

I have a different idea...

There is a fresh inquisitor demon ahead. They are horrific fel casters who see through their floating eyes and specialize in dark pacts. If you steal its power, Jace Darkweaver could use some of it in his ritual to spy on the Legion.

Better yet, you will gain its power by ripping it from its smoking corpse.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text: <name>. I would salute, but I am in the middle of a ritual.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text:
An inquisitor's essence... perfect. Allari was right.

Now to complete my ritual and spy on the Legion's leadership.

passages.title: To Catch a Banshee
passages.text:
The strange-talking vrykul said I might be able to meet you here. I have orders from Greymane. It seems he may have a lead on Sylvanas' location.

He's set up a camp near the base of the mountain. We've run into some troubles, though. It looks like the Horde may have homed in on our position.

We could use your help. You can take my gryphon. Just speak to me when you're ready to leave.

passages.title: To Catch a Banshee
passages.text: It is good you arrived when you did, <name>.

passages.title: Combustible Contagion
passages.text:
It is true that we may have a lead on Sylvanas. Though I want nothing more than to get my hands on the Banshee Queen, the situation here at Greywatch requires immediate attention.

Yesterday, a regiment of guards returned with word of Forsaken forces in the woods. Several of them bore signs of a blight, similar to the one we endured in Gilneas. It would appear these Forsaken seek to unleash this blight upon Greywatch.

Seek out their caches and destroy them, before the blight overtakes us!

passages.title: Combustible Contagion
passages.text: Have the caches been taken care of?

passages.title: Combustible Contagion
passages.text:
The deed is done. 

You have done a great service to the worgen of Greywatch, <name>.

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
We have her now! According to these reports, Sylvanas' forces are after something in Skold-Ashil - a vrykul town not far from here. We must make our way there and track her down.

I had previously dispatched Commander Lorna Crowley and a detachment of Gilneas Brigade to scout the position. Meet up with her there and find out what Sylvanas is after.

Meanwhile, I will muster the fleet to assault their outpost. We will have justice if I have to reduce their camp to rubble!

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
So the cavalry has arrived? 

Good, we must make haste if we wish to uncover Sylvanas' plot before it comes to bear.

passages.title: Shielded Secrets
passages.text:
It's obvious at this point that the Horde wants something in Skold-Ashil. Unfortunately we still don't know what they're after.

We think the secret lies with the shieldmaidens here, so we need to find out more about them. Some early scouting revealed that they have a method of carving their shields to tell their stories. 

Go into the city and find as many of these shields as you can. With luck, we will find what Sylvanas seeks.

passages.title: Shielded Secrets
passages.text:
Val'kyr, you say? This is worse that I had imagined. If Sylvanas is able to create more Val'kyr, there will be no limit to her armies!

It seems the vault is her goal. We must stop her!

passages.title: [PH] Defeat the Dark Val'kyr
