I am unsure what she did, but Helya has weakened you somehow. I have seen similar effects on my shieldmaidens, and now they are trapped by Helya's minions.

I may know a way, however. The Kvaldir ships carry special lanterns bound to this place to navigate through the fog. It is said that the light of these lanterns can release bonds of the spirit.

There is a kvaldir ship nearby. See if you can find one there.

passages.title: To Light the Way
passages.text: Were you able to secure the lantern?

passages.title: To Light the Way
passages.text:
This appears to be what we need. 

Now, we can prepare for the battle ahead.

passages.title: Allies in Death
passages.text:
Our power alone may not be enough to fight the behemoth, Geir. Fortunately, Faljar was kind enough to send our allies into Helheim with us.

Earlier, I had discovered several of them being tortured by the elemental forces of Helheim. You may think the dead can't drown, but with Helya's power, this is not the case. 

I could not release them then, but now that you possess the waylight, you may be able to.

Seek them out and free them from an eternity of suffering!

passages.title: Allies in Death
passages.text: Once unbound, my Valkyra will throttle these wretched minions.

passages.title: Allies in Death
passages.text:
It is good to have my shieldmaidens returned to my side. 

You have gained allies today, but know you have also gained my gratitude.

passages.title: [PH] Collect Weapons
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: Victory is Eternal
passages.text:
There is no more cause for hesitation. Now is the time to strike.

We will defeat this foul behemoth and meet Helya's bargain. The path out of Helheim awaits, outsider. 

Prepare yourself.

passages.title: Victory is Eternal
passages.text: Together, we can defeat this foe!

passages.title: Victory is Eternal
passages.text:
The day is won. Now, we must collect our reward. 

Let us hope that Helya keeps her side of the bargain.

passages.title: Curse of the Sea
passages.text:
[PH] <You find a strange glowing orb inside the treasure chest. A commanding voice emits from the orb-- it is Odyn.> 

Very good, <name>, you've found my orb. The souls of vrykul champions are unrightfully being transported to Helheim. These champions deserve a place in Valhallas, not an eternity alongside that witch.

Use this cleansing orb on the cursed vrykul to free them. If the ship reaches the shores of Helheim before the curse is lifted, they will be doomed to serve an eternity as Helya's kvaldir.

passages.title: Paid in Lifeblood
passages.text:
We have fulfilled Helya's bargain. Now, we see if she will keep to her word.

When you are ready, we should proceed to the throne. If you have any other business here, I would suggest finishing it now.

I will follow your lead, outsider.

passages.title: Paid in Lifeblood
passages.text:
So the dead return from Helheim and back? An impressive feat. 

Your worth has been judged and the trial passed. 

Now, to your destiny. To the Halls of Valor!

passages.title: The Eternal Nemesis
passages.text:
<Helya's voice echoes in the sky above the altar>

You say that you do not belong here among the unworthy, outsider, but your spirit fragments so easily. How am I to know you speak the truth? 

I cannot, so you must show me.

Bring yourself to the eternal battlefield and face my champion. If you manage to defeat him, then I may grant you a pardon.

passages.title: The Eternal Nemesis
passages.text:
You do not look good. 

I take it Helya did not prove lenient?

passages.title: Rite of Blood
passages.text:
Oakin Ironbull vouches for you. He's capable, for a Rivermane. You also brought with you proof of your own strength, albeit rather inconclusive proof.

Before we allow you to move freely within our territory, you must complete the Rite of Blood, which you have already begun. If you succeed--and I doubt you will--talk to me.

Enter the depths of the cave. Defeat whatever foe appears and return to me.

passages.title: Rite of Blood
passages.text: Are you afraid of the dark?

passages.title: Rite of Blood
passages.text: Thank you for saving me. I hope now we can trust each other. We must if we are to defeat these Feltotem.

passages.title: The Siegebrul
passages.text:
Worms do not like battle or the surface. They only go where their master tells them.

So, when in war, kill the master.

Siegebrul Olgrul is the master of worms for the Mightstone drogbar who attack us from the north.

Slay him.

passages.title: The Siegebrul
passages.text: Siegbrul Olgrul torments all who serve him. There are evil drogbar, and then there is this foul monster.

passages.title: The Siegebrul
passages.text:
"Siegebrul." Bah!

Before this war we had no need for such titles.

Olgrul was always just a brute who takes pleasure in the pain of others.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text:
Nathanos Blightcaller, Champion of the Banshee Queen herself, sent for you in Dalaran.

He should be waiting for you in the Violet Citadel. It sounded urgent.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text:
<Nathanos glances over at you, pausing for a moment before acknowledging your presence.>

Yes?

passages.title: Toll for the Soul
passages.text:
[PH] As foretold, you have arrived... Helya is foolish to think I'll let her ferry me into Helheim. Odyn has already smiled upon me, my soul belongs in Valhallas. 

Make no mistake, I am not a prisoner. Before my death Odyn appeared to me in the form of a raven. He praised my battles in life and gave me a quest no vrykul could refuse. The Helerjar arrived... and I let them slay me.

Prisoner-- nay, I am a liberator, sent by Odyn to free the souls of Valarjar.

passages.title: I Have a Bad Feeling About This
passages.text:
You have no reason to trust me. My cousins led by Dargrul have gone mad with power.

But I ask you to investigate something. I have a feeling something terrible is about to befall Highmountain, and that Torok and his Bloodtotem are going to be responsible.

If you don't believe me, look for yourself at the northern side of Cliff's Edge.

passages.title: I Have a Bad Feeling About This
passages.text: <The cage is empty. Navarrogg is gone.>

passages.title: Helping the Hunters
passages.text:
Now, while I continue to fill the rest of our orders, I'd really appreciate it if you would deliver these vellums to Jace Darkweaver down in Azsuna.

He and the other demon hunters have been fighting back the Legion for quite some time and could use this as quickly as possible.

Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: Helping the Hunters
passages.text:
<Jace takes the crate from you and peers inside.>

The vellums! They're finally here.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text:
We could use your help down here, <name>. Some of our hunters would benefit greatly from having those vellums applied to their rings right now.

Here take a few. I'll give the rest to one of my other soldiers to hand out.

My hunters probably won't stop to let you apply the enchants, so you'll just have to do your enchanting even if they're in the midst of battle.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text: There's no time to waste. We need to get these enchantments out to as many of my hunters as possible.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text: That will certainly help us keep these demons at bay for much longer. We're in your debt, <name>.

passages.title: Thunder Struck
passages.text:
I've made contact with a potential source of new enchantments down in Highmountain. The tauren of Thunder Totem command the spirits to imbue items with great power.

Seek out an enchanter named Twaintail and see if he will share his knowledge with us.

Taurens are known for their sharing... right?

passages.title: Thunder Struck
passages.text:
The spirits told me of your coming, outlander. Let us see if you are indeed the hero this land needs.

<The tauren clears his throat.>

Pardon me. I know I come off as a bit dramatic. It's just... well, these things have meaning for me.

passages.title: Fey Enchantments
passages.text:
The new dusts and crystals we've found in these lands are fascinating, as I'm sure you've already surmised. I'm positive we can expand their usefulness to more of our armor.

I'd like you to go back out into the field and talk to a dryad in Val'sharah. Apparently she may be able to clue us into some enchantments for shoulder pieces.

Her name is Nalamya. You'll find her near the Temple of Elune.

passages.title: Fey Enchantments
passages.text:
What is it you want, <race>?

Oh, I see now. You're an enchanter.

I warn you though, if you take my enchantments like those foul elves of Black Rook and use them for evil, you shall feel my wrath one way or another.

passages.title: Led Astray
passages.text:
The night elves are no fools, but the elves of Black Rook follow their commanders with blind loyalty. I've no doubt that the blame for their apathy rests heavily upon their commanders.

I know of two of their leaders, who as we speak continue to command their troops to do nothing against the blight encroaching upon my home.

Go to Black Rook Hold and slay Trelan Shieldbreaker and Starlys Strongbow. Let them be an example for those who can help, but wish to remain cowardly.

passages.title: Led Astray
passages.text: Don't worry about proving what you've done for me. I have my own eyes and ears to tell me of your deeds.

passages.title: Cursed, But Convenient
passages.text:
I need you to return to Azsuna at once, <name>. I've only just heard of an enchantress within the Crumbled Palace who knows of many rare enchantments.

Go to her and see what you can learn at once.

passages.title: Cursed, But Convenient
passages.text:
Ah, a fellow enchanter. Come to earn the marks of my subordinates, have you?

If that's the case, then you may speak with my sentinel and druid. Earn their trust and they'll grant you their marks.

I, however, have a different task for you...

passages.title: An Enchanting Home
passages.text:
The more I learn about the Broken Isles, the more convinced I am that it is a land of wonders!

Ildine and I were just discussing rumors of a dwelling in Stormheim that was once the home to a vrykul enchantress called Tigrid. It is said the site is perfectly preserved, and her enchantments were so potent that they persist to this day!

Investigating the home might uncover valuable knowledge, <name>.

passages.title: An Enchanting Home
passages.text:
So, <race>, you have discovered my home... all that is left of me.

Not even enough to sustain my beloved enchantments...

passages.title: Ringing True
passages.text:
While your presence here would continue to be of value to us, your master in Dalaran has called for you.

I'd like to thank you again for all you've done for us. My hunters have been reminded that they're not alone in this war.

passages.title: Ringing True
passages.text:
<name>, you're back. Excellent work down in Azsuna. Jace gave you high praises for your help with his troops and against the Legion.

Before you go, I wanted to share with you the other new formulas we have for ring enchantments. It would do our side good in this war if you were to share these with your fellow adventurers.

passages.title: Elven Enchantments
passages.text:
You have earned the marks of my most trusted companions. You have also returned my love to me.

I am fortunate to have met you, <name>.

Now return to your master and let him know of what you have learned.

passages.title: Elven Enchantments
passages.text:
<You tell Nalthanis of your time with the cursed elves and the enchantments you learned.>

That's fascinating! You managed, through enchantments, to create a bond with those elves and now they may come to your aid?

Those are some truly powerful enchantments you were gifted, <name>. Don't let them go to waste.

passages.title: The Absent Priestess
passages.text:
After my betrayal, I never thought I could bear to look upon my love again. But thanks to you, <name>, I can at last return.

Go and speak to Enchantress Ilanya. I will let her know that you are worthy of my mark.

passages.title: The Absent Priestess
passages.text:
You have returned my love to me and for that I am forever grateful.

As she is with me now, she shall be at your beck and call should you need her. I grant to you her marks.

passages.title: On Azure Wings
passages.text:
I have some exciting news of my own to report, <name>. Ildine and I had an excursion to Azsuna and made contact with the blue dragons at the Azurewing Repose.

One of the dragons, Kharmeera, is an enchanter who expressed interest in working with you to perfect some of our enchantments.

I understand you were just down there working with the elves, but if you wouldn't mind returning, Kharmeera would enjoy working with you too.

passages.title: On Azure Wings
passages.text: I sense the power of enchantments about you, <name>. Yes, I think I will enjoy working with you!

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text:
We have the pigment, but we still require one more ingredient.

Visitors at the Legerdemain Lounge will often play card games, and occasionally their cards are discarded. Go see if you can find some loose cards that players may have gotten rid of between matches.

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text: The cards are just for reference, mostly...

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text:
And there we have it. Just as good as those witless Darkmoon cretins.

While we owe this success almost exclusively to my genius, I feel you ought to be rewarded for doing the legwork. Here's the recipe for my newest masterpiece.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text:
Have you seen those demon hunters yet? I'm not entirely sold on their allegiance to our cause, but while we have them, we may as well exploit them.

Everybody needs glyphs, you know.

Go see what you can discover about them. Azsuna is as good a place as any to start.

Perhaps my genius has worn off on you and you'll be able to create your own recipes based on what you learn.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text: Are you here to reinforce us, <class>? We could always use your strength.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text:
You wish to learn what it is to be a demon hunter? That may take some time.

The first thing you can do is fight alongside us. Battle the demons with us and observe how we use their strength against them.

Return to me when you are finished.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text: Have you seen enough?

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text: Some may condemn our methods. We simply do what we must to destroy the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Inscription of the Body
passages.text:
We demon hunters must keep our darkness at bay, lest we succumb to it and become demons ourselves. That is the purpose of marking our skin the way we do.

Up to the north, a demon hunter by the name of Baric Stormrunner is preparing to strengthen his markings. Go to him and learn how we keep our demons at bay.

passages.title: Inscription of the Body
passages.text:
Allari sent you? I am about to start a ritual. I could use you, stranger.

You seem more ally than enemy. In this time, allies are more important than ever.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
Now that we have all the essential pieces, let's begin the ritual.

I'll instruct you on how to help me. It is pivotal that you follow my instructions when I give them, or the ritual will fail.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
It is done. I fear that if I had waited any longer to improve my wards, the demon in me may have taken over.

Thank you again, <name>.

passages.title: Scribal Knowledge
passages.text:
We do not simply fight the demons, <name>. We observe them.

One of my best demon hunters, Zaria Shadowheart, is currently gathering intel on the demons in Felblaze Ingress.

Go to her. She will teach you what she has learned from the demons invading that region.

passages.title: Scribal Knowledge
passages.text: Allari has sent you to learn from me? In that case, I have much to tell.

passages.title: Runes of Power
passages.text:
Look closely, scribe, and you may learn. As the demons spread out over a region, the more clever ones will inscribe runes upon the ground. The fel taint pervades this entire hillside, but the corruption is darkest around these runes, disallowing anything pure to grow ever again.

Study these runes.

passages.title: Runes of Power
passages.text:
As I'm sure you sensed, these runes hold quite a bit of energy.

Greater knowledge of the Legion is your best weapon against it.

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
We demon hunters ritualistically remove our eyes in order to see the demons more clearly.

Down below, a demon commander walks amongst his troops, unseen by normal eyes. He keeps the chaos in order, as we must keep our chaos in check.

Destroy his warding crystal, then slay him.

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
I commend you, scribe. You would make an excellent demon hunter.

Take this ink as payment for your efforts. I have no need of it.

passages.title: Aethrem Crystal
passages.text:
<Most aethril has a sharp crystalline fiber in the center of the bloom, but this one is particularly well-developed.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Aethrem Crystal
passages.text:
A crystal... inside the flower? That gives me an idea.

I dabbled in jewelcrafting in my younger years. Take a look at this technique...

passages.title: The Burdens of Hunting
passages.text: There is nothing more I have to teach you, scribe. The Illidari stand behind you in the battle against the Legion.

passages.title: The Burdens of Hunting
passages.text:
<Professor Pallin looks over the demon hunter glyphs you've designed.>

Huh! Apparently I don't have to hold your hand as much as I thought.

Look at this glyph you've made right here. If you flip this symbol around, and adjust the stroke width here...

passages.title: Mysterious Messages
passages.text:
The woman at the archaeology shop just dropped off some tablets to be deciphered. Any fool can see they're written in ancient vrykul, but I lent my codex to one of my students, so I'm unable to decipher them here.

His name is Nicholo Swiftfuse, and he is in Stormheim. Let him know that if he fails to decipher them, his apprenticeship shall be terminated.

That is all.

passages.title: Mysterious Messages
passages.text:
Seriously? Pallin wants me to do what now?!

That old bag of wind thinks he's so great, but he's always making me do all his work. It's a surprise I'm not running that shop.

But fine, I'll help you. As long as you help me too.

passages.title: Not So Complex?
passages.text:
Alright, I believe I've finished adding the missing entries into the codex. And we have the machete... err, knife.

All that's left is to make our own tablet and verify my other suspicion about these tablets:

I believe that they're not just simple texts, but a sort of magical device.

passages.title: Not So Complex?
passages.text:
It was a good thing you were here to help me with that.

I surely would have been killed by those spirits!

passages.title: The Ink Flows
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to make a quick delivery for me.

Yes, I've learned by now that such trivial tasks are beneath your skills... but I'm rather busy right now and we both know my time is much more important than yours.

Deliver these contracts to Raethan, the Guard Captain in Dalaran's Underbelly.

passages.title: The Ink Flows
passages.text:
These all seem to be in order.

If you have a moment, scribe, I have a proposition for you that you may be interested in...

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text:
Wait, <name>, before you leave... did you not notice this?

<Raethan peels a small piece of paper from the bottom of the jewel.>

This wasn't reported stolen. It appears to be a card of some kind. Must be a scribe thing.

Perhaps it may be of some use to you.

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text: What's that you have there?

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text:
I... I know this work. My old apprentice, what's-his-name, was trying to prove he could create something as great as I could.

Impressively, he seemed to have succeeded in this one case.

We should learn from what he created and make our own, less putrid version.

passages.title: Roseate Essence
passages.text:
<The pigment milled from this flower is of an exceptionally high quality.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Roseate Essence
passages.text:
How did you get an extract so pure? Show me exactly what you did, step by step.

Fascinating. Do you mind if I write this down, so I can show my other students?

passages.title: Sallow Essence
passages.text:
<The felwort is reduced to a thick, clotted pigment. While all felwort-begotten pigment is somewhat offensive, this batch practically glows with a malevolent energy.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Sallow Essence
passages.text:
We've ventured into undiscovered territory, <name>. There isn't anyone out there in ANY academic circles I'm aware of that is milling felwort this effectively.

Well done, student. Or, should I say... well done, junior deputy assistant scribe?

Nah... I still prefer "student".

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Very well, I won't deny it. The Steamy Romance Novel is mine.

I only read it for the penmanship, I assure you! He writes such curvy "B"s... and such ample "D"s!

In fact... you might benefit from a penmanship lesson. The author of these books is one B. Spearshaker. I believe he can be found in the library in Ironforge.

Stop reading, student. You are dismissed. And give me my book back!

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Hello! Ye must be one of me many fans here for an autograph.

Oh, yer here about the romance novels, are ye? I see ye've discovered my little secret.

Ye know, I've grown tired of writing those. I've moved on, ye see. Wrote me last one yesterday.

But perhaps ye'd like to carry on the tradition...?

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
I've lost my passion, scribe. I just can't get into the voice o' the characters anymore.

Take a look at that unfinished book over there on the table. I can't seem to finish it. Maybe ye'll have an easier time with it.

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text: Dang-blasted writer's block!

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
Hmm... yes, ye seem to have gotten the hang of it. I particularly like that line: "Oh, Lord Gravesbane!" That would make a nice catchphrase...

Here, take this list o' story prompts. I certainly don't need them anymore.

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Very well, I won't deny it. The Steamy Romance Novel is mine.

I only read it for the penmanship, I assure you! He writes such curvy "B"s... and such ample "D"s!

In fact... you might benefit from a penmanship lesson. The author of these books is one F. Serbacon. I believe he can be found in the library in Undercity.

Stop reading, student. You are dismissed. And give me my book back!

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Come for an autograph, have you? Very well, you may present your chest to me.

Oh, you're here about the romance novels? I see you've discovered my little secret.

You know, I've grown tired of writing those. I've moved on, you see. Wrote the last one yesterday.

But perhaps you'd like to carry on the tradition...?

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
I've lost my passion, scribe. I just can't find the voice of my characters anymore.

Take a look at that unfinished book over there on the table. I can't seem to finish it. Maybe you'll have an easier time with it.

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text: Confound this accursed writer's block!

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
Hmm... yes, you seem to have gotten the hang of it. I particularly like that line: "Oh, Lord Gravesbane!" That would make a nice catchphrase...

Here, take this list of story prompts. I certainly don't need them anymore.

passages.title: An Embarrassing Revelation
passages.text:
This doesn't appear to be an inscription textbook at all... it's more of a steamy romance novel. The pages are just FILLED with tawdry tales of carnality.

Could it have something to do with inscription? Either way, Professor Pallin should be confronted.

passages.title: An Embarrassing Revelation
passages.text:
Get your hands off of... err, I mean... that's not my...

Where did you...

<The professor makes a sputtering sound.>

Someone must be playing a trick on me!

passages.title: Trouble for Okuna
passages.text:
<You open the bottle and find a message inside.>

Help! I need somebody... but not just anybody. I need a champion! I finally escaped the grasp of Prince Oceanus only to be hunted by his father, King Deepbeard.

I was enjoying my freedom and decided to go fishing when that giant attacked. I've been running around these islands trying to avoid that creature ever since... if anyone gets this message, please send help!

passages.title: Kill Azshara
passages.text: xxxxx

passages.title: Meet the Recruits
DEPRECATED
passages.text:
Archmage Khadgar sent word about Val'Sharah not long ago.

His Kirin Tor have opened a gateway between here and Dalaran - you can find it in the alcove behind you if you wish to make use of it, Highlord.

passages.title: Remnants of the Past
passages.text:
<The journal entry appears hastily written.>

I do not know what has become of my village. Ever since the mists engulfed the harbor, my kinsfolk have changed.

Some have grown violent and savage, while others have fallen into madness. Many have ventured into the mists and have yet to return.

In these times, we can usually turn to our leader, Jarl Tarben. Alas, the mists have taken him as well.

I do not know what will become of me. For now, I can only stay at my post and remain vigilant.

passages.title: Remnants of the Past
passages.text:
The mists of this bay rot not only the wood of the ships, but the very souls of its inhabitants.

But it seems you have already discovered this.

passages.title: Khadgar's Discovery
passages.text:
Champion! Please come to the Violet Citadel immediately.

I have made a discovery that I would like to share with you before the Council of Six.

passages.title: Khadgar's Discovery
passages.text: Thank you for coming, <name>.

passages.title: Magic Message
passages.text:
For the last 10,000 years, the elven city of Suramar has been sealed in an arcane barrier, much like Dalaran once was.

That barrier has come down.

Since then, waves of magical energy have been emanating from the city like ripples in a pond. It was in these waves that I sensed a pattern.

A spell, encrypted among the chaos.

I have recreated the spell here. It's not dangerous, but beyond that... I have no idea what it does!

passages.title: Magic Message
passages.text: Go ahead and take a look.

passages.title: Magic Message
passages.text: A magical message in a bottle, slipped right beneath the Legion's nose... Clever.

passages.title: Huln's War - Stormrage
passages.text: <Eche'ro nuzzles your hand and turns around. It looks back, beckoning you to the south.>

passages.title: Huln's War - Stormrage
passages.text: You bring with you Eche'ro, and... what is this? The blessing of Cenarius?!

passages.title: Keepers of the Hammer
passages.text:
High Chieftain Ulan has requested your presence.

We have learned that the Burning Legion has returned and know that if you are true in your purpose in facing this evil, you will need our aid.

Our people have in our possession a great titan relic: the Hammer of Khaz'goroth.

We intend to lend it to you for this task.

When you are ready, join me at our stronghold of Thunder Totem in Highmountain.

passages.title: Huln's War - Reinforcements
passages.text:
Cenarius himself has risked much in coming here, if only briefly, to bestow a blessing upon you. He has seen what you are capable of, and has chosen you as champion in this battle. I would speak with you on this later. It is a rare gift indeed.

But now, I ask for your help, Huln Highmountain. I must finish my incantations to allow dryads from beyond the veil to enter this place and lend us their aid.

passages.title: Huln's War - Reinforcements
passages.text: This shouldn't take long. Please do not allow them to interrupt my spell.

passages.title: Huln's War - Reinforcements
passages.text: The ritual is complete. Reinforcements will be able to push through the portal and assist against the demonic horde.

passages.title: Blessing of Cenarius
passages.text:
Cenarius himself has risked much in coming here, if only briefly, to bestow a blessing upon you. He has seen what you are capable of, and has chosen you as champion in this battle.

Speak with him in the grove to the south. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39991))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39991))");

passages.title: Huln's War - The Nathrezim
passages.text:
I am fully occupied here organizing my troops and planning for the battle to come.

While I would like to slay the Dreadlord Tichondrius myself, I will allow that honor to be yours, Huln Highmountain.

passages.title: Huln's War - The Nathrezim
passages.text: You see now, that Huln was mighty? He united the tribes and defeated terribly powerful foes.

passages.title: Knocking on Valor's Door
passages.text:
The Halls of Valor is your destiny to claim, but it is already in the claiming. The God-King befouls its steps with demons and wickedness.

Your dragon allies have come to Halls' defense, but they need your aid. The vrykul have taken the leader of the storm dragons, the one you call Vethir.

Free your dragon friend, champion, and wash the Felskorn from the Gates of Valor!

passages.title: Knocking on Valor's Door
passages.text:
What is this... I see? 

A friendly face... in a sea of foes?

passages.title: A Familiar Fate
passages.text:
We had come to defend the Halls of Valor... I was taken from the sky...

I cannot break free of my bindings. Find the jailer who made this cell...

Set me free, friend...

passages.title: A Familiar Fate
passages.text: The jailer has... the key...

passages.title: A Familiar Fate
passages.text:
You still manage to surprise me, outsider. Your trials are complete, and yet you still have challenges to face. 

The God-King's forces are many, but in your weapon you possess the powers of Stormheim herself! Approach the gates, and these powers will lay low the enemies of this land!

Now, let us take the fight to the God-King, and cleanse the Gates of Valor of his fel taint!

passages.title: Break the Spine
passages.text:
To lead his tainted forces, the God-King has enlisted demons of great power to act as his lieutenants. If we wish to end his assault, we will need to take their leaders.

These demons are too powerful for most mortals to face, but with the power of Stormheim at your disposal, they will prove no match for you. 

Take them down, and shatter the spine of Skovald's offensive!

passages.title: Break the Spine
passages.text: Are the leaders slain?

passages.title: Break the Spine
passages.text:
With their fel leaders slain, the God-King's forces will scatter. 

Still, we are not finished here. So long as the demons continue to assault the gates, Stormheim will not be safe.

passages.title: Stormheim's Salvation
passages.text:
It would seem that the portals we destroyed down here were not the only ones. Demons still pour in from the top of the Gates of Valor's edifice, summoned by the God-King himself!

I cannot face Skovald alone. Come, champion, let us take the battle to him and end this threat!

For Stormheim!

passages.title: Stormheim's Salvation
passages.text:
It's unfortunate that the God-King escaped, but his defeat has stemmed the flow of the Legion into Stormheim.

Now, the Halls of Valor await you.

passages.title: The Only Way Out is Through
passages.text:
I have much to tell you, but it is not safe to speak here. I cannot hold this barrier forever.

<Thalyssra lifts a delicate flask to her lips. Her eyes shimmer as she takes a sip.>

If we push through, we may find shelter up ahead.

passages.title: The Only Way Out is Through
passages.text: There is no turning back.

passages.title: The Only Way Out is Through
passages.text:
You fight well.

Perhaps it is time for a proper introduction.

passages.title: Tapping the Leylines
passages.text:
The arcways were built to tap into the magical leylines beneath Suramar. As we learned to subsist on the Nightwell, the old facilities fell out of use.

This chamber is clearly receiving power from elsewhere.

There is only a trickle now, but if you can direct more leyline energy here it will help to sustain us.

The closest source is to the north, near Anora Hollow.

passages.title: Tapping the Leylines
passages.text: And just who might you be?

passages.title: Oculeth's Workshop
passages.text:
We need to make contact with Chief Telemancer Oculeth, the man who developed Suramar's teleportation network. 

Oculeth had a workshop in old Suramar, from the age before the Sundering. He may be taking refuge there.

<Thalyssra presses a small coin into your palm.>

If you find him, show him this. Hopefully you see him before he sees you...

passages.title: Oculeth's Workshop
passages.text: If we are to put up any resistance against the combined forces of the Legion and the Grand Magistrix, we must secure a means of traversing the region quickly.

passages.title: Oculeth's Workshop
passages.text: You may deliver me to Thalyssra once my work here is complete.

passages.title: An Old Ally
passages.text:
I was on my way to Ambervale in hopes of finding an old colleague.

Arcanist Kel'danath was fascinated by the withered. He studied them for years hoping to calm their feral nature or even cure them.

When one of his subjects escaped and ran amok in the royal gardens, Kel'danath was ordered to cease his research and kill all withered in his possession. He refused, and was exiled.

If Kel'danath lives, he is near withered. And withered are drawn to old settlements like Ambervale.

passages.title: An Old Ally
passages.text: <Somebody has been living here recently. This scroll bears strange lettering that glows warmly, beckoning your hand.>

passages.title: Aethril Sample
passages.text:
This herb has clearly been absorbing magical energy from the land. Filaments of ley energy course from root to leaf.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Aethril Sample
passages.text:
From the look of it, I would expect such an herb to be fragile and delicate, but... it's quite sturdy.

Oooh, look at these!

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
The stem, leaves, and petals are dazzling, to be certain... but look at the pollination filaments, here, and the reproductive organs in the center of the bloom. They contain more energy than the rest of the plant put together.

I suspect that we can more responsibly and efficiently harvest aethril by focusing on these parts.

Still, it looks like this bloom has been damaged. I need undamaged parts if I'm to be sure.

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
It may seem wrong to remove these most... "intimate" flower parts, but do not fret. They will grow back.

Much like the parts of a troll.

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
<Your trainer looks over the pistil and stamen, clearly impressed.>

The Earthmother must have been feeling generous when she created the aethril.

Continue to focus on this part of the flower, <name>.

passages.title: Ragged Strips of Silk
passages.text:
Finely made strips of clothing, torn, tattered, and dirty: telltale signs of the withered.

The feral, degenerate outcasts of nightborne society must also be harvesting the aethril... but why?

passages.title: Ragged Strips of Silk
passages.text:
You found withered implements near an aethril bloom?

Hmm... you're the third one today.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text:
I believe we may be able to use this clue to our advantage, <name>.

The withered are notoriously thirsty for mana, and will stop at nothing to get it. Perhaps we can study how they use the aethril and use the results to improve our own harvesting methods.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text: I am glad you continue to come to my shop, <name>. I am useless with a weapon. We need adventurers like you to solve cases like this.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text:
<Your trainer examines the stems, fingering the individual bite marks.>

If you'll pardon my language, they really gnawed the crap out of these things.

Look more closely, though. You can see that they focused on extracting the energy from the stem's central filament...

passages.title: Dreamleaf Sample
passages.text:
The herb is brilliantly green, paper-thin, and somewhat sticky.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Dreamleaf Sample
passages.text:
I know this herb. I've seen it once before, in the Pandaria's Valley of the Four Winds.

This is dreamleaf.

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text:
Something is different about this dreamleaf, though. It is less than pure.

I have a theory.

The wilds of Val'sharah have been blighted by a nightmarish curse. Sensitive herbs like this may be susceptible to such a blight.

I need more information before I can draw any conclusions. Find me some healthy samples and some blight-infested samples, and we can continue.

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text: Those poor plants...

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text:
It is just as I suspected. The infested herb is dying... but this may be turned to our advantage.

Look, herbalist. The dying dreamleaf has swollen with herbaceous extract. While harvesting the healthy dreamleaf is trivial, you can harvest enormous amounts of product from the infested ones.

passages.title: Twisted to Death
passages.text:
The corruption has completely taken this herb.

This blight is a mysterious force whose complexities transcend the teachings of simple herbalism. An expert in such infestation will need to tell you what's really going on here.

passages.title: Twisted to Death
passages.text:
Another plant, fallen...

<The druid attempts to blink back tears, and fails.>

DAMN YOU, NIGHTMARE! DAMN YOUUUUU!!!

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text:
We must exact VENGEANCE for this. While I understand the importance of the balance between the Emerald Dream and the Nightmare, this time it's corruption has gone TOO FAR!

Satyrs. I blame the satyrs for this. Make them pay! Make them pay, and Elune will reward you with her bounty!

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text: Exact your bloody vengeance, <class>. Show them the might of an herbalist.

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text:
I feel the blight subsiding. Good.

Our respite will not last forever, but look... even now, the dreamleaf has succumbed more of its bounty.

passages.title: Choked by Nightmare
passages.text:
Another plant, killed by the blight. This one coiled so hard that it starved itself of sunlight.

You should bring it to Wildcrafter Osme in Lorlathil. He won't be happy.

passages.title: Choked by Nightmare
passages.text:
<Osme looks at the herb.>

<He is silent for a moment.>

NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!!!

passages.title: Teeny Bite Marks
passages.text:
This herb has been chewed by some of the local wildlife.

What kind of animal would eat foxflower? A bear?

Perhaps your trainer in Dalaran will know.

passages.title: Teeny Bite Marks
passages.text: You're right, <name>. Something has been chewing on this herb.

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text:
To one not trained in herbalism, this brambly bush might appear to be entirely useless. Your training, however, reveals this to be a very special plant indeed.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see some more samples of this.

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text: What do you have there, herbalist?

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text:
What a fantastic find, <name>. This must be the celebrated vrykul herb, fjarnskaggl. I've only read about it in books!

Here, I'll share what I remember with you...

passages.title: Ram's-Horn Trowel
passages.text:
The rune markings along the tool's grip suggest that it was left behind by a vrykul herbalist.

Apparently, the vrykul are also gathering this fjarnskaggl. Your trainer, Kuhuine, mentioned that she had read about this herb in the past.

Perhaps she might be interested in seeing the tools that the vrykul use to harvest it.

passages.title: Ram's-Horn Trowel
passages.text: You found this near a snarl of fjarnskaggl?

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text:
<Kuhuine studies the trowel further.>

This is a standard digging tool. There is not much to be learned here, except...

...this DOES suggest that the vrykul are still actively gathering this herb.

The vrykul likely know much more about this herb than we do. All we need to do is find out where their knowledge is stored.

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text: Any luck finding those books, <name>?

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text:
This book: "Herblore of the Ancients", seems promising, but several pages are ripped out. Shame.

Still, there is much to learn in the others.

<Kuhuine turns to a random page, flips a few pages back and...>

See, look at this technique here!

passages.title: The Missing Page
passages.text:
<The page appears to be ripped out of a larger book. It reads:>

"...the Cairn of the Sea, a place long-known to be beloved by the gods.

He placed his offering of fjarnskaggl at the foot of the cairn, mouthed the words 'Herbs beget herbs', and received the blessing he desired."

This may be related to the books you brought back to your herbalism trainer.

passages.title: The Missing Page
passages.text: What good fortune! This page matches perfectly with the book you retrieved for me. We just need to piece them together, and...

passages.title: Starlight Rosedust
passages.text:
Despite all your training, the rose disintegrated in your hand.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Starlight Rosedust
passages.text:
This herb just disintegrated in your hand?

Fascinating...

passages.title: The Gentlest Touch
passages.text: Sadly, I don't have any special techniques that can help you here. You'll simply need to practice your methods. Get back out there, and focus on a gentle touch when dealing with starlight roses.

passages.title: The Gentlest Touch
passages.text:
Any success? None?

Even if you haven't found success, your skills are improving. Don't give up, herbalist.

passages.title: Jeweled Spade Handle
passages.text:
An immaculately carved spade handle lies beside the rose. Apparently the spade was more beautiful than it was durable, as the blade has completely fallen off.

Your herbalism trainer may be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Jeweled Spade Handle
passages.text:
You say you found this near a starlight rose?

You adventurers, always finding such interesting things out there in the wilds...

passages.title: The Spade's Blade
passages.text:
Did you notice the script along the base of the handle, <name>? It says "Herbalist Tharillon," in the writing of the nightborne.

The handle does little for us, but perhaps the blade of this spade will give us some information on how to harvest the starlight rose without failing quite so often.

I would start my search for it in Suramar.

passages.title: The Spade's Blade
passages.text: How goes your search?

passages.title: The Spade's Blade
passages.text:
The blade is enchanted - of course it would be. I'm certain that we can replicate this enchantment here in Dalaran.

Shame that that herbalist wasn't more agreeable. There may have been more that we could have learned from him. At least he's still alive out there, somewhere...

passages.title: Insane Ramblings
passages.text:
Scribbled, angry phrases on a dirty scrap of vellum. One part catches your eye:

 "thinks <HE/SHE> knows how to gather herbs
 <name><name>
<name><name> steal my blade
 slit <his/her> THROAT when I

 just need
 a bit more mana
 maybe aethril, yes..."

Your herbalism trainer may be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Insane Ramblings
passages.text:
My word. This person really hates you.

Say - do you think this is written by that nightborne herbalist you... encountered?

passages.title: Felwort Sample
passages.text:
This herb bubbles and seethes with a foul energy. It is smooth, dry, and cool, yet somehow quite painful to touch.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Felwort Sample
passages.text:
Oh. I don't like this herb at all. I'm fascinated, but I don't like it.

<Kuhuine peers into the center of the plant.>

Look at the size of these seeds, <name>. We can use these. Make sure you harvest them carefully next time.

passages.title: The Hunter of Heroes
passages.text:
Helya has made a mockery of my order by creating her own "helarjar", powerful undead tasked with hunting down heroic warriors and taking their souls before my val'kyr can claim them. Among them is her personal champion, Vigfus Bladewind, who wields stolen blades I forged myself long ago.

He has returned to Tideskorn Harbor with a full cargo of stolen souls to take to Helheim. Go there, kill him and his helarjar, and make the swords yours.

passages.title: The Hunter of Heroes
passages.text: Ah, you have returned...

passages.title: The Hunter of Heroes
passages.text: Curse Helya, she's corrupted the blades! Still, her champion defeated, her helarjar skulking back to Helheim, and my weapons in the hands of my chosen champion! She even made them more powerful than before. Wield them well, <name>, smite the enemies of this world!

passages.title: Shadows in the Mists
passages.text:
Many of the Kvaldir here in the bay are former denizens of this harbor, cursed by the sea-witch Helya to do her bidding for all time.

The ones you read about, they still walk the stagnant waters. They could be given respite, should a kind soul bring it to them at the tip of a blade.

So tell me, how kind is your soul?

passages.title: Shadows in the Mists
passages.text:
Their toil is ended, and fewer kvaldir walk the lands of Stormheim.

Both are blessings, I would say.

passages.title: Nature vs. Nurture
passages.text:
I appreciate murloc-kind far too much to tell you to go kill all the adults.

What we should be doing is setting up the next generation to be more peaceful; Murky is the best representative for this. 

Bring him to talk to the murloc tadpoles. He'll get them on our side.

passages.title: Nature vs. Nurture
passages.text: Getting the support of the tadpoles is very important for our mission.

passages.title: Nature vs. Nurture
passages.text: Murky's gained quite the following, hasn't he? Perhaps they can help him out.

passages.title: Scavenging the Shallows
passages.text:
The kvaldir exist to spite Odyn, and it is here their spiteful work is done. They rob the souls of the living - the souls not yet judged - thus robbing Odyn of his champions.

They bring them here to transport to Helya, though the mists obscure any indications of how.

You seem to fare the mists well. Perhaps if you search the wreckage in the bay, the answer may present itself. You outsiders seem to have a knack for uncovering the most hidden of secrets.

passages.title: Scavenging the Shallows
passages.text: Have you found answers, or more questions?

passages.title: Scavenging the Shallows
passages.text:
The Naglfar...

So Helya's kvaldir can navigate the mists?

passages.title: I'll Huff, I'll Puff...
passages.text:
Murky is my favorite little fella. However, in order to lead a change in the murloc population here, he needs some awesome abilities.

There are a lot of pufferfish around in the water, and I think that they could be a good resource for him. 

Kill a few and collect their eggs for Murky.

passages.title: I'll Huff, I'll Puff...
passages.text: Pufferfish have this impressive ability of... exploding. They could be a powerful tool for Murky.

passages.title: I'll Huff, I'll Puff...
passages.text:
The pufferfish will be a perfect resource for Murky! I'll just whip up a spell to make them grow more quickly.

All he'll have to do is throw, then boom!

passages.title: Slime Time
passages.text:
Murky's a growing boy, he needs to eat! What better than slimeweed for a young murloc?

There's plenty of it around in the water amongst the murlocs; swim through it and feed Murky!

passages.title: Slime Time
passages.text: Murky seems to have gotten a very strong slime ability due to this slimeweed. Fantastic!

passages.title: Fel Secrets
passages.text:
The demons made a grave error inscribing their secrets into this book. The fel energy emanating from it is potent.

But there's only enough to enact one of the rituals. After that, the book will be consumed.

It's up to you to choose which secrets we want to use against the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Fel Secrets
passages.text: Have you made up your mind?

passages.title: Fel Secrets
passages.text:
Surprising. I agree. Well chosen, <name>.

Now, you must teach the rest of us.

passages.title: Ancient Vrykul Mastered
passages.text:
Here are those tablets back, along with their deciphered writing. You can take this codex back to Pallin, too. I'll start getting my things ready for when he calls me back to Dalaran.

<Nicholo sighs.>

Learn from my example, <name>. If I were you, I'd break free from Pallin's "requests" as soon as you can.

passages.title: Ancient Vrykul Mastered
passages.text:
So, Nicholo was able to complete the codex? And the tablets are deciphered!

Hmm... that's interesting. These tablets have some interesting spells that we could use to our benefit... although I find working with stone to be a bit archaic. I'll just put these down on parchment and let you test for any side effects.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text:
Student! Your fellow demon hunters in Azsuna have sent for you.

I can certainly appreciate your time being spent fending off the Legion, but it doesn't excuse you from your studies.

While you're down there, I'd like you to come up with some new glyphs for your abilities.

Surely my genius has worn off on you and you'll be able to create your own recipes based on what you learn.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text: <name>, good to see you again. We could certainly use your strength.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text:
I see, you wish to augment your powers through script. I believe we can kill two birds with one stone then.

I need help here reducing the demon threat. Perhaps some more engagement with our enemy will inspire you.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text:
I wish I had more like you, <name>. You fight with a great passion.

And I see you also learned a bit more about how to augment our abilities. I'm sure your master in Dalaran will be pleased.

passages.title: Defense Symbology
passages.text:
As you know, <name>, we demon hunters must keep our darkness at bay, lest we succumb to it and become demons ourselves.

Up to the north, a demon hunter by the name of Baric Stormrunner is preparing to strengthen his markings. He could use your assistance with his ritual.

passages.title: Defense Symbology
passages.text:
You've come to help me with my ritual? I thank you, <name>.

In this time, allies are more important than ever.

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text:
The ruins nearby have had an eruption of ley energies. Twisted night elves deemed "Nightfallen" are scavenging the area as we speak.

Collect ley dust for me from the nightfallen in the ruins up ahead. The dust is infused with arcane energy that I'll need to complete my ritual.

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text: Even though they are opposites, one can not exist without the other.

passages.title: Opposites Repel
passages.text:
If you can believe it, that was the easy part.

The next part will be a bit more challenging, at least for me it will.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
Now that we have all the essential pieces, let's begin the ritual.

I'll instruct you on how to help me throughout it. It is pivotal that you follow my instructions when I give them, or the ritual will fail.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
It is done. I fear that I had waited any longer to improve my wards, the demon in me may have taken over.

Thank you again, <name>.

passages.title: To Know Your Enemy
passages.text:
As we fight the demons, we've also been studying them.

Great understanding can come from gathering intel. I have a demon hunter near the Felblaze Ingress now gathering intel on the demons there.

Go to her and see what she has learned from the demons invading that region.

passages.title: To Know Your Enemy
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <name>. Kayn has sent you to see what I have learned?

In that case, I have much to tell.

passages.title: Bulging Nightmare Pod
passages.text:
<The flower has folded inward, to protect itself from the nightmare energy trapped within.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Bulging Nightmare Pod
passages.text:
Pods like this contain tremendous amounts of energy. Milling one incorrectly can be catastrophic to the front of one's robes.

Learn to mill them correctly, though, and you can dramatically increase your milling speed. Watch and learn, student!

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
I trust you remember why you removed your eyes?

Even though we can see more clearly now, the demons have found ways to mask even their fel energies from us.

A demon commander walks amongst the troops below, commanding them from the shadows. His cloak is powered by an energetic crystal.

Find and destroy that crystal, then kill the commander.

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
I commend you, scribe. You are an excellent hunter.

Take this ink as payment for your efforts. I have no need of it.

passages.title: Woody Seed Cluster
passages.text:
<Attempting to mill this flower has proven more difficult than usual. Located in the bushy center of the bloom is a densely-packed cluster of seeds.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Woody Seed Cluster
passages.text:
This came from a foxflower? Fascinating.

You know, we can use these woody cores to our advantage. If you mill a woody flower along with several softer flowers, you can speed up your process dramatically! Watch this...

passages.title: Fjarnsk
passages.text:
<A goopy substance seeps from the interior of the bloom. It's not ink... it is something else entirely.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Fjarnsk
passages.text:
<The Professor dips his finger into the fluid and tastes it.>

Oh! I know what this is. The herbalists were talking about this. It's called fjarnsk.

You know, stranglekelp often contains pockets of fluid not unlike this. Let's see if we can carry an old milling technique forward...

passages.title: Eagle Egg Recovery
passages.text:
Eagles are revered by the Skyhorn tribe, but their numbers are dwindling.

The drogbar feed their fledgling worms eagle eggs so they'll grow strong enough to ride into battle. 

If the drogbar continue to pilfer these eggs, the eagles may become extinct.

Head deeper into the cave and recover any eagle eggs you can find.

passages.title: Eagle Egg Recovery
passages.text: If the pilfered eggs are not recovered, the eagle may go extinct.

passages.title: Eagle Egg Recovery
passages.text:
These eggs are in poor condition, <name>. Some are cracked and spoiled, while others are cold to the touch.

Yet there is still hope. I believe a few of the eggs you recovered can be saved.

passages.title: Tamer Takedown
passages.text:
The drogbar will continue to breed vicious worms as long as their tamer lives. 

Korgrul is responsible for turning fledgling rockcrawlers into the monstrous siege worms that are ridden into battle.

Head deep into the chasm and end his life, so that we may also see the end of these unnatural creatures.

passages.title: Tamer Takedown
passages.text: Put an end to Tamer Korgrul, so that we may also put an end to the training of siege worms.

passages.title: Tamer Takedown
passages.text: Korgrul deserved his fate. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Huln's War - Malorne's Favored
passages.text:
[In broken Common] Shan'do ask for you. Sent Eche'ro beast with message on rack.

Unng Ak hear Eche'ro sound fighting. You find beast? Give help, maybe feathered night elf be relieve.

passages.title: Huln's War - Malorne's Favored
passages.text: <Eche'ro looks up briefly, then lowers its head before you. This creature is thankful for your aid.>

passages.title: A Murky Fate
passages.text:
You may not know, but you stand upon the grounds of Morheim, home to the greatest warriors of the land. Our deeds were great, our valor legendary. It pains me that we see such an end.

The creatures set upon us at nightfall. Our men fought bravely, but were vastly outnumbered. Now their corpses lie rotting in the sun, with no burial and no rites.

This is not an end befitting to the glorious warriors of Morheim. Make it right, and you will have our thanks.

passages.title: A Murky Fate
passages.text: Have you done this task?

passages.title: A Murky Fate
passages.text:
It is good to know that our warriors remains have been honored.

May they now celebrate their victories in the halls of Valhallas.

passages.title: Cenarius, Keeper of the Grove
passages.text:
Ahh, Val'sharah.

It has been an age since I have set foot in these sacred woods. Too long...

Our work here is simple, <class>. We must call upon my mentor, Cenarius, and learn where he safeguards the Tears of Elune. With them, you will be one step closer to sealing Sargeras' Tomb and thwarting the Legion.

You have many treacherous tasks in front of you. Consider your visit here a brief respite.

Come, this will not take long.

passages.title: Cenarius, Keeper of the Grove
passages.text: Cenarius!

passages.title: Cenarius, Keeper of the Grove
passages.text:
This corruption - I've never seen it before.

And yet, it seems somehow familiar...

passages.title: The Nightborne Pact
passages.text:
<Thalyssra winces and holds her abdomen.>

Ngh... I can ignore this wound no longer.

Help me patch this up. I will explain everything.

passages.title: The Nightborne Pact
passages.text: We must find a way to reclaim Suramar City.

passages.title: Branch of the Arcan'dor
passages.text:
You have used the spellstone of Kel'danath to soothe countless withered. Yet it contains merely a shade of the arcan'dor's power, drawn from its slumbering seed. 

<Thalyssra holds aloft a gleaming white branch.>

This fell from the tree. Though it is severed, it is not dead - invisible threads of magic bind all pieces of the arcan'dor together.

I have enchanted this branch with a new iteration of Kel'danath's charm spell. With it, you can mend the arcane essence of even more withered. Use it well.

passages.title: Branch of the Arcan'dor
passages.text: I never imagined I would spend my time in exile studying withered. Through them, I have learned a great deal about my own people, and the nature of our relationship with the Nightwell.

passages.title: Scrap of Pants
passages.text:
The mouth of this particular beast contained a piece of handsewn cloth. The fabric bears the word "singwa".

While the term "singwa" is unfamiliar, it DOES happen to be the middle of the last name of a fairly notable Azerothian skinner.

passages.title: Scrap of Pants
passages.text: Ye found me extra set o'pants!

passages.title: Immaculate Stonehide Leather
passages.text:
You have been skinning for a long time now, but never have you seen a leather specimen as fine as this. Durable, pliable, beautifully colored...

Your trainer in Dalaran would be VERY interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Immaculate Stonehide Leather
passages.text: <name>, you return. What can I do for you today?

passages.title: Leather for Ske'rit
passages.text:
This hide certifies that you have learned everything about leather that I can teach you, <name>. My skills have dulled since I set up shop here in town.

I have a former protege who skins the creatures of Suramar. His name is Ske'rit. His skills remain as sharp as his blade, and if there is anyone out there who can teach you, it is him.

passages.title: Leather for Ske'rit
passages.text: Ey dere. You be a skinna'?

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Hide of Fenryr
passages.text:
While you be here, I got a favor t'ask you.

I been hearin' whispers about one big, nasty wolf dat's been causin' all kinds of trouble up in de vrykul lands. His name be Fenryr.

I want his hide.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Hide of Fenryr
passages.text: Is it done? Let me see it!

passages.title: Halls of Valor: The Hide of Fenryr
passages.text: I seen wolf hides before, but dis be sometin' else.

passages.title: Unfinished Treatise on the Properties of Stormscale
passages.text:
Tucked between the folds of this animal's hide, you find a scrap of paper. It appears to be a handwritten guide to harvesting stormscales, but too much of the manuscript has been lost to be of use.

Perhaps your skinning trainer in Dalaran could help you find its owner.

passages.title: Unfinished Treatise on the Properties of Stormscale
passages.text:
<Kondal looks over the paper, brows furrowed.>

I know of only two people who may have written this, <name>. I can tell you where they both are located, if you so desire.

passages.title: Glielle
passages.text:
One skinner makes the wilds of Azsuna her home. Her name is Glielle, and she is a night elf - or at least, she was, in life.

Perhaps the scroll was hers.

passages.title: Glielle
passages.text: What? No, that scroll isn't mine. I don't do much writing these days.

passages.title: Under Down
passages.text:
I can train you, though.

Everyone knows about the bright stormscales on the hippogryph's hindquarters, but did you know that they also have a few scales beneath their feathers? You just need to know where to look.

<The night elf spirit indicates a few places near the hippogryph's wing joints.>

Now go see if you can get some on your own.

passages.title: Under Down
passages.text: Remember to check the entire beast, not just what's visible on the surface.

passages.title: Under Down
passages.text: Looks like you've got the hang of it. Well done.

passages.title: Seymour and Agnes
passages.text:
The other skinner - pair of skinners, to be honest - that comes to mind when you show me this scroll is a student of mine, named Seymour, and his mother Agnes.

Last I heard, they were in Stormheim, hunting the storm drakes.

passages.title: Seymour and Agnes
passages.text:
Yes, yes, that's my manuscript, but there's no time for that.

Look what they've done to my MOTHER!

passages.title: Mother's Prized Knife
passages.text:
The other day, Mother and I were up at the top of the nearby mountain, and she threw her skinning knife at me because the view wasn't good enough.

Her knife is still up there, somewhere. I'd feel horrible just leaving it.

passages.title: Mother's Prized Knife
passages.text: Mother always wanted to live long enough to see me die. Why did this have to happen!?

passages.title: Mother's Prized Knife
passages.text: This is it - look, you can still see some of me on it.

passages.title: Red-Eyed Revenge
passages.text:
It came out of nowhere. I was waiting for mother to finish skinning her half of the drake when the biggest storm dragon I'd ever seen came and... and...

<Seymour finds his resolve.>

I want you to kill as many of them as you can. Skin them, don't skin them, I don't care. Just get revenge for mother!

passages.title: Red-Eyed Revenge
passages.text: Thank you. I don't know why, but your murder spree helps me feel a little bit better.

passages.title: Drakol'nir Must Die
passages.text:
The dragon that took Mother's life was named Drakol'nir.

Mother always wanted to wear his scale as a pendant, but we never got a chance to skin him because I couldn't kill him alone, and she didn't care much for killing. Only skinning.

You... you wouldn't mind bringing it for her, would you?

passages.title: Drakol'nir Must Die
passages.text: Even if I COULD have killed Drakol'nir, I never would have been able to drag him all the way down here.

passages.title: Drakol'nir Must Die
passages.text:
<Seymour places the scale lovingly upon his mother's chest. Even in death, she seems to disapprove.>

Thank you, <name>. Here, you take her skinning knife. It's not much, but she won't be needing it anymore.

passages.title: Immaculate Stormscale
passages.text:
You have been skinning for a long time now, but never have you seen a scale specimen as fine as this.

Your trainer in Dalaran would be VERY interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Immaculate Stormscale
passages.text: What do we have here, <name>?

passages.title: Scales for Ske'rit
passages.text:
Your skills surpass mine, <name>. I have never even SEEN a scale such as this... let alone remove one so expertly.

If you still wish to learn more, you will need to seek an even greater skinner than I. His name is Ske'rit, and he was once my student.

You will find him in the wild areas of Suramar.

passages.title: Scales for Ske'rit
passages.text: What do we got here?

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Scales of Serpentrix
passages.text:
I got ta ask you a favor.

I haven't been ta Azsuna, and I don't see myself leavin' Suramar anytime soon. Problem is, dere's a big ol' serpent out dere dat's just beggin' ta be skinned. Just BEGGIN' for it.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Scales of Serpentrix
passages.text: You got dis, skinnah.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: The Scales of Serpentrix
passages.text: Very nice. You got a good knife hand, <name>.

passages.title: Felhide Sample
passages.text:
This demonic hide is completely unlike any standard beast hide you are accustomed to.

Your skinning trainer in Dalaran would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Felhide Sample
passages.text:
I know very little about demonic hides, <name>. I prefer to stay away from them.

That said, I will share with you what I do know...

passages.title: An Unseemly Task
passages.text:
I'm quite impressed with what you've been able to skin in these lands, felhide in particular.

But as my knowledge is limited in this area of skinning, I know of one who may have increased his skill in skinning such beasts.

You can find my old apprentice, Ske'rit in Suramar. Ask him if he knows how to yield better results from skinning demons.

passages.title: An Unseemly Task
passages.text: What'cha be needin' from me, mon?

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: The Pestilential Hide of Nythendra
passages.text:
There is one more demon hide to gather... but it isn't that of a demon. It's a dragon.

Nythendra, great green dragon, has nearly been eaten up by the Nightmare. Only a master skinner would be able to remove what bits of bug-eaten hide remain on her body.

Go on then, <name>. Show me what you've learned.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: The Pestilential Hide of Nythendra
passages.text: Any luck with the dragon?

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: The Pestilential Hide of Nythendra
passages.text:
You have done it, <name>. You've earned the last of my knowledge.

Now get out there, and get skinning!

passages.title: Magic Clams
passages.text:
<The clam resonates with a arcane energy.>

What are murlocs doing with arcane clams?

Perhaps your Nightfallen allies could make use of them.

passages.title: Tapping the Underground
passages.text:
Have you seen them, <name>?

These are not ordinary murlocs. They have been drawn by the ley line that flows from Azsuna into this land. 

Somehow they have managed to tap into its arcane current and are tapping its power for their own devious purposes.

These disturbances must be stopped if the ley line is to remain intact.

passages.title: Leying with Murlocs
passages.text:
I have seen these Seerspine summon minor elementals, which is no small feat for a murloc, but their high summoner, Blargrrrl, is trying to summon Torretus from the river.

I doubt a mere murloc has the capabilities to control an entity as powerful as Torrentus.

Blargrrrl will be deeply entranced if he is trying such a feat. We'll need something powerful to halt his ritual.

Infuse yourself with ley energies and return to me.

passages.title: Crossroads Rendezvous
passages.text:
An old apprentice of mine left during the war, shortly before we were all cursed.

I've recently heard that she's been seen near the Felblaze Ingress. I would very much like to speak to her once more.

Go and find her. Take her journal to her and let her know that I don't blame her for what she did.

And if she's willing, please bring her back to me.

passages.title: Crossroads Rendezvous
passages.text:
<The satyr takes the journal you offer and sobs.>

You bore the book of someone lost long ago, stranger. Better that you leave me in my misery than linger in this fel-cursed place.

passages.title: Amateur Hour
passages.text:
The hunters' lodge has attracted a lot of amateurs who call themselves hunters. They're scarin' away all the prize game with their antics.

While I'm a known expert with my rifle, I've yet to manage the art of negotiation.

How about ya do us all a favor and tell those novice hunters to head for the hills?

passages.title: Amateur Hour
passages.text: Have those amateur hunters scattered? Don't be afraid to use your fists if words don't do the job.

passages.title: Amateur Hour
passages.text:
Ya seem to have a gift when it comes to dealin' with amateurs. Maybe ya can help my ghostwriter, Addie?

I've promised to teach her how to hunt, but I don't have time to show her the basics.

passages.title: Leather Lady
passages.text:
I'd like you to start working with my apprentices.

The first is Diane Cannings, who has focused her expertise on the softer leather armors. She's just not that into mail armor, like the twins are.

Go talk to her about this new type of leather.

passages.title: Leather Lady
passages.text:
You're the one Namha's been talking to. Pleased to meet you.

Hopefully we can expand our pattern list beyond the helm you've made.

passages.title: Vestment Opportunity
passages.text:
While the vrykul of Northrend wore strong armor, their craftsmen always had the strongest.

Go to Stormheim, search for someone who knows about leather armor, and bring their chest piece back to me.

passages.title: Vestment Opportunity
passages.text: How's your search going?

passages.title: Vestment Opportunity
passages.text:
<Diane examines the chest piece thoroughly.>

This has some very interesting design. I think we can easily copy what they've achieved with this piece.

Here, try this pattern out.

passages.title: Stormheim Savagery
passages.text:
There's a land below - Stormheim, they call it - that's inhabited by vrykul. I remember the vrykul from my days in Northrend.

What I remember most was how well-crafted their armor was.

If the vrykul here are as skilled as the ones in Northrend, then I'm certain we can learn something by studying their armaments.

passages.title: Stormheim Savagery
passages.text: Are the vrykul giving you much trouble?

passages.title: Stormheim Savagery
passages.text:
Well now, this is a good variety of equipment you've brought me. Let's see what we have here...

<Diane studies the armor pieces very carefully for a while.>

Look here, <name>. See how they've strengthened the leather by over-stitching the seams...

passages.title: Mail Men
passages.text:
The two dwarves behind me are the Glowergold brothers. They're my resident mail armor experts.

While Ranid has decided to focus his skills towards lining his pockets, his brother, Thanid, still enjoys the crafting side of the trade.

Introduce yourself to Thanid. You may work with him to further our knowledge of turning these stormscales into something extraordinary.

passages.title: Mail Men
passages.text:
Pleasure to meet ye! Now, I'll be needing ye to do one very important thing fer me.

Ignore anything me brother tells ye. He's been out of practice fer years, but still thinks he's better than me.

It's a lie, lad.

passages.title: Black Rook Bandit
passages.text:
I've heard rumors of a grand castle in Val'sharah that's known to house an impressive army. Surely, the armor they wear ain't made of sticks and hay.

I'm willing to bet they've fashioned some mail armor at some point fer their troops and it's just sitting there, ripe for the taking.

How about ye head over there and see what ye can "borrow" from their armory.

passages.title: Black Rook Bandit
passages.text: Make sure ye don't get captured now, lad.

passages.title: Black Rook Bandit
passages.text:
I knew ye had it in ye! Good work, lad.

<Thanid looks the pieces over with a careful eye.>

Very clever. The elves certainly know their trade.

We should be able to copy this method with little to no problem.

passages.title: Too Good To Pass Up
passages.text:
All types of Black Rook Hold armor are intriguing, but I'm most interested in their chest pieces.

If ye can, try to find someone of importance there and... relieve them of their shirt.

If it makes ye feel any better, I've heard they're all cursed, so puttin' them out of their misery is the least ye could do.

passages.title: Too Good To Pass Up
passages.text: Chest armor is the best armor, I always say!

passages.title: Too Good To Pass Up
passages.text:
Oh, this is a beauty. Just look at that craftsmanship.

<Thanid looks the piece over very carefully.>

And looking at how it's pieced together, this should be a snap to replicate.

Here, lad, give this pattern a try and see how that works for ye.

passages.title: Tauren Tanning
passages.text:
Have you heard of the Highmountain tauren tribes? They're not unlike the tauren we know on Kalimdor.

I've heard they have a leatherworking master there who might be able to help us come up with some new patterns.

Travel to Highmountain and see if they're willing to teach you how they craft their armor.

passages.title: Tauren Tanning
passages.text:
I can smell the leather on you, stranger.

It's in your skin, your bones, your spirit. It's also clear to these eyes that you wish to know about the leather of these lands.

If that's the case... then I must test your grain.

passages.title: Drogbar Durability
passages.text:
We are currently at war with a race known as the drogbar. We have long maintained peace with the drogbar, but lately, they have no respect for anyone but themselves.

Slay them. Prove your worth as an ally of the tauren. Do this, and I will reward you with knowledge.

passages.title: Drogbar Durability
passages.text:
If you can take down the drogbar, then perhaps you are worthy of my knowledge.

I'll start you with a couple simple patterns to start.

passages.title: Links in the Chain
passages.text:
Well, <lad/lass>, I'm afraid I'm at me wits' end with these scales. Not quite sure how to fashion the remaining pieces fer a full set.

However, I've heard that the elves of Azsuna had some great crafters in their cities. Perhaps one or two of them still exist.

Go there and search fer a master. Maybe they can fill in the missing patterns fer us.

passages.title: Links in the Chain
passages.text:
Yes, <class>? You seek to know the techniques of crafting elven mail?

I see. Perhaps a bargain can be struck to benefit us both.

passages.title: Best Served Cold
passages.text:
My partner and I both fell victim to the fallout of the Sundering. We were betrayed and abandoned by a trusted friend.

That "friend" has recently appeared in the ruins to the east. His name is Ranaris.

Go to and take revenge for us and I will grant you some of my wisdom.

passages.title: Best Served Cold
passages.text:
You are a man of your word, <name>. I thank you for your service to us.

And as we agreed, I shall pass on some of my wisdom to you.

passages.title: Naga Know-How
passages.text:
The naga of this region wear little armor, but what they do wear is particularly durable.

If you wish to make a strong shoulder piece, I would first study the naga's armor and then create a pattern of similar construct.

The city nearby is overrun by naga. Slay them and bring me their armor and I will show you what I mean.

passages.title: Naga Know-How
passages.text: They may be vile, but they still know how to craft as well as any master.

passages.title: Naga Know-How
passages.text:
These are good pieces. Look here...

<Celea begins to explain the armor's construction to you.>

...and with that, I trust you can create something of equal quality.

passages.title: Hardening the Hide
passages.text:
Back to Highmountain for you, <name>! I hear they know even more efficient ways to craft our patterns.

When you get there, put in a good word for me, will ya? I'd like to start a relationship the tauren, so I don't have to keep sending you back and forth.

passages.title: Hardening the Hide
passages.text:
Come for more lessons, <name>?

Very well. Let us begin.

passages.title: Stamped Stories
passages.text:
Stamped onto the leather of the tanning racks behind me are the ancient ways of our tribe's leatherworkers.

They tell the stories of masters who, through perseverance - and luck, in some cases - pioneered our way of leatherworking.

Read the stories and learn from them. Perhaps you'll find some insight on how to better your own methods.

passages.title: Stamped Stories
passages.text: I see hope in your eyes, <name>. I take it our lessons of the past will aid you with your future?

passages.title: Getting the Kinks Out
passages.text:
Now listen, <lad/lass>. Everything ye make can always be done better. I just haven't quite worked out the way to do it with these fancy new scales.

Perhaps that ghost-like elf friend of yours can help ye. An' if she DOES know somethin', perhaps ye can relay that information back to us.

It would certainly go towards making the shop more lucrative.

passages.title: Getting the Kinks Out
passages.text:
Back so soon, <name>?

Ahh... you wish to master your existing patterns. That's the characteristic of a true leatherworker.

Yes, I can help you.

passages.title: A Daring Rescue
passages.text:
My brother, Taldranis, was on a ship headed here to Azsuna. The ship was ambushed by the sea giants and my brother was taken captive.

I believe he still lives out his days in those horrible caves, slaving away for the giants. Go and free him, please.

Take this with you, it may give him enough protection should you run into any trouble. And be careful not to get captured by the giants yourself.

passages.title: A Daring Rescue
passages.text: Wait, Celea sent you? I thought she had been lost ages ago.

passages.title: Adventuring Anxieties
passages.text:
<name>! I was recently talking with Mei, the mount trader, and she asked me if it was possible to make a barding that could prevent adventurers from being dismounted.

I'd like you to go and discuss this idea with her further.
