passages.title: Consecrating Ground
passages.text:
We have everything we need.

In the alcove below you will find the shattered remains of the Argunite Matrix. Replacing the Keystone will restore it to full capacity.

The pylons you activated will then be able to repel those who still hunt my people. At long last this battle will be over.

I hope it brings them peace.

passages.title: Consecrating Ground
passages.text: Hurry <name>, we cannot let this continue any longer.

passages.title: Consecrating Ground
passages.text: <Velen peers at you, troubled.>

passages.title: Seeking Lost Knowledge
passages.text:
During the assault, our forces uncovered an ancient night elf tome. The fact that it survived so long in these harsh lands is quite remarkable.

Its enchantments have faded over the ages, but I sense the book is almost... hungry, as if reaching out to places where the night elves practiced magic long ago.

Bringing the tome to nearby ruins may reveal secrets that could give us an edge against the Legion.

passages.title: Seeking Lost Knowledge
passages.text: How was the tour of night elf ruins?

passages.title: Seeking Lost Knowledge
passages.text:
This tome is fascinating! It appears to seek out any and all knowledge that it does not already possess.

I'd wager an experienced researcher could direct it to locate specific knowledge.

Hmm, that gives me an idea...

passages.title: A Walk to Remember
passages.text:
It's good to have you at my side, <name>.

I've come to the Broken Shore to see, for myself, the price that my father... that the Alliance has paid to protect our world.

As long as I am blind to the suffering and sacrifices of my people, I will never be able to lead them to peace.

Time is short, we should move onward.

passages.title: A Walk to Remember
passages.text: This place is filled with indescribable horrors. To think... I was blind to all of this pain and suffering.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Pain
passages.text:
Darkness envelops us... the Light has gone from this place...

<Arkhaan mumbles to himself before noticing you are still talking to him.>

Arkhaan could not save them. Brothers. Sisters. Whispers twisted them. The Light cannot see them. It turns away from us.

Arkhaan failed.

<Arkhaan stares off into space.>

passages.title: Arkhaan's Pain
passages.text: <Arkhaan mutters incoherently to himself.>

passages.title: Arkhaan's Pain
passages.text: <The broken peers suspiciously at his surroundings, avoiding eye contact with you.>

passages.title: Lost Souls
passages.text:
Never in my life have I beheld such destruction... such misery. The very ground we walk on us paved with the bones of our allies.

Even now I can see the lost spirits of Alliance soldiers wandering the ruins.

I cannot leave this place without putting the souls of our brave soldiers to rest. We owe them... I owe them that much.

passages.title: Lost Souls
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. A peaceful rest is all we have to offer those who have made the ultimate sacrifice for the Alliance... for Azeroth.

passages.title: Something Different
passages.text:
Even the most bloodthirsty combatants eventually grow weary and turn their backs to the unending struggle of war. They seek a new way to test their mettle and destroy their enemies. 

Join the Brawl in progress and fight your opponents in a limited time event that tosses traditional rules aside.

passages.title: Something Different
passages.text: Even I could not foresee the strange ways in which you would fight your enemies <name>.

passages.title: Something Different
passages.text: Even I didn't see that coming.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Plan
passages.text:
Arkhaan remembers. He remembers something that will... yes... will save us.

Follow Arkhaan. Isolon calls! We will offer soft words to the Light. The Light will banish the darkness.

<Arkhaan eyes Alleria warily.>

Arkhaan will watch that one closely.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Plan
passages.text: I should have seen this coming.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Peril
passages.text:
Whatever called to him, it cannot have good intentions. We need to go in after him.

Before we step through this portal, <name>... ensure you are prepared to fight. The Void's influence is rarely peaceful.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Peril
passages.text: We must address this threat.

passages.title: Arkhaan's Peril
passages.text: As I said, the Void's influence is rarely peaceful. We must press on.

passages.title: A Personal Message
passages.text:
The time has come for me to travel to the Broken Shore and see, for myself, the place where my father died.

If I am to be the king my father was... the king Stormwind deserves, I must know firsthand the threat my people face.

Please tell my advisors that I've gone to the Broken Shore. If I told them myself they'd only try and stop me.

I'll wait for you at Deliverance Point. Farewell.

passages.title: A Personal Message
passages.text:
<Velen listens closely to your words as you tell him of King Anduin's plan.>

The Broken Shore is a dangerous place... far too dangerous to travel alone. But perhaps this journey is necessary for Anduin to find peace.

When the moment is right, I'll inform King Greymane of Anduin's departure. Until then, go and see that Anduin is not alone on the Broken Shore. I trust that you will return him safely.

passages.title: Sources of Darkness
passages.text:
I think I understand what he was trying to show us, <name>.

I feel a surge of power building ahead. They must be cultivating the Void, calling it here.

We need to stop them before they plunge this entire city into shadow. Find the source and cut it off by any means necessary.

Locus-Walker and I have unfinished business to attend to.

passages.title: Sources of Darkness
passages.text: Locus-Walker and I have some unfinished business to attend to.

passages.title: Sources of Darkness
passages.text: We buy time but nothing more.

passages.title: The Shadowguard Incursion
passages.text:
As you have surely gathered by now, a certain subset of my people have tragically succumbed to the call of the Void.

I had hoped to find more who possess the necessary strength of mind. I am disappointed to find such an utter lack of resistance.

It cannot be helped. To advance your cause, and mine, we will need to eradicate these weak-willed beings.

passages.title: The Shadowguard Incursion
passages.text: Walking the razor's edge does have risks, <name>.

passages.title: The Shadowguard Incursion
passages.text: It is good to know we can share a common goal. Perhaps I will find some use for your kind yet.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text:
adventurer,

We have won many battles against the Burning Legion, but it is time to end this war once and for all. 

Final preparations have begun to depart for Argus.

Make haste to Stormwind Harbor. A ship awaits you there to grant you and your allies passage to Azuremyst.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text: I'm glad you were among those called for the expedition to Argus. There will be plenty of fighting ahead.

passages.title: Two If By Sea
passages.text:
The Tomb of Sargeras was only the beginning. If we do not destroy the Legion utterly, they will return even stronger.

We will travel to Azuremyst by sea to avoid drawing unnecessary attention. The less time the Legion has to react to our assault, the better.

Just say the word when you are ready to depart.

passages.title: Two If By Sea
passages.text: May the Light protect us all this day.

passages.title: Light's Exodus
passages.text:
Prophet Velen and the others have gathered within the Vault of Lights below. There is an entrance just down this path.

We should find the Prophet at once so that we do not stall the invasion.

passages.title: Light's Exodus
passages.text: Thank the Light you have arrived.

passages.title: The Vindicaar
passages.text:
Everything is prepared for our assault. We need only establish the beacon to transport us to the vessel.

Once the beacon arrives, place your hand upon its surface to board the Vindicaar, the instrument of our retribution.

passages.title: The Vindicaar
passages.text: Today marks the beginning of the Legion's downfall.

passages.title: The Vindicaar
passages.text:
I have waited many years for this day.

Behold the triumph of the draenei, the Vindicaar!

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate
passages.text:
Even with the Sigil of Awakening in hand, the Crown cannot save us until it is whole.

That is why we must enter the Seat of the Triumvirate, even knowing that L'ura awaits us there.

This is a dire task, one that I would not ask if it were not completely necessary.

We will descend together. Come.

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate
passages.text: Such a task I cannot undertake alone. Your help is greatly appreciated, <name>.

passages.title: The Seat of the Triumvirate
passages.text: This is grave news indeed. It would be wise to follow Alleria's lead from here.

passages.title: Interesting Times
passages.text:
<name>, I don't mean to alarm you, but we may be experiencing some... temporal disturbances.

Have you ever heard the phrase 'I hope the past doesn't come back to haunt you?'

Come visit me in the Valley of Spirits and we can speak more.

passages.title: Interesting Times
passages.text: <name>, you're here. You must have received my letter.

passages.title: Interesting Times
passages.text:
<name>, I don't mean to alarm you, but we may be experiencing some... temporal disturbances.

Have you ever heard the phrase 'I hope the past doesn't come back to haunt you?'

Come visit me in the Stormwind Royal Library and we can speak more.

passages.title: Interesting Times
passages.text: <name>, you're here. You must have received my letter.

passages.title: Whispers of a Frightened World
passages.text:
Champion, Magni needs your help!

The Speaker has a message for you, perhaps from Azeroth herself. He seems to be having trouble understanding her, but I'm sure he can explain everything better.

He said he was in Sholazar Basin, in Northrend. He should be contacting you shortly.

passages.title: Whispers of a Frightened World
passages.text: Yes, <name>? What news do you bring?

passages.title: Whispers of a Frightened World
passages.text:
This warning is an ill omen indeed, <name>. It seems the fate of Azeroth is tied to that of Argus, the homeworld of the Legion.

We must uncover the Dark Titan's plan! I believe the Speaker's connection to the world soul will prove crucial to our efforts.

Stay vigilant, Huntmaster. We must trust in Magni's guidance... and Azeroth's as well.

passages.title: Shadow of the Triumvirate
passages.text:
Talgath's words carry more gravity than I think he knew. In an attempt to hurt me one final time, he has given us the answer.

The Crest of Knowledge is hidden away in the Seat of the Triumvirate, and it is not unguarded.

If my suspicions are correct, we may be facing a greater threat than any of us dared imagine.

A dark naaru.

Let us return to the Vindicaar. We will plan our next steps there.

passages.title: Shadow of the Triumvirate
passages.text:
I worried for L'ura, but this is... unthinkable.

How she must have suffered...

passages.title: Gathering Light
passages.text:
Alleria and I long for more time with our son, but we cannot afford to wait any longer, <name>. We must strike now.

The Army of the Light is scattered, but not defeated. Any survivors should have stayed near the crash site of the Xenedar. If there is any hope of victory, we must rally them and rescue Xe'ra.

With the pit lords dealt with, we should have a safer route to the Xenedar. Meet me in the krokul hovel as soon as you can.

passages.title: Gathering Light
passages.text:
We've secured a foothold. Good.

Now we take the fight to them!

passages.title: Sizing Up The Opposition
passages.text:
Turalyon was no doubt hoping for better news, but I fear I cannot provide it. Attempting to drive into the heart of the Legion now would cost us everything.

There must be another way. I do not know what it is, but I trust that we will find it.

Best not keep Turalyon waiting. We must move forward.

passages.title: Sizing Up The Opposition
passages.text: <Turalyon listens in grim silence.>

passages.title: Fire At Will
passages.text:
Look out there, the wings of the bats fill the sky. We must offer what ranged support we can, but our hands are full here.

It looks like the Legion has not yet destroyed all of the artillery batteries. If you can get to one, you should be able to show those flying fiends the Light.

passages.title: Fire At Will
passages.text: Those bats are always a nuisance to deal with. This method will be more... efficient, I believe.

passages.title: Fire At Will
passages.text: We may be grounded, but that does not mean they have to rule the skies!

passages.title: Bringing the Big Guns
passages.text:
Light's Judgment has a security feature to prevent it from falling into enemy hands. We can trigger its recall mechanism, which will teleport it back to a vessel.

With the Xenedar out of commission, the gun should recall to your ship instead. You can make good use of its firepower.

The process takes time, though, and will likely attract the Legion's attention. Be on your guard.

passages.title: Bringing the Big Guns
passages.text: <The panel is now pulsing a soft golden glow. According to Romuul, activating it should teleport the cannon to the Vindicaar.>

passages.title: The Best Prevention
passages.text:
If you've brought the High Exarch back to us, you are a welcome ally indeed.

More is needed of you. You see our soldiers out there, fighting against all odds? Defend them. Slay the enemy.

Strong words for a priest, perhaps, but every dead man'ari is one less blade at our throats.

Show them that the Light protects its chosen even as it scorches the unfaithful.

When you are finished, seek out Y'mera. She will have fewer troops, and more need of your abilities.

passages.title: The Best Prevention
passages.text: You fought well. The Light shines brighter, thanks to your efforts.

passages.title: The Day That Chromie Dies
passages.text:
Oh, <name>! I was just thinking about you! Talk about being at the right time in the right place!

I was just reviewing some aberrations in the timeways, when I discovered something... unexpected. Something not-so-great.

I'm going to die in the near future. Bad times.

I was just about to jump ahead and see if I can figure out why, how, who... but I'd feel better with |5<race> like you by my side. Care to join me?

passages.title: The Day That Chromie Dies
passages.text: I'm sure I just fall into a hole or something. This wouldn't be the first time!

passages.title: The Day That Chromie Dies
passages.text: That didn't go so great, did it? Maybe next time.

passages.title: Smoldering Chronoshard
passages.text: This shard of crystal is hot to the touch. The void creature that carried it wasn't a wielder of flame in any noticeable way, so perhaps the chronoshard is related to fire in some other way.

passages.title: Smoldering Chronoshard
passages.text: Yeeeeeowch! It's hot! What could it possibly... oh, yeah, that makes sense.

passages.title: Fel-Touched Chronoshard
passages.text: This shard of crystal is scarred with deep rivets of green, malevolent energy. Being held by a dreadlord will do that to you.

passages.title: Fel-Touched Chronoshard
passages.text: A chronoshard, you say? I know what to do with those.

passages.title: Gleaming Chronoshard
passages.text: This shard of crystal glitters with a metallic sheen. Based on Chromie's reaction, it may be used to connect you to another time and place.

passages.title: Gleaming Chronoshard
passages.text: Hand over that chronoshard, <name>. If you don't mind.

passages.title: Frozen Chronoshard
passages.text: This shard of crystal is encased in a thin, frigid layer of permafrost. It still has that distinctive lich smell to it.

passages.title: Frozen Chronoshard
passages.text: I hate when they get all chilly like this.

passages.title: Wanna Buy a Lamp?
passages.text: Ey dere, wanna buy a lamp? You be not regrettin' it.

passages.title: Wanna Buy a Lamp?
passages.text: I promise ya don' regret dis.

passages.title: Wanna Buy a Lamp?
passages.text: See, I told ya it be a great idea!

passages.title: I'll Take Those, Thanks!
passages.text: These coins, dey be vanishin' inta air ya say? Dat be soundin' perfect, as I have jus the fella ta give dem to.

passages.title: I'll Take Those, Thanks!
passages.text: Oh man, I can't wait to use these. I be thankin' you.

passages.title: I'll Take Those, Thanks!
passages.text: Dis be da best day. I'm going ta fleece dat Baron so hard his eyes be covered in more wool than a flock of sheep.

passages.title: The Mysterious, Magnificent Al'Abas
passages.text: I see you, puny mortal! I appreciate your concern for my lamp!

passages.title: The Mysterious, Magnificent Al'Abas
passages.text: The very world trembles, trembles with the weight of magic. Their pockets are full of it.

passages.title: The Mysterious, Magnificent Al'Abas
passages.text: You really don't see it? I can sense the magic in their pockets!

passages.title: In the Land of Magic
passages.text:
I think I see the problem. Your puny eyes are too weak to detect the mana-infused finery that these elves have spread throughout the land. They've been wearing jewelry the entire time, and you simply couldn't see it.

I propose a partnership, my newly minted associate. My lamp currently suffers from an embarrassing lack of magic and could always use more beautiful decorations. I propose a trade. I shall pierce this sinister veil, and you shall give me the spoils of your theft.

passages.title: In the Land of Magic
passages.text: Fantastic, simply fantastic. This will be a profitable partnership, my puny associate.

passages.title: Coins of Air
passages.text:
I would be much interested in these magical trinkets that reside in the pockets of the denizens of this land, and humbly offer my services in helping you acquire them, <name>. 

However, I sadly cannot pay you in the coin of this realm. What I can offer are ephemera - coins of purest air. They're better than nothing, though!

Carry my lamp with you. Drop the treasures you steal within, and I will grant you these coins. Perhaps the former owner of my lamp would have a use for them.

passages.title: Coins of Air
passages.text: I entrust you with my lamp. May our partnership be fruitful.

passages.title: Loyalty Is Its Own Reward
passages.text: I offer you a challenge, mortal. Obtain a thousand of my coins, and I believe that I can empower my lamp and the vision within.

passages.title: Loyalty Is Its Own Reward
passages.text: My goodness, already!?

passages.title: Loyalty Is Its Own Reward
passages.text: Yes, yes, YES! Do you see the power radiating from the lamp? I can sense objects of great power that were concealed even from my mighty eyes.

passages.title: Vengeance
passages.text:
The Army of the Light will not have fallen in vain.

Our forces will assault the main encampment while we destroy their siege weapon.

This will be but the beginning of our vengeance.

passages.title: Vengeance
passages.text: Until their weapon is no longer a threat, we are cornered here like vermin.

passages.title: Vengeance
passages.text: It seems we underestimated the Legion's cunning.

passages.title: Signs of Resistance
passages.text:
Our forces sustained heavy losses defending the Vindicaar, <name>. We require allies.

The Army of the Light was known to take in survivors of the Legion's crusade to bolster their ranks. We must do the same.

I sense the presence of the Legion slaves you freed nearby. I suspect that they have carved out a resistance against their masters.

I would appreciate your company, adventurer.

passages.title: Signs of Resistance
passages.text: This must be it.

passages.title: Soul Crystal
passages.text:
<The three shards combine neatly into a large crystal. Once reassembled, the image of a powerful lich appears above the crystal's surface.>

<The lich speaks:>

Keep the Ruby Shrinewardens occupied. I shall carry out our master's attack from within the great tree itself.

passages.title: Soul Crystal
passages.text: I think this is the spot.

passages.title: The Ancients' Wisdom
passages.text:
The three ancients left three clues:

"...the great nightmare..."

"...by the water..."

"...within the dragon's palm..."

Perhaps Chromie's attacker lies in the place the ancients describe?

passages.title: The Ancients' Wisdom
passages.text:
Based on the clues the ancients gave us, this must be the spot. It HAS to be!

Let's do this, <name>!

passages.title: Demonic Corestone
passages.text:
<Deep within the demonic corestone, the image of a dreadlord speaks ominously:>

Yes, master. It shall be done, at the exact time that you specified. The bronze dragon will see nothing. One shot from outside the Obsidian Dragonshrine is all I require.

passages.title: Demonic Corestone
passages.text: I'm not a big fan of dreadlords, but I think you and I can handle one if we stick together. You ready, <name>?

passages.title: Voidcallers' Scroll
passages.text:
<The scroll pieces combine to form a tattered, but readable message:>

The time is nigh. The invocation will take place above the azure shrine. The void will swallow the bronze dragon. Our master has spoken, and we obey.

passages.title: Voidcallers' Scroll
passages.text: I sense something... bad.

passages.title: The Light Mother
passages.text:
We must know for sure whether the Light Mother survived, <name>.

Xe'ra was weakened by sending her heart to Azeroth, but she is the prime naaru. She is the Light, and she cannot fade.

Let's head into the Xenedar and look for her. Light willing, she will return to guide us once more.

passages.title: The Light Mother
passages.text: Light Mother... you must have survived...

passages.title: The Light Mother
passages.text:
Light be praised! This was a dark day, and many lives were lost. 

But the Army endures. The Light Mother's prophecy will be fulfilled.

All is as it was meant to be.

passages.title: Light's Return
passages.text:
Xe'ra has been saved! We have won an important victory here.

The Light Mother should be back on the Vindicaar. No doubt she will want to speak with you. There is so much to explain...

Romuul should be able to teleport us back to the ship now. Let me know when you are ready.

passages.title: Light's Return
passages.text:
The Army endures. The Light Mother's prophecy will be fulfilled.

All is as it was meant to be.

passages.title: A Timely Summons from Shattrath
passages.text: The blazing star holds a peculiar alignment this cycle, calling out across the heavens. Seek out the sage Vormu in Shattrath City, and lend her your aid.

passages.title: A Timely Summons from Shattrath
passages.text: I foresee you will need the strength of many allies to walk this path.

passages.title: A Timely Summons from Shattrath
passages.text: Oh, is it time?

passages.title: Not-So-Humble Beginnings
passages.text:
Now we may begin our search for the Crown of the Triumvirate. We will start with the fragment Archimonde carried: the Sigil of Awakening.

To the east and north you will find all that remains of the greatest school of magic on Argus. It was there that Archimonde gained his mastery of the arcane. I can think of no other place he would stow his treasures.

It will be guarded, no doubt. We will leverage the expertise of Fareeya's forces here to follow this trail.

passages.title: Not-So-Humble Beginnings
passages.text: This place has its share of secrets. Thankfully, I know enough of them to get us started.

passages.title: Gatekeeper's Challenge: Tenacity
passages.text:
My master Archimonde was not known for his willingness to suffer indecision.

He preferred to teach by rewarding frustration with more frustration-- punishment with more punishment. Absolute conviction was required to succeed under him.

At the opposite end of the Conservatory you will find a large structure. Once inside, your goal is to overcome all the obstacles placed before you.

 Emerge unscathed and I will be forced to consider your will strong enough to proceed.

passages.title: Gatekeeper's Challenge: Tenacity
passages.text: Take all the time you need. Failure is an art, I hear.

passages.title: Gatekeeper's Challenge: Tenacity
passages.text: You may be worthy of the Conservatory's secrets, if you survive that long.

passages.title: A Non-Prophet Organization
passages.text:
I have complete faith that Velen is nearby. We would know if he had been captured.

All the same, we must not delay. The Legion has a vested interest in finding him after all he has done to resist them. I shudder to think what they might do, given the chance.

That is why I am going with you.

We will find Velen and help him track down the Crest of Knowledge. We must have faith in his mission or all will be lost.

passages.title: A Non-Prophet Organization
passages.text:
You came upon me in a moment of reflection.

<Velen peers at you with a tired expression.>

There is no time for such sentiment. We must press on.

passages.title: The Great Gnomeregan Run
passages.text:
Ready for the big race today, <name>?

Every year, gnomes from near and far gather to run all the way from Gnomeregan to Booty Bay!

It reminds us that no goal is too tall, even for us! Whether you run fast or slow, alone or with friends, you'll make it as long as you keep trying! So make sure to stretch, then get out there and show the world what we gnomes are made of!

passages.title: The Great Gnomeregan Run
passages.text: One small step for <name>, one giant leap for gnomekind!

passages.title: The Child of Light and Shadow
passages.text:
It is time, <name>.

Xe'ra is returned to us. We have Light's Heart. We have her Chosen One.

Come, let us restore her. Let us forge a bright new path against our foes.

Speak to me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: The Child of Light and Shadow
passages.text: Xe'ra...

passages.title: The Child of Light and Shadow
passages.text:
I did not expect this of Xe'ra. Nor could I have foreseen Illidan's reaction.

We must ensure these events do not crush the spirits of our allies.

passages.title: Smoke, Meat, and Pretty Flowers
passages.text:
Back of town's on lockdown, kid. And yes, I do have a key, but you're a stranger.

<Emery pats his pocket gingerly.>

Listen, I'd like to help you out. You've got an honest look to you. Fetch me some venison, some pipe tobacco, and a bundle o' yellow flowers, and I might be able to make an exception.

passages.title: Smoke, Meat, and Pretty Flowers
passages.text: You're not in a hurry, are you?

passages.title: Smoke, Meat, and Pretty Flowers
passages.text: The smoke and the meat are for me. The flowers, on the other hand, are for the kids at the orphanage down the street.

passages.title: Yeah, Definitely for the Kids
passages.text:
I don't know if you've ever seen Orphan Matron Meliana before, but she is a goddess come down to humble Lordaeron. Her hair, those cheekbones, and...

...and anyhow, these flowers are for the kids at the orphanage where she works. Tell Meliana that they're from me. For the kids.

passages.title: Yeah, Definitely for the Kids
passages.text: What's this?

passages.title: Yeah, Definitely for the Kids
passages.text:
These are from Emery, I assume?

<Meliana blushes.>

That dummy. Gotta admire his persistence, though...

passages.title: Holing Up
passages.text:
Did... did you see that? Prince Arthas just struck that person down in cold blood! Right in the middle of the street!

<Meliana regains her composure.>

I need to protect the children. Please, help us, visitors. I need a gun, bandages, and some venison jerky.

Children! Everybody, get into the house!

passages.title: Holing Up
passages.text: The children are priority one.

passages.title: Holing Up
passages.text: I don't know how long we'll need to stay holed up in the orphanage, but there's no way I'm letting the kids out while our prince walks the streets like some sort of madman.

passages.title: Fight Plague with Fire
passages.text:
One final request of you, stranger. I've seen what's happening outside, and I've heard about this "plague". I don't want to go down without a fight.

I have enough rum in the back of this bar to set this whole tavern on fire, but I don't have the tools to do it safely. Fetch me a flint and some rope, and I'll give you my key to the backstreets of Stratholme.

passages.title: Fight Plague with Fire
passages.text: Mad Prince or drooling zombie - nobody's going to take this bar away from me without a fight!

passages.title: Fight Plague with Fire
passages.text:
This'll do, <class>.

Take this key. You've earned it.

passages.title: For Emery
passages.text:
We do have plenty of food here, however. If you're braving the streets, please deliver this venison to that big dummy at the tavern.

Tell him it's from the kids.

passages.title: For Emery
passages.text: Say, what've you got there?

passages.title: For Emery
passages.text:
From the kids, you say?

<Emery struggles to conceal a smile as he pockets the jerky.>

passages.title: Locating the Longshot
passages.text:
We're going to need a bigger gun if we hope to free Xe'ra.

One of the other bunkers crashed closer to the Xenedar. If Baraat was on it, he will have already begun surveying the area. Perhaps he's found the main cannon of the ship.

If you head over that way, make sure he hasn't died, will you?

passages.title: Locating the Longshot
passages.text: We're under too much pressure here. And it's so close to us...

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text:
Oh! It's me! And <name>, was it? I remember this!

I seem to have found myself in the middle of a battle between the Horde and the Alliance, which wouldn't USUALLY be a big deal, except for that enormous cannon that seems to be trained on me anytime I try to fly away.

Think you could take it out for me?

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text: Any luck? I just need the Horde cannon taken disabled if I want to escape.

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text: You did it! Now hurry along... if I remember this correctly, you don't have much time left!

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text:
Oh! It's me! And <name>, was it? I remember this!

I seem to have found myself in the middle of a battle between the Horde and the Alliance, which wouldn't USUALLY be a big deal, except for that enormous cannon that seems to be trained on me anytime I try to fly away.

Think you could take it out for me?

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text: Any luck? I just need the Alliance cannon taken disabled if I want to escape.

passages.title: Sky Ablaze With Cannonfire
passages.text: You did it! Now hurry along... if I remember this correctly, you don't have much time left!

passages.title: Unsettled Power
passages.text:
The release of the energy previously trapped in the Nightwell has... complicated the influence of Aman'Thul scattered about the Broken Isles. Sadly, the results of my previous work have been invalidated, much like the contents of this vial.

I must understand what has caused this change! Please, bring me more samples so that I may continue my work. It goes without saying that you will be the beneficiary of any breakthroughs I may find.

passages.title: Unsettled Power
passages.text: The people of Suramar spent 10,000 years tapping into the latent energies of a dead titan. I wonder if any of them considered what might happen if they suddenly stopped doing so.

passages.title: Unsettled Power
passages.text:
I've managed to stabilize the mixture without diminishing its potency. No simple task, mind you, and I do hope you will appreciate the hard work it took to get this far.

I feel a great sense of unease regarding what might have been the source of this disruption. One would have expected that releasing Aman'thul's power would bring harmony, not chaos.

passages.title: The Spoiled Sample
passages.text:
<You pick up a vial of thick, inky liquid. Its contents react to your touch, boiling and popping furiously for a moment before settling down into a persistent glow. The substance resembles arcwine in this form, but the reaction reminds you of the breakdown of obliterum.

You tuck the vial in your bags. Someone in Dalaran familiar with the obliterum forge might know more.>

passages.title: The Spoiled Sample
passages.text:
This is worrisome. Gul'dan's defeat may have disrupted forces far more fundamental than anyone realized. 

Hmm... perhaps we can turn that to our advantage.

passages.title: Worried About My Friends
passages.text:
I've heard about some trouble over at the black dragonshrine. I know, I'm a bronze dragon, but still! I worry about them sometimes! They weren't ALWAYS so grumpy.

If you're going there anyways, would you mind taking care of... whatever's causing so much of a disturbance?

passages.title: Worried About My Friends
passages.text: I don't know what I'd do without my aspect. Must be tough.

passages.title: Worried About My Friends
passages.text:
It was a dreadlord? That's... unusual. I mean, I know we're in Northrend and everything, so risen skeletons aren't all that rare, but demons?

Oh well! Thanks for taking the time to calm my worries.

passages.title: The Dead Walk
passages.text:
Greetings, <race>. I know you are here in the service of the bronze, but I have a request of you.

The Ruby Dragonshrine is plagued by undead. My shrine's wardens were unprepared, and we risk losses if an intervention is not done quickly. Would you assist us?

passages.title: The Dead Walk
passages.text: Thank you for hearing my request.

passages.title: The Dead Walk
passages.text:
You have my thanks, <race>.

I know that you are here today in service to the Bronze Dragonflight. Perhaps this gift will aid you in your journeys.

passages.title: Darkness in the Ley
passages.text: A strange, dark disturbance perturbs the ley lines in my flight's dragonshrine. Do you have the time to investigate?

passages.title: Darkness in the Ley
passages.text: <Kalecgos eyes you cautiously.>

passages.title: Darkness in the Ley
passages.text: Your assistance is appreciated.

passages.title: Darkened Dreams
passages.text: The ancients at the Emerald Dragonshrine suffer in their dreams. With Ysera gone, I am shorthanded and unable to investigate the matter myself. Would you help me cleanse the nightmare from the Emerald Dragonshrine?

passages.title: Darkened Dreams
passages.text: I appreciate you taking the time to listen to my concern, <race>.

passages.title: Darkened Dreams
passages.text: With your assistance, the ancients have fallen back into their restful slumber. Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text:
adventurer,

We have won many battles against the Burning Legion, but it is time to end this war once and for all. 

Final preparations have begun to depart for Argus.

Make haste to Bladefist Bay. A ship awaits you there to grant you and your allies passage to Azuremyst.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text: I knew you would be among those called to fight. It will be an honor to fight by your side.

passages.title: What Might Have Been
passages.text:
<Velen continues to stare at the statue as he speaks.>

Thousands of years ago, when I was young, I made a choice.

A choice that allowed my world to fall to ruin. A choice that made my people exiles. A choice that forever separated me from my beloved brothers.

<Velen shakes his head.>

I cannot leave, not yet. Not until I have had a chance to reflect.

passages.title: What Might Have Been
passages.text: Memory roots me in place, more surely than the heaviest stone.

passages.title: What Might Have Been
passages.text:
<Prophet Velen peers solemnly at you.>

Thank you.

passages.title: Across the Universe
passages.text:
Talgath. There was a time I called him an ally, a friend.

I put my trust in him when it came time to leave Argus. I asked him to call out to the others who would join me.

I gave him all that he needed to betray me and slaughter my followers.

I do not know what brought this hatred to lurk in his heart, but his machinations repeatedly forced my people to flee world after world. He made it his mission to hunt us across the universe.

This must end, <name>. Talgath must die.

passages.title: Across the Universe
passages.text: It is done. This one wrong, of many, is finally set to rights.

passages.title: REUSE ME
passages.text: Hey you've finished part 1 of the Velen arc. Stop here. Nothing past this point is done.

passages.title: Two If By Sea
passages.text:
The draenei have crafted a vessel to take us to Argus safely. They are gathering the invasion force on Azuremyst Isle as we speak. 

We will join them there by sea. The Legion is no doubt keeping a close eye on the gateway to their world. We must retain the element of surprise.

Let me know when you are ready.

passages.title: Two If By Sea
passages.text: May the Light protect us all this day.

passages.title: Conservation of Magic
passages.text:
I have an idea. This construct will be of use to us. We simply need to jolt it awake.

We once stored great quantities of energy in conduits throughout the Conservatory. They are still functional, but only just.

Take this.

<Y'mera hands you a brightly glowing crystal.>

It will provide a small burst of magic that should help stabilize an erratic conduit. I think I have enough stored for eight or so.

Stabilizing a few should allow us to access the whole network.

passages.title: Conservation of Magic
passages.text:
Yes, excellent. The conduits are back online.

The construct however is proving a little more difficult to awaken than I had hoped.

passages.title: The Longest Vigil
passages.text:
It was a good thing we sought two sources of energy. Even with the conduits active, the construct has not stirred.

It has likely been inactive a long while. Perhaps as long as Eredath has floated above Argus.

What a long, lonely vigil it must have been.

<Y'mera is silent for a moment as she peers at the construct.>

Go ahead and jostle it a little. That combined with one last burst of magic ought to do the trick.

passages.title: The Longest Vigil
passages.text: Prepare yourself, stranger.

passages.title: The Speaker Calls
passages.text:
Magni sent for you to meet him in the Krokul Hovel. He has found something that he believes could help us overcome the Legion's infinite armies.

We need every advantage we can muster if we are to see this war through. You should seek him out.

passages.title: The Speaker Calls
passages.text: Thank ye fer joinin' me, lad. There's somethin' ye have to see.

passages.title: Visions of Torment
passages.text:
I've been hearin' whispers ever since we got to Argus. They're just like Azeroth's, only... they ain't hers.

I'm convinced that Argus has a titan of its own that's reachin' out to us!

The broken have a relic stowed away that's darn near holy to 'em. Hatuun says they hear whispers from it... I think it might have some sort o' link to Argus itself!

It's just in this chamber. Let's see what we can learn.

passages.title: Visions of Torment
passages.text: I know, I know, it's a lot to ask, but we need all the help we can get lad!

passages.title: Visions of Torment
passages.text: I don't know how Sargeras managed to raise Aggramar, but it's bad news for us, believe you me.

passages.title: Dire News
passages.text:
Azeroth was right in sendin' us here, <name>. We have to stop whatever it is Sargeras is plannin', or we may not have a home left to save when this is all over.

Ye should go back to Turalyon and let him know what ye've seen. I'll stay here and see if I can't glean anything else that might help us.

passages.title: Dire News
passages.text: What did Magni have to show you?

passages.title: Storming the Citadel
passages.text:
We have already secured ground near Nath'raxas Hold. It is one of the Legion's chief military fortifications on Argus.

Striking it now, and hard, may be our only opportunity to tip the scales in our favor.

passages.title: Storming the Citadel
passages.text: If we do not act quickly, the demons stationed here are more than enough to overwhelm us.

passages.title: Bert's Bots
passages.text:
If I'm going to clean up Gnomeregan, I've got to be ready to battle all manner of rat, roach, and potentially even the dreaded mutant rat-roach.

What I'm saying is that I need to put these bots to the test! A real, live-action field demo.

Are your pets up for a code review?

passages.title: Bert's Bots
passages.text: Better bots, by Bert!

passages.title: Bert's Bots
passages.text: I'm going to have to go back to the drawing board!

passages.title: An Argus Roper
passages.text: My warriors stand no chance against even the smallest of the Legion's forces without our Cragscalers. If you can capture a few and bring them here, my warriors can better defend our people.

passages.title: An Argus Roper
passages.text: We need those talbuk!

passages.title: An Argus Roper
passages.text: With these new steeds our forces stand a chance.

passages.title: Heralds of Apocalypse
passages.text:
We've been presented with a rare opportunity.

Our scouts have spotted two shivarra priestesses in the western fel pools enhancing the Legion's war effort.

The inner circle of Sargeras' chosen never leave the walls of Antorus. If we take them out, we might be able to sow fear among those closest to the Dark Titan.

passages.title: Heralds of Apocalypse
passages.text: Impressive. Without the shivarra bolstering their strength we just might stand a chance.

passages.title: Dark Machinations
passages.text:
Eredar are adept at manipulating the fel that courses through this world. Those who do not shape it into living weapons build other armaments, like the Spires of Woe.

The spires will make it difficult for even a small force to penetrate the main stronghold. We must dismantle enough of them to clear the way before we advance upon it.

passages.title: Dark Machinations
passages.text: We do not have time for failure.

passages.title: Dark Machinations
passages.text: No war is won by a single act, but without the spires protecting them the rest of the hold will fall as well.

passages.title: Lord of the Spire
passages.text:
Lord Nath'raxas rules over this hold as thanks for his role in delivering Argus to the Legion many years ago.

Make no mistake, he is powerful, but he has also grown overconfident in his seat.

Take advantage of his hubris and make use of the warframe's firepower while you can. We will storm the courtyard shortly!

passages.title: Lord of the Spire
passages.text: By the Light...

passages.title: Limited Supplies
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. It's good to see a fellow alchemist again.

I've been supplying our camp with necessary potions to deal with the demons, but lately I've been running low on supplies. Normally when scouting parties go out, they return with empty vials, but as of late fewer have been returning.

I try to recycle as much as I can, so you see, those vials are precious to me. If you'd be willing to go out and retrieve them, I could show you what I've been making to help combat the demons.

passages.title: Limited Supplies
passages.text: How goes the search? Any luck on finding my vials?

passages.title: Limited Supplies
passages.text:
You've found some! These will certainly be enough to get us by for a good while longer.

As promised, here is a recipe for one of the potions I brew to help in our fight against the Legion.

passages.title: Tracking the Trackers
passages.text:
<name>, have I told you about my tracking potion? Our scouts use it to track demons, especially their "fiends".

Those particular creatures tend to consume the astral glory in the area, making it difficult to replenish our stores of the herb.

If you could help thin their numbers out, it would greatly help us from having to search elsewhere for supplies. You can find many of them in the Annihilan Pits.

I could also teach you the recipe for this potion for your effort.

passages.title: Tracking the Trackers
passages.text:
You're an honorable ally, <name>. Thank you for helping us.

As promised, here is the recipe for the potion.

passages.title: Chromie
passages.text:
<name>. Is that you?

I'm convinced that something unusual has happened in the timelines. I need your help!

Come find me at Wyrmrest Temple, in Dragonblight, and I'll show you.

passages.title: Chromie
passages.text: Any luck traversing the timeways?

passages.title: Chromie
passages.text: Despite her troubles, this has been a welcome reminder that, although our battle with the Legion remains at the forefront of our concerns, the rest of the world does not simply wait for us.

passages.title: Youthful Resistance
passages.text: <As you begin to gather the flowers, you realize that some of the younger blooms are still resistant to your approach and refuse to yield. Perhaps Funen might know more about how to handle the herb in its adolescent stages.>

passages.title: Youthful Resistance
passages.text:
Indeed, the newer blooms are particularly stubborn and would rather give up their life than live in servitude to those who pick them.

To handle the herb in this form, one must coax the herb into submitting, as it can't quite fully read the intentions of those who wish to gather it.

passages.title: The Heart of It
passages.text:
<Having handled astral glory for a while now, you've picked up on something interesting about its roots. Tightly wound in a cocoon, small flecks of light permeate through the cracks creating a shimmering effect.>

<Perhaps Funen might be able to expand on the nature of these lights.>

passages.title: The Heart of It
passages.text:
I see the glory has come to trust you fully. It is now exposing its heart to you.

Focus your intentions here and you will gather it in its entirety.

passages.title: Don't Just Pick At It
passages.text:
<Even though you've learned to expose the ore, large chunks of it still seem to be embedded in the surrounding rock. Picking those pieces away may not result in the pure form of empyrium that you're looking for.>

<Perhaps Khamir can show you a way to remove the ore from these sections of the seam.>

passages.title: Don't Just Pick At It
passages.text:
Empyrium seams can be tricky in that regard. The ore is very good at interweaving itself into the surrounding elements.

I've found that striking those areas with the shaft of the pick loosens the empyrium's grip on it, so that when you pick at it, the rock should just fall away.

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text:
<name>, I was hoping to ask you for a small favor. The naval fleet at Stormwind Harbor have been requesting large amounts of felslate to help construct supplies for their ships.

I'm pretty busy here coordinating the gathering efforts and all my couriers are still out. I was wondering if you wouldn't mind taking that shipment over there to them?

I heard there's a portal to Stormwind in the Greyfang Enclave here in Dalaran so it shouldn't be a long trip or anything.

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text: Did Alard send you?

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text:
Whaddya got for me?

More felslate, fantastic! This stuff weighs a ton, and is perfect for anchors.

I see you have the arms of a blacksmith. Perhaps you'd like ta have a hand at making a few anchors as well, eh?

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text:
<name>, I was hoping to ask you for a small favor. The naval fleet at Bilgewater Harbor have been requesting large amounts of felslate to help construct supplies for their ships.

I'm pretty busy here coordinating the gathering efforts and all my couriers are still out. I was wondering if you wouldn't mind taking that shipment over there to them?

I heard there's a portal to Orgrimmar in the Windrunner's Sanctuary here in Dalaran so it shouldn't be a long trip or anything.

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text: Did Vridiel send you?

passages.title: Weigh Anchor
passages.text:
More felslate, fantastic! This stuff weighs a ton, and is perfect for anchors.

I see you have the arms of a blacksmith. Perhaps you'd like to have a hand at making a few anchors as well, eh?

passages.title: A Feast for Our Kin
passages.text:
Ah, the Highmountain tauren. They have been our allies ever since we felled the Legion.

Are you interested in hearing how they joined the Horde? It is quite the tale!

It all began with Baine Bloodhoof and Mayla Highmountain. Baine was hosting a great feast in Thunder Bluff to welcome the Highmountain tauren...

passages.title: A Feast for Our Kin
passages.text:
Welcome, <name>.

Mayla speaks of you as a trusted ally. Your presence will surely help convince her of the merits of joining the Horde.

passages.title: Shadow Over Thunder Bluff
passages.text:
A dark force has descended upon us. I refuse to believe that the Highmountain are behind it.

The cacophony out there is disturbingly familiar. Could it be... 

No! The minions of the Old Gods are attacking! We must fight for Thunder Bluff, <name>!

passages.title: Shadow Over Thunder Bluff
passages.text: For the Old Gods to manifest even these fledgling minions is troubling.

passages.title: Shadow Over Thunder Bluff
passages.text:
The Old Gods are known for subversion and duplicity. To attack so brazenly...

Whatever they seek, they want it badly.

passages.title: The Wrench Calls
passages.text: <name>, Didi the Wrench is looking for you back in Dalaran. You might want to see what she's working on. Pretty fancy stuff from what I heard.

passages.title: The Wrench Calls
passages.text:
<name>, you came at the perfect time. I just finished creating this Ionized Geographical Recorder.

Now, here's how you're gonna use it...

passages.title: Looming Over Me
passages.text:
When I rallied to the Xenedar, I left behind a valuable tool. My lightweave loom. Without it, I'm forced to labor for much longer to make garments of power for our allies.

But you are powerful, much more so than I. Perhaps you could do me a favor. Should you happen to be in the Arinor Gardens, could you retrieve my loom and return it to me?

I'd be more than willing to share my knowledge of sewing lightweave with you.

passages.title: Looming Over Me
passages.text: Any luck in finding my loom?

passages.title: Looming Over Me
passages.text:
You have no idea the time you've just saved me, <name>. You have my utmost gratitude.

And as promised, here is my most coveted design.

passages.title: Return to Highmountain
passages.text:
Spiritwalker Ebonhorn remains in great danger. He and Mayla have returned to Highmountain, but I believe they still need our aid.

Let us journey to Thunder Totem and do whatever we can to mend Ebonhorn. Perhaps our deeds will strengthen the bond between our peoples.

passages.title: Return to Highmountain
passages.text:
Ebonhorn has spoken of ancient wards that must be maintained in Highmountain. Wards that hold back a great darkness.

This may be tied to the evil that grips him now.

We must hope that Spiritwalker Graysky can tell us more.

passages.title: A Floating Ruin
passages.text:
We knew the Legion to be a formidable foe, but recent events demonstrate that we do not possess the necessary strength to continue. We have come too far to fail at this critical moment.

I know of a relic on Eredath, my ancient home, that may be our salvation. We must take the Vindicaar beyond the surface of Argus, to the floating ruin suspended above us.

Perhaps there we will find the salvation we so desperately need.

passages.title: A Floating Ruin
passages.text:
<Velen's gaze is drawn to the ruins spread out before him.>

I am home.

passages.title: The Sigil of Awakening
passages.text:
This relic is too powerful to keep it out in the open.

We must return to the Vindicaar at once. The Prophet will know what to do.

I did want to thank you, <name>. Without you this would not be possible. Quoram would have ensured I never got near the Sigil. Perhaps some day I will share that story with you.

passages.title: The Sigil of Awakening
passages.text: Did you recover the Sigil of Awakening?

passages.title: The Sigil of Awakening
passages.text: We are that much closer to restoring the Crown of the Triumvirate to its former glory.

passages.title: Shadow of the Sepulcher
passages.text:
Ebonhorn spoke of another ward safeguarding the lands of the Skyhorn tribe. Somewhere close to the Sepulcher of the Sky, he said. It was there that this "Darkness" once manifested.

Meet me there, <name>. I will show you how to walk in the memories of a great Skyhorn hero.

passages.title: Shadow of the Sepulcher
passages.text: The next ward is nearby. I can sense it.

passages.title: Huln's Mountain
passages.text:
We have made progress reactivating the wards, but more must be done.

I sense Ebonhorn's struggle. Though he fights with all his strength, he is slipping away. Should this "Darkness" emerge into our realm, I fear our friend will be lost.

Ebonhorn spoke of another ward somewhere within Snowblind Mesa. Meet me there, so that I might guide you along another journey into the memories of the past.

passages.title: Huln's Mountain
passages.text:
Do you sense it, <name>? Such strength... such courage.

The echo of Huln Highmountain's spirit is all around us.

passages.title: Fragment of the Past
passages.text:
<Your eye is drawn to the faint glow of the crystalline fragment. Examining the piece, you trace the partial pattern of a rune that had been inscribed upon its surface.

The fragment appears similar to the argunite crystals used by the Army of the Light to power their armaments. Could this crystal have belonged to the eredar who fought to escape Argus so long ago?

Perhaps Captain Fareeya would be able to tell you more about the crystal.>

passages.title: Fragment of the Past
passages.text:
<Fareeya examines the crystal fragment.>

This is old... very old. It is a piece of an elaborate key, the sort my people use to secure our most prized and sacred places.

I wonder...

passages.title: Visions of Fear
passages.text:
I've done it, <lad/lass>. I've reached him again! 

Oh, but it's so painful. So painful! He's not doin' well, not one bit!

You'll have to listen on in with me to understand.

passages.title: Visions of Fear
passages.text: It's a lot to take in, I know, but it might help us while we can still be helped.

passages.title: Visions of Fear
passages.text: The Pantheon has been dead for thousands of years... I fear this plan has been in the works for a very, very long time.

passages.title: The Speaker Listens
passages.text:
Magni has sent for you in Krokul Hovel once more. He seems to have made a new breakthrough in trying to reach Argus.

I suggest you find him immediately. His last vision foretold Aggramar's coming, and there is still so much we do not know of Sargeras' plans.

passages.title: The Speaker Listens
passages.text: Thank ye fer joinin' me, lad. There's somethin' ye have to see.

passages.title: The Speaker Seeks
passages.text:
Our forces are ready for battle, but we still do not know where Eonar's spirit lies.

You should seek Magni out at once and see if you can find her while we still have a chance. If she falls, nothing we muster will be able stand against Sargeras.

passages.title: The Speaker Seeks
passages.text: Ye came just in the nick of time.

passages.title: Fate of the Life-Binder
passages.text:
I don't even want to think about what happens if Aggramar can find Eonar's spirit before we do. The fate of far more'n Azeroth may hinge on her safety.

Let Turalyon know what we saw right away. We're going to need to bring all we can to bear to save her.

passages.title: Visions of Another
passages.text:
Whoever's tryin' to reach us now might give us the information we need to find Eonar.

We need to see what's goin' on right away!

passages.title: Visions of Another
passages.text: Eonar's still out there somewhere, but I don't know how much longer she'll last.

passages.title: Visions of Another
passages.text: Our answer lies in the Legion's own portal network in the heart of Antorus.

passages.title: We Have a Problem
passages.text:
We have a problem, <name>. The Legion has come to Eredath.

When you claimed the Sigil it was as if we announced our presence to all of Argus. The eyes of Antorus are firmly upon us.

Just wait. It gets worse.

Velen took Captain Fareeya and her forces into the Arinor Gardens area to search for the Crest of Knowledge. To my knowledge, they are all now behind enemy lines.

Come with me to the Conservatory. We need to bring Velen and the others back before it is too late.

passages.title: We Have a Problem
passages.text: There is no room for error here, <name>.

passages.title: Talgath's Forces
passages.text:
I must continue to seek the Crest of Knowledge, my friend. Nothing short of the whole Crown of the Triumvirate can turn the tide in the battle we face.

Talgath's forces stand between us and that goal. I will need you to clear a path.

We can let nothing stand in our way. Not even Talgath.

passages.title: Talgath's Forces
passages.text: <Velen does not seem to notice your presence.>

passages.title: The Darkness
passages.text:
For thousands of years, the Darkness was held at bay. The wards stood... protecting Highmountain.

Now they are gone, and evil is free once more.

The Darkness that haunted our dreams... that even the kobolds spoke of only in frightened whispers... has come.

Uul'gyneth, herald of the Old Gods, paves the way for his masters. Unless we stand together and defeat him, all is lost.

You must hold nothing back, champion. None of us can.

passages.title: The Darkness
passages.text:
I cannot put into words how much you have done for us this day, or how grateful I am to have you as an ally.

You have our thanks, hero. You have MY thanks.

I owe you a great debt for this.

passages.title: How Fares Ebonhorn?
passages.text:
Three of the ancient wards are restored. The mountain is not yet secure, but we may have done enough to break Ebonhorn free of the shadows gripping him.

Let us return to Thunder Totem and see how he fares. Hopefully Ebonhorn can tell us more about what is happening with the Necrodark and the insidious master they serve.

passages.title: How Fares Ebonhorn?
passages.text:
I am myself again, <name>.

You and Graysky have freed me from the grasp of the Old Gods. Had I remained in that state for much longer, I would have been lost.

passages.title: Into the Night
passages.text:
What we do this day, we do for Azeroth. For the countless souls lost to the Legion's foul crusade.

Once you are ready we will take the Vindicaar into the very heart of the Legion.

Argus awaits.

passages.title: Into the Night
passages.text: We must act quickly!

passages.title: Nath'raxas Hold: Preparations
passages.text:
One of two fates await krokul prisoners taken to Nath'raxas Hold. Consume the fel, and become a willing soldier in the infinite army, or be mutated into a disfigured abomination. An ur'zul.

While the Army of the Light occupies the Legion's attention, I am presented with an opportunity to save my people. I ask for your aid.

Before we begin, your forces must be adequately equipped.

passages.title: Nath'raxas Hold: Preparations
passages.text: Soon, the krokul will raid Nath'raxas Hold. My people are anxious to begin.

passages.title: Relics of the Ancient Eredar
passages.text:
I failed Arkhaan. I won't fail again. 

If there is to be any hope of freeing the krokul, the ethereal threat must be removed from Eredath. L'ura has been vanquished, but the void clings heavily near the Shadowguard Incursion.

Before we commence, ensure your forces are protected from the shadow. Your champions should seek ancient eredar armaments in the nearby ruins.

passages.title: Relics of the Ancient Eredar
passages.text: The voidcallers roaming the Shadowguard Incursion must be extinguished. Your people are sufficiently armed for the coming encounter.

passages.title: Duskcloak Problem
passages.text:
Here in this forest, species of talbuk and panthara still roam. However, the balance has been disrupted and now the panthara risk hunting the talbuk to extinction. To ensure their survival, we must decrease the number of panthara.

Do not let their suffering linger. A swift death is the most merciful.

passages.title: Duskcloak Problem
passages.text: Keeping balance within the forest ensures its longevity.

passages.title: The Wranglers
passages.text:
Great evil exists on Argus and our forests house some of the worst of it. My wranglers are at the edge of the forest and are waiting for reinforcements. That would be you.

Seek out Lead Rider Jerek, he will tell you more.

passages.title: The Wranglers
passages.text: I fear the forest may be lost.

passages.title: A Stranger's Plea
passages.text:
My people... enslaved...

Beaten... within death's grasp...

<The cowled figure weakly raises his arm, handing you a small liquid skin.>

Help... us...

passages.title: A Stranger's Plea
passages.text:
A cowled figure... and it did not attack you?

Most curious.

passages.title: The Spires of Home
The Hand of Fate
passages.text:
Ever since the Legion invaded the Exodar, the draenei have been hard at work preparing to return to Argus. At long last they have a vessel that can take us there.

With the way to that dreadful world open, we simply could not ask for a better opportunity to strike. Prophet Velen called for you quite specifically to join the assault force.

You should make your way to Stormwind Harbor right away. Arrangements have been made for a ship there to take you to Azuremyst.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text: I'm glad you were among those called for the expedition to Argus. There will be plenty of fighting ahead.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text:
Ever since the Legion invaded the Exodar, the draenei have been hard at work preparing to return to Argus. At long last they have a vessel that can take us there.

With the way to that dreadful world open, we simply could not ask for a better opportunity to strike. Prophet Velen called for you quite specifically to join the assault force.

You should make your way to Bladefist Bay right away. Arrangements have been made for a ship there to take you to Azuremyst.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text: It seems fate has conspired to bring us together, <name>.

passages.title: The Hand of Fate
passages.text: I knew you would be among those called to fight. It will be an honor to fight by your side.

passages.title: Invasion Point Offensive
passages.text: The invasion points are key to cutting off Legion reinforcements to Argus. Defeating their armies within the lesser portals will allow us to assault larger invasion points and extinguish the Legion presence within.

passages.title: Invasion Point Offensive
passages.text: The offensive continues.

passages.title: Invasion Point Offensive
passages.text: The Legion's defeat is at hand.

passages.title: Woah, Nelly!
passages.text:
<name>, you have my thanks. My Wranglers should be able to take it from here. If I can ask one more favor, would you pass a message to Chieftain Hatuun? Tell him the forest is secure once again. I'm sure he will reward you for all of your effort.

I'll loan you one of my fastest Cragscalers for the trip. Make sure to look both ways before crossing that path outside this forest, there's a giant Legion Obliterator that patrols there. Good luck!

passages.title: Woah, Nelly!
passages.text: The Wranglers are essential for our survival here. Any assistance you have given them must be repaid.

passages.title: Strange Ecologies
Quest
An Offering of Light
passages.text:
I sense it. The nobility in Xe'ra's heart. Her relentless defiance of the Legion. Let this be her legacy.

In building the Vindicaar, we fashioned the Netherlight Crucible to harness the tremendous powers at play on Argus. I believe Xe'ra's essence is one key to that potential.

Yet the Light alone is not enough. Without balance, there can be no harmony, no cohesion.

Infuse this essence into the crucible, champion. It is the first step in unlocking the strength needed to end the Burning Crusade.

passages.title: An Offering of Light
passages.text:
An important first step, <name>.

If we can bring balance to the Netherlight Crucible, I believe it will make your weapon even more powerful.

passages.title: An Offering of Shadow
passages.text:
Can you sense it, <name>? The darkness within this essence is palpable.

In the past, I might have shunned such power, even denied its very existence. But what have we learned throughout our long struggle, if not that Light and shadow must coexist?

This may prove to be exactly what we need to bring balance to the Netherlight Crucible. To give us the edge we need against the Legion.

Infuse this essence into the crucible, champion. Draw one step closer to realizing your weapon's full potential.

passages.title: An Offering of Shadow
passages.text: Light and shadow... forces that shape our very existence.

passages.title: An Offering of Shadow
passages.text: Ah, yes. Balance is key, just as the Prophet said.

passages.title: Take the Edge Off
passages.text:
The demons streaming out of Antorus equip themselves at Felfire Armory. We need to deny those weapons. Will your <class>s fight alongside the Army of the Light once again?

Before the assault, gather materials. My smiths will craft your soldiers more powerful armor. The Legion won't give up Felfire without a fight.

passages.title: Take the Edge Off
passages.text: Make your preparations, <name>.

passages.title: Take the Edge Off
passages.text: One step closer to defeating the Legion.

passages.title: Commander's Downfall
passages.text: A champion of the Legion is vulnerable within an invasion point! Track it down and destroy it before it can return to fight on Argus.

passages.title: Commander's Downfall
passages.text: The Legion must fall.

passages.title: Commander's Downfall
passages.text: Their commanders fall before us!

passages.title: Securing Krokuun
passages.text: Legion patrols are an ever-present threat. Eradicate demon commanders you encounter, and I will grant you a ridgestalker guide.

passages.title: Void Extract
passages.text:
The void calls to its own. 

When they are destroyed, powerful creatures of shadow leave behind vast amounts of undiluted void. It's lure is powerful enough to draw out the noxious influence polluting my brethren. Not all survive the purge, but the alternative is worse than death - you've seen the voidscarred roaming Oranaar.

Destroy a powerful agent of shadow, collect its essence, and bring it to me. I will use it draw out the corruption.

passages.title: Beneath Oronaar
passages.text: The krokul we found beneath Oranaar did not wish to leave. Could you speak with him, <name>? Convince him to board the Vindicaar.

passages.title: Beneath Oronaar
passages.text: I told the others; I will not abandon my people. I must remain here, but maybe you can help? I have discovered a way to purge the shadow from the void-addled.

passages.title: Lightforged Beacon: City Center
passages.text:
Hail, friend!

Captain Fareeya sent us ahead to secure this area. We were just about to call down a beacon and report back to the Vindicaar.

We would be honored if you would help us complete our mission.

The signal beacon just needs a light touch. The Grand Artificer will do the rest.

passages.title: Lightforged Beacon: City Center
passages.text: Grand Artificer Romuul is a reliable soul. We would be lost on this planet without him.

passages.title: Lightforged Beacon: City Center
passages.text:
This beacon will be added to the Navigation Console.

A contingent of the Army of the Light will remain to hold this location for future use.

passages.title: Forging a Key to the Past
passages.text:
The armory key fragments are gathered, and the dendrite clusters should provide just enough power to reforge the key.

This should not take long... assuming it works. It has been a long time since I made one of these!

passages.title: Forging a Key to the Past
passages.text: Bear with me as I finish my work.

passages.title: Forging a Key to the Past
passages.text:
Success! It is nice to know I haven't lost my touch.

Here you go, <name>; it is as good as new.

passages.title: The Broken Blacksmith
passages.text:
<class>, I believe this may be a piece of the key to the Armory of the Triumvirate. We locked it behind us as we made our escape from Argus. The last time I saw it, my second in command, Atalaa, was leading a force to secure the armory. That was so long ago...

I cannot be certain, but there may be another who would know. The smith who forged the key was called Gaal. With the reports of broken surviving on Krokuun, he may still live.

passages.title: The Broken Blacksmith
passages.text:
I am glad to hear Fareeya is well.

She is right... this is a fragment of the armory key I forged her so long ago.

passages.title: The Many-Faced Devourer
passages.text:
<The scroll's runes shift to a more intelligible form.>

An effigy. The Many-Faced One requires it.

Steal from the Imps. Steal from the Fiends. Steal from the Ur'zul.

He comes.

passages.title: Supplying Krokuun
passages.text:
This desolate place offers little for my people. Every hour is spent scraping together enough to survive. If I had more supplies, I could offer you another ridgestalker.

What say you, offworlder?

passages.title: Supplying Krokuun
passages.text:
This desolate place offers little for my people. Every hour is spent scraping together enough to survive. If I had more resources, I could offer you a ridgestalker.

I can only part with a Krokul-Ridgestalker for this few resources once per week. Next week, I will offer you this trade again.

passages.title: Supplying Krokuun
passages.text: What say you, offworlder?

passages.title: Void Inoculation
passages.text:
All entities touched by shadow leave behind traces of void when they are defeated, If you collect enough in your travels through the city, return to me, and I will distill it into its undiluted form. 

We can save more of my kin.

passages.title: Void Inoculation
passages.text:
If you bring the necessary supplies, I can begin the distillation process, <name>.

I can only free one of the Void-Touched with this few resources once per week.

passages.title: Void Inoculation
passages.text: Another soul freed from the cruelty of the void.

passages.title: Supplying the Antoran Campaign
passages.text: The Legion requires raw materials from conquered words to fuel their crusade. Travel through Legion portals, destroy demons you encounter, and deny them the resources required to maintain their war machine.

passages.title: Supplying the Antoran Campaign
passages.text:
The campaign against the Legion has taxed our existing resources heavily. Bring me supplies and I will place a lightforged under your command.

I can only spare a lightforged for this few resources once per week.

passages.title: Supplying the Antoran Campaign
passages.text: A lightforged soldier can wade through a sea of demons. They will serve you well.

passages.title: Sizing Up The Opposition
passages.text:
No doubt your High Exarch will fret at the news that we lack the resources to assault Antorus. He is not used to believing his vaunted Army of the Light to be inadequate.

His pride is no concern of mine. While he plots a new strategy, I will bathe the ground in demon blood.

Go. There is much to be done before we can achieve our final victory.

passages.title: Sizing Up The Opposition
passages.text: <Turalyon listens in grim silence.>

passages.title: Telogrus Rift
passages.text:
Umbric and his blood elves were cast out of their home for their pursuit of understanding.

I know the dangers of the void better than most. We should lend them our aid and ensure they don't do anything too foolhardy.

This rift will take us to their current location. I hope we are not too late to help them.

passages.title: Telogrus Rift
passages.text: Former blood elves willing to pledge to our cause. This is better than I dared hope.

passages.title: Immortal Ace
passages.text:
<The scroll's runes shift to a more intelligible form.>

An effigy. The Many-Faced One requires it.

Steal from the Imps. Steal from the Fiends. Steal from the Ur'zul.

He comes.

passages.title: Paragon of Argussian Reach
passages.text: Your allies among the Argussian Reach have requested your presence. They wish to reward you for your continued efforts on their behalf.

passages.title: Paragon of Argussian Reach
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>.

Long have we awaited this day. Argus was all but lost, its true denizens forced to remain hidden lest we perish. Your efforts on our behalf have allowed us to once again live free from fear. Please accept these trophies as a symbol of our gratitude.

passages.title: Paragon of the Army of the Light
passages.text: Your allies in the Army of the Light would like to thank you for your continued support. They await you on the Vindicaar.

passages.title: Paragon of the Army of the Light
passages.text:
Krona ki cristorr, champion!

Your presence among the Army of the Light has been a singular boon to our cause. Gratitude is not all that we may offer. Please accept these trophies as a tribute to your unwavering support.

Together we will bring about the Legion's end.

passages.title: Commander on Deck!
passages.text:
<The device hums to life, ready to provide you with access to Squadron Commander Vishax's portal in the Antoran Wastes.>
